candidates.name: Sara Rodriguez
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2021-2023); lieutenant governor of Wisconsin (2023-present)
candidates.gov_q1:
I'm a nurse. I worked night shifts in the ER, served as an epidemic intelligence officer for the CDC, and spent years as a working mom raising two kids while caring for my dad through Alzheimer's. I know what it's like to be stretched in every direction.
As lieutenant governor, I've traveled to all 72 Wisconsin counties four times, listening to what's actually keeping people up at night. I’ve spent my career solving problems. And I know how to win. I flipped a Republican-held Assembly seat in Waukesha County – a seat the GOP had held for years – then won statewide alongside Gov. Evers. Wisconsin has a real chance to deliver relief for Wisconsinites this November, and I know how to get it done.
candidates.gov_q2:
The cost of living. People are working harder than ever and still falling behind. We’re sick and tired of it. Donald Trump's tariffs raised costs on everything from groceries to gas. His budget handed tax breaks to billionaires and corporations while cutting health care and increasing premiums. And Congressman Tom Tiffany voted for every bit of it.
As governor, I will create a public health care option that brings down the cost of premiums, prescriptions, and hospital care. I will freeze utility rate increases so families get breathing room. I will tackle housing costs head-on. I will make childcare affordable so parents can afford to work. And I will fully fund our schools the way we're supposed to, so property taxes stop climbing every year.
candidates.gov_q3:
Lowering health care premiums. Health care costs are rising faster than wages, and families are stuck choosing between a prescription and groceries. That shouldn't be a choice anyone has to make, and families can’t wait four years for relief.
In my first 100 days, I will begin building a Wisconsin-run public health care option that uses the state's power to bring down what people pay for premiums, prescriptions, and care. If you like your current plan, nothing changes. If you don't, you'll have another choice, whether you're a farmer, a young person, a small business owner, or someone between jobs.
Lowering premiums and lowering the cost of health care overall means more money back in people's pockets for rent, groceries, and the things that matter.
candidates.gov_q4:
A governor's job is to work with Washington when it helps Wisconsin and stand up to Washington when it doesn't. After Trump’s ICE agents escalated earlier this year, I called for accountability – judicial warrants for arrests, and protections for schools, hospitals, and courthouses.
Donald Trump and Congressman Tom Tiffany are ignoring the real struggles of Wisconsinites. Their policies are raising the costs of everything from groceries to gas, causing health care premiums to double, and putting thousands at risk of losing their coverage altogether.
As governor, I won't wait for Washington to fix what it broke. I'll act quickly to lower health care premiums, make housing and childcare more affordable, fully fund our public schools, stop utility rate increases, and deliver much-needed relief for Wisconsinites.
candidates.gov_q5:
I've spent three years as lieutenant governor watching a Republican Legislature say no to fully funded schools, lower health care costs, affordable childcare, and property tax relief while Wisconsinites fall further behind. I'll keep showing up anyway. 
I'll be honest about where we disagree, but I'll look for the places where we can actually get things done, the way Gov. Evers has throughout his time in office. And I'll use the bully pulpit of the governor's office to make clear to Wisconsinites exactly who is blocking progress and why, because people deserve to know who's fighting for them and who isn't.
candidates.gov_q6:
For 15 years, every good idea Democrats have fought for has run into the same wall in Madison. We've had the plans. We've had the support from Wisconsinites. What we haven't had is the power to make them real.
When Wisconsin elects Democratic majorities, that wall comes down and I intend to move fast. Fully funding our schools, lowering health care premiums, stopping utility rate increases, and tackling housing costs would all become real, achievable priorities in a first budget, not just proposals that get stripped out. I'd work closely with legislative leaders to get this done, because Wisconsin families have waited long enough for these things to actually happen. Democratic majorities won’t be a blank check. They’ll be an opportunity to finally deliver results.
candidates.gov_q7: I’m the granddaughter of dairy farmers, so I’m obligated to defend Wisconsin’s cheese supremacy. Wisconsin is the only state in the country with a master cheesemaker program. This certification is so rigorous that the journey from becoming a licensed cheesemaker to earning the master title typically takes more than 13 years. I think that says something bigger about Wisconsin. We're a state that takes the time to do things right, whether that's cheese, our schools, or how we take care of each other. That's the standard I want to bring to the governor's office, too.

candidates.name: Andy Manske
candidates.gov_q1: The easiest answer is my direct accountability. My phone number is 414-640-3400, and my email is manskeandy23@gmail.com. Anyone across the state can contact me for their needs in the governor mansion if elected. I also literally am the only non-politician in the race. I am also the only non-bought out choice for governor from big anything, special interests, and millionaires, and billionaires. I hope with due time, policy vision, and unity focused tackling the cost of living from the up 40% we had we can make Wisconsin a utopia.
candidates.gov_q2: Crushing inflation! I would immediately go to activate the release valve by reforms, ending taxes, and making lever adjustments to see people start to prosper instead of living paycheck to paycheck, or as it's sometimes called just surviving. Gas markup, Gas tax, tax on female products, groceries from two ways. These are but a few of my relief policies.
candidates.gov_q3: Writing a budget like retail to consolidate our 70 state agencies will overlap into a more manageable amount like 3 into 1 new agency. I would then take half off that tripled budget, and return it to our state budget to prepare for tax cuts. The reason this would be a top goal is that a budget has only so much time after being elected to be done, and if it isn't we may have to wait for relief now for citizens.
candidates.gov_q4: One of cooperation, and not cooperation. As odd as that sounds, we want the government to focus assets on us like funds, but we also don't want the federal government destroying our culture or putting WI lives in danger. I would say no to data centers which are argued for by saying China is doing them. We need to compete. I would seek to protect our small town feeling, great lakes, energy costs then bow to Washington's demands from either side to strip our culture. Sometimes our federal government makes choices that hurt us to boost "America" as a whole. We must be independent enough to say no, but also take what we can get.
candidates.gov_q5: I would end gridlock, and get something done, if they controlled both. We would pass reform, and work to get relief to Wisconsin citizens win win.
candidates.gov_q6: I would end gridlock, and get something done, if they controlled both. We would pass reform, and work to get relief to WI citizens win win.
candidates.gov_q7: I refuse to say as Wisconsin has way too many fun history facts. We have such a beautiful unique state culture. I am so proud to live in Wisconsin, and working in the medical field in this state is so fulfilling. I hope me and my wife who are trying for children get to see Wisconsin even better someday for their sake.

candidates.name: Mandela Barnes
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2013-2017); lieutenant governor of Wisconsin (2019-2023)
candidates.gov_q1: Nobody in this race has the experience I have, and no one is more ready to do the job of governor and stand up to Trump’s chaos. We are going to reject the Washington Way of corruption and high costs and fix the rigged system holding back our families. I will get things done the Wisconsin Way as governor and that starts by taxing the rich, freezing the rates, passing universal childcare, and keeping Wisconsin safe.
candidates.gov_q2:
Wisconsinites are living in a rigged system. While the rich get richer and richer — while Elon Musk becomes the world’s first trillionaire — Wisconsin families are left to pick up the crumbs. The deck is stacked against working families because billionaires and greedy corporations keep buying politicians to maintain that status quo.
When I’m governor, we will end that broken system by taxing the rich. We will close the loopholes that allow billionaires and out-of-state corporations to get away without paying their fair share so we can cut taxes for middle class families, pass universal childcare, and a public option to lower healthcare costs.
candidates.gov_q3:
On day one as governor, I will call a special session to expand BadgerCare and pass a public option, and I won’t stop until we get this done. Wisconsin is one of just 10 states that has yet to expand Medicaid under President Obama’s Affordable Care Act. Even Republican states have done it, but not Wisconsin. 
That ends when I become governor. I will veto any state budget that does not include BadgerCare expansion. BadgerCare expansion is a critical first step to providing coverage to thousands of uninsured Wisconsinites, but we also need a public option for folks to buy-in to BadgerCare. This will give families an affordable alternative that pushes insurance companies to lower costs.
candidates.gov_q4: Right now, we have a president who is doing nothing but making life more expensive for Wisconsin. Donald Trump is the most corrupt president in American history. He’s a wannabe dictator who has used a rogue militia to assault and kill American citizens in our streets. As governor, my job will be to protect this state from the dangers Donald Trump poses to our state and do everything in my power to make life more affordable. At the same time — it’s not enough to just be anti-Trump. Democrats must have a real plan to take this state forward. My Wisconsin Way agenda will deliver real relief for working families who are being crushed by Donald Trump and Tom Tiffany’s massive price hikes.
candidates.gov_q5: We are working overtime in this campaign to not just win the governor’s race, but also a Democratic trifecta so we can deliver generational change for this state. No matter the makeup of the legislature, there will be a new governor, speaker, and Senate majority leader. Lowering utility costs, keeping this state safe, bringing down the cost of healthcare—my Wisconsin Way agenda is built on solutions every single legislator should be able to come together to solve no matter their party. I’ve worked across the aisle before and will continue to do so as governor.
candidates.gov_q6: With a Democratic trifecta, we will have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to take Wisconsin forward. We cannot let it go to waste. I will work with state legislators to pass every single piece of my Wisconsin Way agenda. This includes taxing the rich, cutting taxes for middle-class families, passing universal childcare, repealing Act 10, and fully funding our schools. Wisconsinites have been failed by Republicans in the state legislature for far too long, and that ends in January when we finally get things done the Wisconsin Way.
candidates.gov_q7: At the bottom of Lake Michigan near Manitowoc, there is a fully intact schooner shipwreck. That ship, Home, was part of the Underground Railroad and helped fugitive slaves reach freedom. It ran into another boat on a foggy morning and sank to the bottom of the lake. It's one of my favorite pieces of Wisconsin lore because it ties to who we've always been as a state. Wisconsin was the only state to declare the Fugitive Slave Act unconstitutional. While we’ve fallen off track at times, this state has always led the way in pushing the country forward when it matters most.

candidates.name: Joel Brennan
candidates.occupation: President of the Greater Milwaukee Committee (currently on leave)
candidates.gov_q1: I grew up one of 11 kids in Wisconsin, worked five jobs to pay for college, and raised my family here with my wife, Audra. For 25 years, I've solved problems in government, business, and nonprofits, running Discovery World, leading the Greater Milwaukee Committee, and serving as Gov. Evers' top cabinet official. We created a $4 billion budget surplus and grew the rainy-day fund to $1.7 billion. During the pandemic, we helped families, farmers, and small businesses across the state when they needed government to be there for them. I know what it means when the numbers don't add up for Wisconsin families, who need someone committed to helping them get ahead, not focused on getting even with our opponents.
candidates.gov_q2: Everything is too expensive. Healthcare, housing, child care, groceries, utility bills. Wisconsin families are squeezed from every direction. I'd address it the way I've solved problems my whole career: with real solutions. My Healthy Wisconsin Promise expands coverage and access and cracks down on drug costs. Build Roots, Build Wisconsin delivers 3% state-backed mortgages and builds 100,000 new entry-level homes. Child care is going over a cliff as funding disappears, and we need a long-term solution even as providers are on the verge of closing across the state. Wisconsin residents need utilities and big users to pay their own way instead of sticking families with the bill. Affordability is a crisis with many fronts, and I'm ready to take on all of them.
candidates.gov_q3: Building a budget that actually addresses the cost-of-living crisis and reflects what every Wisconsinite needs. We have to get this right because the budget sets the tone for everything else we do as a state. And I know how state budgets work because I've built them, as Secretary of Administration under Gov. Evers. I'd move to fix the school funding formula so it's built around what kids actually need, not their zip code. I'd make child care investment a top priority before more providers close their doors and more parents are forced out of the workforce. And I'd make sure housing and health care affordability are baked into the budget from day one, not negotiated away in the final days of session.
candidates.gov_q4: I would describe a healthy relationship as respectful, but not deferential, and based on mutual accountability. Wisconsin is a sovereign state, and the governor's job is to protect Wisconsinites' interests, not roll over when Washington oversteps. I'd work with the federal government where our interests align, on infrastructure funding, disaster response, and economic development. But where the federal government threatens Wisconsin's elections, civil rights, or the basic ability of working families to get by, I'll push back hard, using the courts, executive authority, partnership with the legislature and the power of the office. Wisconsin runs Wisconsin, and too many of our rights have been compromised by the federal government by the Trump Administration.
candidates.gov_q5: I've done this before. As Secretary of Administration, I worked with Republicans on the state budget, especially capital projects, and I collaborated with local government leaders of all ideological stripes during COVID. During the first year of the Evers Administration, I managed the Foxconn project and started down the path that eventually reduced the state’s exposure from $2.85 billion down to $80 million. My approach is simple: show up, do the homework, and find where real agreement exists, whether that's fiscal responsibility, government efficiency, or protecting taxpayers. Where agreement isn't possible, and the legislature acts against Wisconsin families, I'll use the partial veto and executive authority to protect people. Divided government doesn't have to mean gridlock. It can be where things get done.
candidates.gov_q6: For the first time in 16 years, Wisconsin has a real chance at a Democratic trifecta, and that means we can stop playing defense and start delivering together: lowering costs, expanding healthcare access, fixing the school funding formula, and building housing that families can actually afford. I'd work closely with legislative leadership from day one, building the same kind of real relationships that got things done when I was secretary of administration. Shared goals don't mean automatic agreement on every detail, and I'd rather work through those differences honestly than paper over them. The job is the same no matter who holds the gavel: deliver real results, and don't waste the chance when you have it.
candidates.gov_q7: During the Depression in the 1930s, the federal government created three “Greenbelt” communities in the United States, including one in Wisconsin. The planned communities included affordable homes for rent and purchase, a town center, gardens and walkable neighborhoods. The Wisconsin project  the city of Greendale in Milwaukee County — still includes the 366 original homes, which were built between 1936 and 1938 by people whose lives had been upended during the Depression. My grandfather, who had lost his job at the outset of the depression, was one of hundreds of Wisconsinites who worked on the project as part of FDR’s Works Projects Administration (WPA).

candidates.name: Missy Hughes
candidates.gov_q1: Right now Wisconsin needs leaders focused on results, not rhetoric. I have spent my entire career fighting for Wisconsinites and delivering real results, from helping save 1,600 family farms during my 17 years at Organic Valley, to creating over 45,000 jobs and helping 9,500 Wisconsinites start a small business when I served as Gov. Evers' head of Economic Development. I’m running for governor to deliver better jobs with higher paychecks, fix our broken healthcare system, and invest in our schools so that every family can get ahead. To move Wisconsin forward we need a governor with the experience and vision to improve the lives of Wisconsin families.
candidates.gov_q2: Everywhere I go I hear from Wisconsinites about the exploding cost of living. Everything from healthcare to gas is getting more expensive, and for too many families their paychecks aren't keeping up. As governor I will be laser focused on growing wages, and lowering the costs of the fundamentals: housing, healthcare, and childcare by bringing in targeted state investments. No matter what happens in Washington, and the chaos and the corruption of the Trump administration, as governor I’ll fight everyday to make sure Wisconsin families have the money in their pocket to build a better life.
candidates.gov_q3: My top priority for my first 100 days will be to lay the foundation of my Unlock Wisconsin agenda, including expanding badgercare and creating a public option so that every Wisconsinite can buy into the system. Invest in our public schools by finally fixing the broken school funding formula. Expanding the Wisconsin shares program to cap the cost of childcare at 7% of a family's income. Laying the pathway to building 200,000 homes in my first term in office. And restarting, and expanding, my Main Street Bounce Back program to create 50,000 new small businesses in my first term.
candidates.gov_q4: As governor I’ll fight anyone who tries to make life harder for Wisconsinites, including the federal government and the Trump administration. But I’ll never let politics get in the way of delivering for Wisconsinites. I’ll work with the federal government where I can, I will fight them where I need to. But above all else I will be focused on strengthening Wisconsin so that we are as self reliant as possible.
candidates.gov_q5: As governor I’ll be focused on delivering real results for Wisconsin families, and work with anyone who is willing to roll up their sleeves and get to work. If Republicans hold onto one or both of the chambers this November I’ll be clear about my vision for Wisconsin, where we focus on getting more people better jobs, build the housing we need to help young Wisconsinites stay in Wisconsin and start families of their own, and fix the broken healthcare system that is holding too many communities back. These are not red or blue issues, these are Wisconsin issues, and I will do everything in my power to deliver real results to them.
candidates.gov_q6: Fair maps have made a trifecta within our reach for the first time in a generation, and I am confident that this November Wisconsinites will elect Democratic majorities in the State Senate and State Assembly. Together we will be able to deliver real change for Wisconsin. For the past 8 years Gov. Evers has done an incredible job defending Wisconsinites rights from GOP attacks, and with a democratic trifecta we will be able to turn the page from this era of dysfunction in Madison and finally invest back into the people of Wisconsin.
candidates.gov_q7: Many folks don’t know that Wisconsin was the first state to ratify the 19th amendment enshrining women’s right to vote into the U.S. Constitution. Wisconsin has a rich history of advancing women’s rights and freedoms, but has yet to elect a woman to the governor’s seat. This November we have the opportunity to change that.

candidates.name: Francesca Hong
candidates.gov_q1:
I'm offering Wisconsin a bold, hopeful vision worth fighting for.
While others offer incremental fixes, I'm building a movement rooted in permanent affordability— universal childcare, fully funded public schools, paid leave, and lower healthcare costs. In a crowded field, I'm the candidate meeting this moment with clarity and conviction. That's why I've been consistently leading in the polls and steadily gaining momentum. I’m the only candidate who supports a moratorium on AI data center construction, and I was the first in the race to propose a plan to regulate Big Tech to ensure development benefits Wisconsin.
We're building a broad, multiracial, multi-generational coalition of working-class voters that spans the political spectrum, engaging people who normally sit out elections. Democrats need this coalition to win.
candidates.gov_q2:
Affordability. The cost of living keeps climbing while wages stay flat and corporations get richer on the backs of working people. This has happened by design, and we’re at a breaking point.
Permanent affordability is more than a slogan — it's a practice and a promise of enacting structural change that outlasts any one budget cycle or administration. For too long, politicians have failed to deliver for working people. It’s time to do better.
We do this by taxing the ultra-wealthy and the corporations, and then investing that revenue in what working families need: higher wages, universal childcare; fully funded public schools; paid leave; fairer, cheaper healthcare. It’s time to rebuild power for working-class people and give them a seat at the table.
candidates.gov_q3:
Universal childcare is the single highest-impact policy we can implement if we want to solve the affordability crisis in Wisconsin. It doesn't just benefit parents and kids — it benefits the entire economy. Because when parents can stay in the workforce, they can advance in their career. And when businesses can hire and retain employees, they can grow. And when kids are guaranteed to get the care they need, they have a better shot at life.
My plan guarantees free childcare for virtually every Wisconsin family, building on the state’s existing Child Care Counts program and modeled after what's working in Vermont and New Mexico. We pay for it the way we pay for Social Security: a small payroll contribution, split between worker and employer.
candidates.gov_q4:
Wisconsin's governor should always put Wisconsin first. I'll work with Washington wherever it helps families afford their lives: protecting our farmers, fixing our roads, keeping federal dollars flowing for healthcare and schools.
But when the federal government attacks our rights, targets our neighbors, cuts services working families depend on, or tries to turn Wisconsin into a testing ground for unconstitutional policies, the governor has to be willing to resist. That means using every tool available: litigation, executive authority, legislation, and public pressure. I’m not interested in political theater. I’m interested in whether the people of this state are being protected. A governor should know how to pick up the phone, build relationships, and deliver results. But they also need a backbone. Wisconsin deserves both.
candidates.gov_q5: I've spent five years as a Democrat in a Republican-controlled Legislature, and I’ve worked with Republicans to pass legislation, so I know exactly what this takes. We find the overlap and we go to work. I’ll work with anyone serious about delivering real relief for working-class Wisconsinites. Plenty of Republican voters want lower property taxes, affordable childcare, and good jobs that stay in Wisconsin. I'd take those fights straight to them and dare their representatives to vote against the interests of their own constituents. Where they obstruct, I'd make the stakes plain to the public. The AI data center issue is a perfect example. People on the left and right agree that Wisconsin families shouldn’t subsidize Big Tech’s energy bills.
candidates.gov_q6:
I’d treat a Democratic majority as a mandate to go big and deliver the bold reforms working families desperately need. A trifecta would be the biggest governing opportunity Wisconsin Democrats have had in a generation, and we cannot waste it. That means setting a clear agenda early, working closely with legislative leaders, and being disciplined about what we can pass, fund, implement, and
defend. My approach would be urgent, focused, and public-facing: keep the coalition aligned, move quickly on the issues people elected us to solve, and make sure the changes we pass are tangible, visible, and built to last.
When we get power, we have to use it — not to tinker around the edges, but to prove that government can work for working people.
candidates.gov_q7:
I was the first Asian American elected to the Wisconsin State Legislature, and if elected, I would be the first woman governor in Wisconsin history. So I got curious about other Wisconsin firsts and found out that we have some incredible ones:
The first kindergarten in America opened in Watertown. Wisconsin was the first state to enact unemployment compensation, which helped shape the federal unemployment insurance system. We passed the nation’s first constitutionally upheld workers’ compensation law. And Wisconsin also helped pioneer direct primary elections, a move that strengthened democracy by giving regular voters more power over party bosses.

candidates.name: Tom Tiffany
candidates.elected_experience: U.S. House (2021-present); Wisconsin State Senate (2013-2020); Wisconsin State Assembly (2011-2013); Town of Little Rice board (2009-2013)
candidates.gov_q1: I’m a lifelong Wisconsinite who grew up on a dairy farm, worked my way through UW-River Falls, and spent two decades running a small business with my wife, Chris, in Wisconsin’s Northwoods. I’m running for governor because I know Wisconsin’s best days are still ahead of us, but we need leadership that will unlock our state’s full potential. Right now, too many families feel like they are falling behind. Property taxes are too high, utility bills keep rising, and government has become too disconnected from the people it serves. As governor, I will focus on lowering costs, improving educational outcomes, creating economic opportunity, and restoring common sense to state government so every Wisconsin family can achieve the Wisconsin Dream.
candidates.gov_q2: Families across Wisconsin are feeling squeezed by rising costs. Under Gov. Evers, property taxes have risen at some of the fastest rates in decades, while the Public Service Commission has approved more than $2.2 billion in utility rate increases. As governor, I will start by ending the 400-year property tax increase to lower taxes, and I will bring greater accountability to the Public Service Commission to ensure ratepayers come first. We also need to make it possible for Wisconsin families to buy a home and build a future here. That's why I will work to lower the cost of housing and child care by cutting red tape, preventing Wall Street investors from buying up single-family homes, and making it easier to build homes and start small businesses.
candidates.gov_q3: My first action as governor will be calling a special session to end the 400-year property tax hike. Regardless of your politics, I think we can all agree that no governor should be able to raise property taxes for the next 400 years with the stroke of a pen. Wisconsin already has some of the highest property taxes in the nation. As we work to deliver lasting property tax relief, I will implement a statewide property tax freeze to ensure homeowners have certainty that their taxes will not continue to increase. Seniors on fixed incomes, working families, and young people looking to put down roots deserve the peace of mind of knowing they won't be taxed out of their homes.
candidates.gov_q4: Wisconsin’s relationship with the federal government should be based on partnership and accountability. The federal government sends significant taxpayer dollars to our state, and the governor has a responsibility to ensure those funds are spent wisely, protected from fraud, waste, and abuse, and directed toward helping our most vulnerable citizens. By working with our federal partners, we can improve infrastructure, strengthen public safety, and create economic opportunity. I will always stand up for Wisconsin and ensure our state receives the resources needed to help our communities succeed.
candidates.gov_q5: As governor, I will get to work on day one delivering results for Wisconsin. Too many Wisconsin families are struggling with rising costs and feeling like state government is making life harder instead of easier. My agenda is focused on making life more affordable by lowering property taxes, eliminating fraud and waste in government, improving educational outcomes, increasing health care price transparency, and protecting utility ratepayers and our farmland. The people of Wisconsin want common-sense solutions, and I will work with anyone committed to delivering results.
candidates.gov_q6: Having served in Congress and the Wisconsin Legislature, I understand that results require working with people who may not always agree. In Congress, I have introduced bipartisan legislation, including a bill with a Democrat member from New York to revoke China’s preferential trade status. As governor, I will work with anyone who is serious about delivering results for Wisconsin. That includes lowering property taxes, eliminating fraud and waste in government, improving educational outcomes, increasing health care price transparency, and protecting our utility rates and farmland from data center development. Wisconsinites expect leaders to solve problems, and that is how I will govern.
candidates.gov_q7: One of my favorite Wisconsin history facts is that the first Flag Day celebration took place in Waubeka in 1885. What began with a simple lesson at the Stony Hill School grew into a national tradition that reminds us of the ideals that unite Americans. As our country approaches its 250th birthday, it is a chance to reflect on the challenges our nation has overcome and to celebrate the contributions of Wisconsinites who helped build America, from our farmers and loggers to our manufacturers, veterans, and small businesses.”

candidates.name: David Crowley
candidates.elected_experience: Milwaukee County executive (April 2020-present); Wisconsin State Assembly (2017-June 2020)
candidates.gov_q1:
Wisconsin needs a governor who understands the challenges families face and has a record of delivering results. As Milwaukee County Executive, I have worked to expand mental health services, invest in affordable housing, strengthen public safety, grow our economy, and make government work better for the people it serves.
I’m running on the Badger Basics: great public schools, affordable health care, safe communities, economic opportunity, and infrastructure that supports growth. My focus is on lowering costs, raising wages, supporting working families, and ensuring every Wisconsinite, regardless of where they live, has a fair shot at success. Wisconsin’s future depends on investing in people, and I have the experience and vision to get it done.
candidates.gov_q2:
The top issue facing Wisconsinites is affordability. Too many families are working hard but still struggling to keep up with the cost of housing, health care, child care, groceries, and everyday necessities. When people cannot afford the basics, it affects every part of their lives and limits our state's economic potential.
My approach starts with the Badger Basics: fully funding public education, expanding access to affordable health care, increasing the minimum wage to $20 an hour, building more affordable housing, lowering energy costs, and investing in workforce development and infrastructure. Wisconsin succeeds when working families succeed. My goal is to make sure every Wisconsinite has a fair shot at economic security and the opportunity to build a better future for themselves and their families.
candidates.gov_q3:
My top priority in the first 100 days would be launching a statewide affordability agenda focused on reducing the everyday costs that are squeezing Wisconsin families. Too many people feel like they are falling behind despite working hard, and government should be focused on making life easier, not more expensive.
This means taking action to reduce housing costs, lower utility bills through energy-efficiency investments, expand access to affordable child care, and ensure families can access quality health care without financial hardship. I would also work to make strategic investments that put more money back into people's pockets. Wisconsin's success should be measured by whether working families can build financial security and plan confidently for the future.
candidates.gov_q4: The governor's job is to be Wisconsin's strongest advocate, working with the federal government when it benefits our state and standing up to it when it does not. Whether the administration in Washington is Democratic or Republican, my focus will be on securing resources, creating economic opportunities, and delivering results for Wisconsin families. As Milwaukee County Executive, I have successfully worked through both Democratic and Republican administrations, including during the Trump presidency, to bring federal investments, economic development opportunities, and critical resources back to Wisconsin. I will work aggressively to secure federal funding for infrastructure, health care, workforce development, and education. When federal policies threaten Wisconsin's economy, values, or constitutional rights, I will not hesitate to push back. My loyalty is not to any administration in Washington, it is to the people of Wisconsin.
candidates.gov_q5:
I have spent my career working with people who do not always agree with me, and I understand that governing requires partnership, not constant conflict. As Milwaukee County executive, I successfully worked with a Republican Legislature to pass Act 12, securing a long-term fiscal solution that protected essential county services and demonstrated that meaningful progress is possible when leaders come to the table focused on results.
If Republicans control one or both chambers, I will look for common ground on issues where Wisconsinites expect action - lowering costs, strengthening our workforce, improving infrastructure, supporting public safety, and expanding economic opportunity. That does not mean compromising on core values. I will always fight for public education, voting rights, reproductive freedom, and policies that help working families. My approach will be simple: work together where we can, stand firm where we must, and never lose sight of who we are elected to serve.
candidates.gov_q6: If Democrats control one or both chambers, I would see it as an opportunity to move quickly on the issues that Wisconsin families have been waiting too long to address. That includes strengthening public education, expanding access to affordable health care, increasing housing supply, supporting working families, protecting reproductive freedom, and making strategic investments in our workforce and infrastructure. But unified government is not a blank check. I believe in setting clear priorities, demanding accountability, and focusing on policies that produce measurable results. My goal would be to build broad coalitions, move meaningful legislation, and ensure that every decision we make improves the lives of Wisconsinites. The people of this state expect progress, and I would work every day to deliver it.
candidates.gov_q7:
One of my favorite Wisconsin history facts is that the first kindergarten in the United States was established in Watertown, Wisconsin, in 1856. German immigrants brought the idea from Europe, and it eventually spread across the country, transforming early childhood education in America. I love that story because it shows how Wisconsin has long been a place of innovation and opportunity, where new ideas can take root and make a lasting impact far beyond our state borders.
But the tastiest fun fact about Wisconsin is that Two Rivers is the true home to the ice cream sundae!

candidates.name: Kelda Roys
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Senate (2020-present); Wisconsin State Assembly (2009-2013)
candidates.gov_q1:
We need to raise wages, lower costs, fund public education, and protect our freedoms. As governor, I have detailed plans to raise the minimum wage and restore workers’ rights, open the state’s health insurance to let the public buy in, and make housing, utilities, and childcare more affordable. I’m an effective lawmaker, small business owner, attorney, and parent of five. Together, we’ll build a Wisconsin where everyone can thrive.
Working together, we have a rare chance to make real progress – I know how to use power to deliver. As the only candidate who has expanded healthcare, served in the senate, assembly, and Joint Finance Committee, and passed progressive legislation in the toughest legislative environments for over 20 years, I know how to get things done.
candidates.gov_q2: We must make Wisconsin a place where young people want — and can afford — to live and build families. Our state is aging, as our best and brightest leave. We need to make Wisconsin’s public schools the best in the nation again. After decades of Republican budget cuts, our public schools are hurting. I’ll properly fund public education with state dollars, reduce property taxes and end the divisive referendum cycle, and fix the school funding formula. I also have a plan to bring the private voucher scheme to a responsible end. I’m proud to have earned the trust and endorsement of WEAC, Wisconsin’s teachers, in this race, because they know I’m the only candidate with a plan and the commitment to put our kids first.
candidates.gov_q3:
To address the affordability crisis, I have detailed plans to raise the minimum wage, restore workers’ rights, and lower costs for childcare, housing, groceries, utilities, and prescription drugs at keldaroys.com.
But healthcare is the most urgent problem facing Wisconsinites. I have a bold, Trump-proof plan to expand affordable coverage by allowing any Wisconsinite or business to buy into the same health insurance state employees have. This will enable everyone — school districts,  manufacturing companies, independent contractors — to buy high quality, competitively priced, often nonprofit coverage, at no cost to taxpayers. Small businesses can start, compete, and grow. Plus, by covering more people and expanding the pool, we will reduce uncompensated care, lower premium costs for everyone including taxpayers, and keep rural clinics and hospitals open.
candidates.gov_q4:
I have a two-decades long bipartisan track record of passing legislation, and I’ll work to get federal dollars for our state. But Trump’s regime is attacking our pocketbooks, communities, and constitutional rights. We need a governor who will fight this authoritarian regime and work to hold them legally accountable for any crimes they commit. 
I’ve crafted the strongest plan to combat ICE’s violent abuses, to strengthen civil rights protections so Wisconsinites can sue when our rights are violated, and to prosecute any crimes they commit in Wisconsin. Legal accountability is essential to democracy. As governor, I’ll protect us from the harms of Trump and Tiffany: from their illegal tariffs and wars to corruption and healthcare cuts that are decimating our farmers, small businesses, and families.
candidates.gov_q5:
I’m proud of my Democratic values, but I’ve never hesitated to work accross the aisle to help Wisconsinites. For over two decades, I’ve turned commonsense progressive ideas into law in our Republican-dominated legislature, and I’m the only candidate with a track record of doing so – on issues from criminal justice reform to reproductive rights to consumer protection to expanding healthcare access. 
Wisconsin’s most transformational governors have been long-term legislators — unfortunately, they’ve been Republicans: Thompson and Walker. To make real, durable change, I will continue to work closely with all members of the legislature on our shared goals, and to use the full power of the governorship to deliver the transformative change we need. This is a time for our most experienced, effective leader to govern.
candidates.gov_q6: Wisconsin Democrats will move from our “goalie” era to our governing era, if we have a governor with moral clarity, political courage, and the willingness to use power to actually deliver. I’ve spent my life building broad, diverse coalitions, electing Democrats statewide, and turning progressive ideas into law. That’s why Lt. Governor Barbara Lawton says I’m “the only candidate who ticks every box – able to beat Tom Tiffany, govern on day one, and lead fearlessly.” It’s why I’ve earned the most endorsements by far from elected officials in every corner of the state, and from the state’s largest union. They know I can win, and they trust me to bring Wisconsin together and deliver on our Democratic priorities that have been sidelined for a generation.
candidates.gov_q7: Wisconsin had the nation’s first kindergarten! As the mom and stepmom of 5, I’m passionate about early childhood education. Back in 1856, Margarethe Meyer Schurz, a progressive German immigrant and mother, opened America’s first kindergarten in Watertown. When I was elected to the Assembly in 2009, the Wisconsin Historical Society invited legislators to select an art piece from their archives for display in our capitol office. I chose a small oil painting of that first kindergarten, a humble one-room schoolhouse — very like the one I grew up in rural Taylor County, Wisconsin. Our state has a proud progressive history, leading in workers’ rights, women’s enfranchisement, conservation, and LGBTQ non-discrimination, but my favorite first is this one, because public education is the foundation of our democracy.

candidates.name: David Varnam
candidates.ltgov_q1: We can all think of politicians that said what they would do if elected, then after being elected seemed to do the opposite. When I ran for Mayor of Lancaster in 2016, I ran as a fiscal conservative. When I left office in 2022 after serving three terms, Lancaster had the lowest property taxes and lowest utility fees of any city in Grant County. I was the first Mayor of Lancaster in over 20 years to use the veto, and I used it multiple times including to veto a 40% stormwater fee increase. I broke a tie to defeat a “wheel tax.” I did what I told voters I would do. I am endorsed by Wisconsin Family Action PAC and Pro-Life Wisconsin PAC.
candidates.ltgov_q2: I am running for lieutenant governor, hoping to work with Congressman Tom Tiffany to make Wisconsin a leader in the Midwest again. I have traveled to all corners of our state since announcing my candidacy in late September, driving more than 45,000 miles and visiting more than 60 of Wisconsin’s 72 counties. Together we can be bold on lowering taxes, cutting red tape, shrinking the size of government, protect the sanctity of life, and keep men out of women's sports and their bathrooms. We need to improve our education system and the opportunities it provides our children. I will work to give parents a choice and a voice in education, and work to raise test scores, standards and expectations for our students.
candidates.ltgov_q3: My unique background as a former rural mayor, former federal policy analyst for Dr. James Dobson at Focus on the Family, and as a former housing, water, and transportation district aide to a member of Congress sets me apart. I will be able to use my wide breadth of knowledge to advise a governor Tom Tiffany and to advocate for his accomplishments with the media, groups, and individuals throughout the state.
candidates.ltgov_q4: The first governor of Wisconsin, Nelson Dewey, was from Lancaster.

candidates.name: Will Martin
candidates.occupation: Consultant working on public-private partnerships to expand access to skilled workforce training (e.g., construction trades, information technology, etc.), homeownership, and economic development, including advising the British, Dutch, and Israeli governments.
candidates.ltgov_q1: I am the only lieutenant governor candidate in either party who has served in senior roles in two gubernatorial administrations. Having worked in the governor’s office, led major reforms, and served as a liaison across several departments, I understand how state government works as well as where it does not. In the last 7 years, our state budget has grown by 46% with over 70 departments, agencies, commissions, and boards as well as more than 2.5 million square feet of office space — much of which is all-too-often unused. My experience and knowledge would allow me to assist a new governor by recommending opportunities to consolidate agencies, eliminate redundancy and waste, reduce red tape, cut costs and taxes, and expand support for homeownership and economic/job growth.
candidates.ltgov_q2: The measure of success for me is not visibility as Wisconsin’s lieutenant governor; it is effectiveness. first and foremost, that success is defined by being able to work closely with the governor, being able to provide strategic advice and recommendations that will make state government work more effectively and cost-efficiently for the people of Wisconsin. Growth in state government’s budget has outstripped inflation and increases in household income. The Badger State is now one of the most regulated states in the nation. My priority is helping the next Governor make Wisconsin the state for those who want to own a home, start a family or business, develop high-demand skills, and expand job opportunities, and enjoy retirement with dignity.
candidates.ltgov_q3: My firsthand experience in senior roles in state government in the governor’s office and across departments as well as in the private sector as a small business owner will allow me to help the next governor reduce redundancy, eliminate ineffective programs, streamline systems, cut costs and taxes, and make Wisconsin more business-friendly and affordable again.
candidates.ltgov_q4: Wisconsin has led the nation at so many important crossroads. As someone who was born on Juneteenth, I am proud that it was Wisconsin where the Republican Party was founded, leading to the freeing of 4 million souls. When women cried out for the vote, Wisconsin was the first to ratify the 19th Amendment. When injured employees needed support, Wisconsin became the first in the nation to establish both workers compensation and unemployment insurance. Wisconsin has a proven record of moving the nation forward.

candidates.name: Sarah Godlewski
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin secretary of state (2023-present); Wisconsin state treasurer (2019-2023)
candidates.ltgov_q1: I'm the daughter of two public school teachers, raised in a union family, and I worked my way through college believing in the Wisconsin promise: if you work hard and play by the rules, you can build a good life. I've spent my career fighting to keep that promise alive. As state treasurer, I delivered record-breaking investments in public schools, created a foreclosure prevention fund, and overturned a gag order on climate change. I flipped Trump counties and outperformed statewide Democrats because I showed up everywhere, listened, and fought for working families.Today, too many Wisconsinites are working harder than ever while Republicans put billionaires and special interests first. I'm running because Wisconsin families deserve a fighter, and that's exactly what I'll be.
candidates.ltgov_q2: The lieutenant governor's office is only as effective as the person holding it. I've spent my career proving that underestimated offices can deliver meaningful results. As state treasurer, I created Wisconsin's first Treasurer Taxpayer Transparency Report and launched a program to help families achieve homeownership. I've worked in local government, state government, and one of the largest bureaucracies in the world — the federal government. At every level, I've learned that success comes from showing up, building relationships, and finding ways to get things done. As lieutenant governor, I'll bring that same approach to every corner of Wisconsin, serving as a direct link between the governor and the people we serve while fighting every day for working families.
candidates.ltgov_q3: I bring a unique combination of economic, executive, and coalition-building experience to the lieutenant governor's office. Before serving as state treasurer and secretary of state, I worked in microfinance, helping entrepreneurs and small business owners access capital and create opportunity. As state treasurer and secretary of state, I've managed statewide offices, navigated complex challenges, and delivered results for Wisconsin families. I chaired a $1.6 billion public trust fund and invested in Wisconsin communities to support local projects, create jobs, and strengthen our economy. As lieutenant governor, I'll bring that same approach —showing up, listening, and finding common ground to expand opportunity, strengthen communities, and ensure government works for all Wisconsinites.
candidates.ltgov_q4: I'm proud to call Eau Claire home. Here's something even many locals don't know: there were once three Eau Claires! Before March 1872 there were three separate villages: West Eau Claire, East Eau Claire, and North Eau Claire. They decided to join together to reduce competition, combine resources, and build a stronger future. I've always loved that story because it reflects a value that still defines Wisconsin today: we're stronger when we work together. Whether it's neighbors helping neighbors or communities coming together to solve problems, that spirit of cooperation has helped Wisconsin thrive for generations, and it's one of the things that makes me proud to call Wisconsin home.

candidates.name: Joshua Kaul
candidates.attygen_q1: I have a strong record of protecting public safety, defending our freedoms, and delivering real results. We need to continue to have an attorney general we can count on to take on tough fights and stand up for all Wisconsinites. Under my leadership, the Wisconsin Department of Justice (DOJ) has investigated and/or prosecuted serious criminal activity, including homicides, sexual assaults, internet crimes against children, and drug trafficking. My administration has also worked to make our schools safer, gotten accountability from those alleged to have violated laws that protect consumers and our natural resources, and joined more than 50 multistate cases against the current Trump administration. We should build on the progress we’ve been making, not go backwards.
candidates.attygen_q2: We should be able to rely on our attorney general to stand up for the best interests of Wisconsinites. But Eric Toney won’t stand up to corporate special interests or the Trump administration like I have. He also won’t stand up for our freedoms like I have. In 2022, Toney attacked me for seeking to block a law dating back to the mid-1800s from being enforced as a sweeping criminal abortion ban, left open the possibility of bringing prosecutions for abortions in cases involving rape or incest and raised the possibility of “allowing for adjoining counties to be able to investigate and enforce that abortion ban in Wisconsin.” In addition, Toney supported Michael Gableman’s wasteful and absurd so-called investigation into the 2020 elections in Wisconsin.
candidates.attygen_q3:
My administration has helped to fight the opioid epidemic, including by seeking accountability from opioid manufacturers, distributors, and others that allegedly contributed to the opioid epidemic and helping to secure the recovery of hundreds of millions of dollars.I successfully fought to get legislation passed that will help prevent a future backlog of untested sexual assault kits in Wisconsin, and my administration launched a statewide sexual assault kit tracking system.
My administration obtained a ruling last year from the Wisconsin Supreme Court that makes clear that abortions are not broadly banned in Wisconsin by a law dating back to the mid-1800s.
My administration has effectively stood up for democracy, including by successfully defending the outcome of the 2020 presidential election in Wisconsin in court.
candidates.attygen_q4:
My top priority as attorney general has been and will continue to be public safety. Wisconsin DOJ should continue working to reduce violent crime, fight the opioid epidemic, and make our schools safer. In another term as AG, I will continue advocating for additional resources that can help make communities safer and for common-sense gun-safety measures, such as expanding background checks for firearms transfers.
Wisconsin DOJ should also continue being a watchdog for Wisconsinites against special interests and others who harm consumers, taxpayers, or our natural resources.
Additionally, Wisconsin DOJ should continue standing up for Wisconsinites’ freedoms and against federal government actions that violate the law and harm Wisconsinites.
candidates.attygen_5: Wisconsin was the first state to ratify the 19th Amendment.

candidates.name: Eric Toney
candidates.attygen_q1: When I survived open heart surgery at 39 years old, I reflected on my life and didn't have any regrets. I love helping keep people safe, and I've done that for nearly 14 years as the district attorney in Fond du Lac County, where I was born and raised. I was named Wisconsin's 2024 District Attorney of the Year. As past president of the Wisconsin District Attorneys Association, I worked with the Republican Legislature and a Democratic Governor to secure crime lab positions, internet crimes against children DOJ positions, over 50 new prosecutors where they were needed most, and increased resources for prosecutors and public defenders. I'd be honored to take my bipartisan record to our DOJ and put public safety over politics.
candidates.attygen_q2: Josh Kaul's record is filled with broken promises, but he's asking for a third term. He promised to improve forensic testing. Instead, the crime labs are slower than under his predecessor, and the nonpartisan Legislative Audit Bureau documented that he failed to fill lab positions, including DNA analysts. He's testing fewer items — with DNA turnaround times taking twice as long — despite more staff and resources. He promised rape kit convictions, and after $9.5 million spent and over 4,000 kits tested, he's gotten fewer than 15 convictions in nearly eight years. He promised to confront the drug crisis, but he eliminated drug investigators in northern Wisconsin, which the tribes say is unnecessarily costing lives. Wisconsin cannot afford four more years of broken promises.
candidates.attygen_q3: I've always put public safety over politics. That's why I've fought to get additional crime lab and crimes against children positions added to the DOJ. I'm proud of the bipartisan team I've built in my office — including former Democrat and Republican district attorneys. I've held Wisconsin's most dangerous criminals accountable, in cases ranging from homicide to human trafficking. I helped establish Fond du Lac County's first Drug Court and chaired an Opioid Coalition to fight addiction at its source. As president of the Wisconsin District Attorneys Association, I worked across both parties to secure increased resources for prosecutors and public defenders, additional crime lab positions, and over 50 new prosecutor positions where need was greatest. My colleagues named me 2024 District Attorney of the Year.
candidates.attygen_q4: First, the Department of Justice needs leadership that will put public safety over politics. That means an immediate priority is to fix the crime labs. I'll support the great lab analysts, end misguided policies that limit law enforcement's ability to have items tested, end work from home for analysts that takes them away from the lab, and ensure we're filling the vacant positions we learned about in the nonpartisan audit. Second, confront the drug crisis by empowering public safety leaders to aggressively prosecute drug crimes and restoring the narcotics agents northern Wisconsin lost under Kaul. Third, target violent crime in Milwaukee — a safer Milwaukee means a safer Wisconsin. Fourth, back victims, survivors, and law enforcement in all 72 counties by putting public safety over politics.
candidates.attygen_5: Ripon, Wisconsin is the birthplace of the Republican Party — which was founded in opposition to the expansion of slavery. It’s an honor to serve as District Attorney for a county with that kind of legacy, and one could argue Ripon became a catalyst that helped end slavery in America — truly embracing Wisconsin’s motto “forward.” Ripon is not only a significant part of Wisconsin's history, it's a significant part of America’s history in our quest for a more perfect union.

candidates.name: JoCasta Zamarripa
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2011-2021); City of Milwaukee Common Council (2020-present)
candidates.secstate_q1: Wisconsin deserves a secretary of state who shows up. I have spent my career delivering for working families on Milwaukee's south side, first in the state Assembly and now as alderperson. I know how to use a platform to fight for people who have been ignored and underestimated. The secretary of state chairs the Board of Commissioners of Public Lands, managing Wisconsin's $1.4 billion public lands trust and funding every public school library in the state. That is real responsibility and I take it seriously. I will bring the same tenacity and community focus to this office that I have brought to every role I have held.
candidates.secstate_q2: After a decade in the state Assembly and two terms as Milwaukee alderperson, I understand how state government works and how to make it work for people. I have passed legislation, navigated complex bureaucracies, managed budgets, and built coalitions across lines that do not always agree. The secretary of state oversees Wisconsin's public lands trust, manages state business filings, and chairs the board that funds public school libraries statewide. These are technical responsibilities that require someone who understands policy, accountability, and what is at stake for working families. I have spent my entire career building exactly that foundation.
candidates.secstate_q3: The secretary of state is a constitutional office with real responsibilities and real potential. I believe in working with the Legislature and the governor to make sure this office is as useful as possible for the people of Wisconsin. If there are ways to expand the office's capacity to serve Wisconsinites better, I want to have that conversation. What matters is that this office delivers results for working families, protects our public lands trust, and earns the trust of the people who elect its occupant.
candidates.secstate_q4: Wisconsin accounts for more than half of all Korbel brandy sold worldwide every single year. After World War II, Wisconsin distributors bought up a massive cache of California brandy and the state never looked back. The brandy old fashioned became our signature cocktail and Korbel has been thanking us ever since.

candidates.name: Jay Schroeder
candidates.occupation: Real estate and stock market investor
candidates.elected_experience: Menomonie City Council (two terms); town of Menasha board (one term)
candidates.secstate_q1: I am the only candidate that is explaining why your taxes are going up from the wasteful corrupt spending from this office. The current budget went up 157% and from two to six employees with little or nothing to do and an office so small all six employees could not even fit in it. You will not hear vague or sound bits from me, only the truth regarding this office. Election honesty and integrity are job one with me, the taxpayers deserving nothing less.
candidates.secstate_q2: Having studied the issue of election honesty integrity I have uncovered the fact that five governmental entities govern elections like Wisconsin does. The troubling group to be in is Illinois, New York, Maryland, Washington, D.C., and Wisconsin. Wisconsin is run by what I call the "Wisconsin Elections Conmission" an organization that the voters have no control over. 33 states have the secretary of state in charge of elections. Wisconsin will as well if I am elected secretary of state. There are more deceased names on the voter rolls in Wisconsin than alive. We need paper ballots, same day voting, proof of citizenship just as the Safe Act requires. Making Elections Great Again. I will move the office out of Dane County as well.
candidates.secstate_q3: The secretary of state will be in charge of elections one way or another if I am elected. I can work with the Legislature for election honesty integrity if they so choose, or as a co equal branch of government. As secretary of state I will implement election honesty integrity cleaning up the voters rolls, same day voting, proof of ID, proof of citizenship. I will be willing to take this case all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court if need be to once and for all clean up the voting in Wisconsin. I will abolish WEC. My democrat opponent I will take head on and ask why she supports bloated spending as the voters trust me in the primary.
candidates.secstate_q4: As I have traveled the state speaking at many events and asking for the 2,350 voters that signed my nomination papers that made me a viable candidate I have noticed one thing in common. The majority of the people I meet are good caring Christian people that want to pass on to the children and grandchildren what they inherited. Wisconsin lands are full of beautiful lakes, forests in Northern Wisconsin, rolling hills in Hillsboro Wisconsin. Lake Michigan from Milwaukee to Door County. And of course the first 4 wheel drive ever made was in Clintonville Wisconsin my hometown.

candidates.name: Pete Karas
candidates.secstate_q1: My background spans practical experience, including elected public service, small business ownership, and grassroots organizing. As a Racine city alderman, I navigated the real-world of government bureaucracy, constituent needs, and public accountability. As a small business owner, I understand compliance, recordkeeping, and what it means when government processes fail working people.
candidates.secstate_q2: I've also spent this campaign fighting for ballot access rights — researching Wisconsin election law, engaging the Elections Commission, and defending democratic participation against partisan suppression. That firsthand experience with the mechanics of electoral access is exactly what a reform-minded secretary of state needs. I'll bring transparency, accessibility, and accountability to an office that too often operates in the background.
candidates.secstate_q3: Significantly more. Wisconsin's secretary of state is among the most hollowed-out such offices in the nation. That changes under my administration. The Capitol belongs to all three branches of government. Placing operational control under the governor creates an inherent conflict: one branch controlling the shared home of all three. The secretary of state, as an independent constitutional officer, is better positioned to manage the Capitol neutrally, covering facilities, public access, historic preservation, event permitting, and space allocation, without favoring any branch or party. I also support converting the office to a nonpartisan institution, removing the structural conflict between party loyalty and neutral administration.
candidates.secstate_q4: Milwaukee was actually one of the original cities in the American League when it formed in 1900. The Milwaukee Brewers lasted just one season before relocating to St. Louis and becoming the Browns (later the Baltimore Orioles). Making it even cooler, Connie Mack was their manager!

candidates.name: Brayden Myer
candidates.secstate_q1: I have the education and experience that directly relates to this office. My plan for the Secretary of State will benefit all Wisconsinites. This includes working to form an easily accessible website of all the records this office holds and overlooks. This will streamline business, hold the office more accountable, and increase transparency. Through this, taxpayers will save time and money. Timeliness is essential for a government to properly serve its citizens. I will bring accountability by using best practices to prioritize efficiency. As this position chairs the Board of Commissioners of Public Lands, which provides loans to local governments, rather than providing loans for politically divisive projects, I will push for these loans to address critical infrastructure needs such as fixing our roads.
candidates.secstate_q2: In high school, I dual-enrolled at UW-Green Bay. Taking all college courses my junior and senior year of high school, I graduated with 91 college credits. Six months later, I graduated with my Bachelor's Degree in Political Science, being designated Magna Cum Laude, along with minors in Public Administration and Democracy & Justice Studies as well as with a certificate in Organizational Development. I was the Vice President of the Lincoln High School Young Republicans. At UWGB, I was the Treasurer for the College Republicans. After college, I formed the Manitowoc County chapter of Moms for Liberty where I am the Vice Chair and Treasurer. I also formed and run the Manitowoc County Patriots. I have directly served the public as a congressional staffer.
candidates.secstate_q3: The secretary of state should be given more responsibilities. Half a century ago, the legislature removed the secretary of state's oversight on elections and handed control to unelected boards. I will fight to abolish the Wisconsin Elections Commission, clean the voter rolls and remove their cost, and put this office in charge of elections so voters have someone to directly hold accountable. In the last state budget, the secretary of state’s funding and number of staff increased. Simultaneously no responsibilities were added. Instead, responsibilities were removed. This demonstrates our government is bloated. I oppose increased spending and higher taxes, especially when work is being taken out of the office’s responsibilities.
candidates.secstate_q4: While it may not be a “fun” fact, it certainly is important. Four years ago, Harry Wait exposed that ballots can be mailed to any address through the MyVote Wisconsin website. When he exposed this, rather than fixing the vulnerability, the Wisconsin Elections Commission took him to court and engaged in a prolonged legal battle. During his sentencing this year, I was the only candidate who showed up for him. This shows there is still work that needs to be done. We not only need to fix what Harry exposed, but other critical issues too like mandating voter ID, going to hand-counted paper ballots only, removing Meagan Wolfe from her office, and more to ensure we have secure and verifiable elections.

candidates.name: Nate Pollnow
candidates.secstate_q1: For the last 40 years, the secretary of state has either been someone who just wanted a paycheck or someone who was angling for another political office. I actually want to do the job and to bring transparency and openness to state government. As a small business owner and second-generation beef farmer, I have never backed away from hard work. I have spent my live in service to others through my work in local government and in my commuity, and I will bring that same eithic and approach to the secretary of state's office, holding all politicians accountable, regardless of partisan affiliation.
candidates.secstate_q2: I would bring an outsider's perspective to the office that I think is needed in what should be a watchdog role for state government. As a farmer, you can't fake results. As secretary of state, I will bring the transparency and honesty to state government that cuts through the legalese and political posturing so voters can know exactly what their government is doing.
candidates.secstate_q3: Many voters I talk to wonder what exactly the secretary of state even does. Others will say "Not much." And they're partly right. According to the state constitution, the secretary of state is responsible for keeping “a fair record of the official acts of the legislature and executive branch” as well as keeping track of the official state seal. Some members of my own party have tried to sideline the secretary of state's office and limit its responsibilities, but I disagree with that approach. While the last thing we need is more bureaucracy in Madison, taxpayers deserve someone who actually wants to do the job. I believe the current responsibilities, when executed with energy and purpose, are appropriate for the office.
candidates.secstate_q4: We all know Wisconsin is an agricultural and manufacturing powerhouse, but did you know that we supply 25% of all the nation's cheese, we're the top cranberry producing state supplying 60% of all cranberries harvested in the U.S., we're one of the leading ginseng producers in the world, and we rank No. 1 in the country in paper mills and employees.

candidates.name: Cindy Werner
candidates.occupation: Strategic partnerships director for a nonprofit organization
candidates.secstate_q1: Wisconsin voters deserve a Secretary of State who is committed to transparency and public service. As an Army veteran, community leader, educator, and former and present school board member, I have spent my life helping people understand government and become active participants in their communities. I believe the office should serve as a trusted resource that connects citizens with their government while preserving Wisconsin’s history and civic traditions. My focus will be on civic education, public accessibility, and ensuring that every Wisconsinite can easily access information about their state government. I will bring practical leadership and a servant’s heart to the office while working to strengthen public confidence in our institutions.
candidates.secstate_q2: My experience spans military service, education, nonprofit leadership, business, and community engagement. I have worked with civic organizations, educators, elected officials, and community leaders to develop programs that promote constitutional literacy, civic participation, and leadership development. As a former and current school board member, I understand the importance of making government information accessible and understandable. As a veteran, I value service. As a nonprofit leader, I have experience building partnerships and managing initiatives that serve diverse communities. These experiences would help me modernize public outreach, expand civic education resources, preserve Wisconsin’s historical records, and ensure the secretary of state’s office remains responsive and accessible to all Wisconsinites.
candidates.secstate_q3: The responsibilities of the secretary of state should be determined by what best serves Wisconsin citizens. I believe the office can play a larger role in civic education, historical preservation, public engagement, and making government information more accessible to the public. Any expansion of responsibilities should be done thoughtfully and transparently through the legislative process. My priority is not expanding government for its own sake, but ensuring that the office provides meaningful value to taxpayers. Wisconsin has a rich history and a strong tradition of civic involvement. The secretary of state can help strengthen both by serving as a trusted resource that connects citizens to their government and encourages informed participation in our constitutional republic.
candidates.secstate_q4: One of my favorite Wisconsin history stories is that of Joshua Glover. Glover escaped slavery and settled in Wisconsin, but in 1854, he was captured under the federal Fugitive Slave Act and jailed in Milwaukee. Thousands of Wisconsinites rallied to his defense, broke him out of jail, and helped him reach freedom in Canada. The event became a defining moment in Wisconsin history and demonstrated the courage of ordinary citizens who stood up for liberty and justice. What inspires me most is that Joshua Glover never gave up fighting for his freedom and dignity. His story reminds us that perseverance, principle, and courage can change history and help move a society toward greater freedom for all.

candidates.name: Yee Leng Xiong
candidates.occupation: Executive director, New Beginnings for Refugees
candidates.elected_experience: D.C. Everest Area School Board (2014-present);  Marathon County Board of Supervisors (2016-present); Weston Board of Trustees (2018-2022)
candidates.treas_q1: I have managed public budgets at every level of government. That is exactly what this office needs. As D.C. Everest School Board treasurer, a Marathon County supervisor, and a village finance committee member, I have made the hard decisions about how every taxpayer dollar is spent. As former executive director of the Hmong American Center, I rescued a nonprofit from the brink of closure and grew its budget to $1.9 million. This office is not ceremonial. It is a responsibility. The treasurer helps oversee more than $1.3 billion in school trust funds, finances local infrastructure, and answers directly to the people, not the governor or the Legislature. Born in Wausau to refugees, I learned to stretch every dollar. I will do the same for Wisconsin families.
candidates.treas_q2: I bring hands-on financial management. I have overseen complex public budgets as a Marathon County supervisor, balanced a school district's finances as board treasurer, and turned around a nonprofit, growing its budget to $1.9 million. Gov. Evers appointed me to his Financial Literacy Council because of that experience. It translates directly for Wisconsinites. Because I have sat on a school board, I understand how trust fund investment decisions reach real classrooms, and I will protect the $1.3 billion Common School Fund's principal while growing returns. I also know that families around Wisconsin are struggling, so I will use the office to help more families recover the unclaimed property they are owed.
candidates.treas_q3: More. Wisconsin's treasurer is now one of the weakest in the nation. Over the past two decades, the Legislature stripped the office of responsibilities and shifted them to other agencies. In 2018, voters rejected an attempt to abolish the office entirely, sending a clear message that they want an independent watchdog over public money. I would work to restore real authority to the office. A stronger treasurer means another set of eyes on Wisconsin's finances, more transparency, and a true check that does not answer to the governor or the Legislature.
candidates.treas_q4: Most people are surprised to learn that Wisconsin is home to the third-largest Hmong community in the country, behind only California and Minnesota. And my hometown of Wausau has the highest concentration of Hmong residents of any city in the state, and one of the highest anywhere in America. I love this fact because of the story behind it. Hmong families came to Wisconsin in the 1970s with almost nothing, sponsored by local churches and neighbors, and built lives, businesses, and traditions that are now part of who we are. It is the reason a kid born to refugees in Wausau can grow up to run for statewide office. That is a very Wisconsin story, and I am proud it is mine too.

candidates.name: John S. Leiber
candidates.treas_q1: The job of the state treasurer is to ensure that the funds entrusted to the office are managed and invested well. As state treasurer, I am on the Board of Commissioners for Public Lands, which manages the $1.6 billion trust Common School Fund. The Common School Fund invests money and distributes the profits to public school districts across the state. This year was the largest distribution ever, at $73.5 million. The results speak for themselves, and I am proud to run on my record of fiscal management.'
candidates.treas_q2: As the current state treasurer, I have been doing the job for three and a half years already. Prior to my term as state treasurer, I worked as an attorney in the private sector and served as a legislative aide in the Wisconsin State Assembly. My legal background helps navigate our complex state laws, while my legislative experience supports my efforts in negotiations with other elected officials to implement policies that help all Wisconsinites.
candidates.treas_q3: Rather than growing the office, I believe the state treasurer should be focusing on the existing duties. The state treasurer already has a job to do, and focusing on gaining more power is counterproductive. That is why I have dedicated my time in office to doing the very best job I can with the existing powers and duties of the office. Overseeing and growing a $1.6 billion trust fund is a meaningful responsibility without adding new duties.
candidates.treas_q4: I really love our state Capitol, where my office is located. Our current state Capitol building is actually the third capitol built on that same site. The first one was too small and soon replaced with the second capitol. In 1904, that capitol burned down during a winter so cold the water for the fire hoses was frozen and couldn't be used. Our current Capitol, which was finished in 1917, was designed to be state of the art for the time, with electrical lighting, pneumatic tubes to deliver messages, and the first electronic voting board in the Assembly chambers. Our Capitol is almost entirely open to the public, which sets it apart from other state capitols.
