candidates.name: Dylan Helmenstine
candidates.occupation: Former auditor and financial analyst for Wisconsin Medicaid programs; candidate for office; coffee shop barista
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin Heights School Board (2023-present); Village of Black Earth Board (2024-present)
candidates.treas_q1: Voters should elect Dylan Helemenstine to be the state treasurer because he has the plan, energy, and experience to put the office back to work for the people of Wisconsin. He grew up in a rural community, returned home after earning a master’s of public affairs, and has been elected to the school board, village board, and president of the local EMS district. He also served as a National Guard citizen commander during the pandemic, and as an auditor and financial analyst for Wisconsin Medicaid. As treasurer, he will use public power for the public good. He will bring government transparency into the 21st century, defend public education, and protect & grow the common school trust fund.
candidates.treas_q2: Dylan Helmenstine has worked as an auditor and financial analyst for Wisconsin Medicaid programs, helps oversee the state’s public pension system as a Governor’s Appointee to the Teachers’ Retirement Board of Wisconsin, and serves as a school board member, village trustee, and former EMS district president in his local community. These experiences have shown Dylan that our systems are not built for us. Instead, they are made to be controlled by consultants, special interests, and corporations. As state treasurer, he will use public power for the public good. He will defend public education, safeguard Wisconsin’s trust funds, and bring transparency into the 21st century, so Wisconsinites can clearly see where their money goes and trust that it’s working for them.
candidates.treas_q3: It’s not about whether the treasurer's office should be given more or fewer responsibilities. It’s about whether the office is doing enough for Wisconsin communities as a statewide office. In 2018, Wisconsinites made it clear that they wanted to keep an independent Treasurer because they expect the office to stand up for them and use its platform to serve the public good. The treasurer’s office can bring people together, lift up local ideas, and push for practical reforms and solutions. Sarah Godlewski showed what that looks like by using the office to support affordable housing, college savings, and retirement security. Dylan will build on that model by using the office’s statewide reach to increase transparency, protect public trust funds, and better support communities across Wisconsin.
candidates.treas_q4: One of my favorite fun Wisconsin history facts is how much our geography shaped everyday life. In southwest Wisconsin, the Driftless Area’s hills and valleys meant towns were more isolated, so rural communities ended up building a lot of small, local school districts so kids could more easily get to school. That history still shows up today in the challenges rural schools face, like closures, long transportation routes, and limited access to services. It’s part of the reason I care so much about making sure rural communities aren’t left behind.

candidates.name: Lorenzo J. Santos
candidates.cong_q1: The federal government is being dismantled from the top down. We need someone that understands government from the bottom up. As someone who has worked at the local level and served at the federal level, I have broad experience as a Navy veteran, emergency manager, former regional sales manager in the manufacturing industry and as a Navy reservist to see things from many different perspectives and use that knowledge to advocate for the people of the first district. Regardless of party, I will stand up for all Wisconsinites in the first district to ensure there is an economy that works for us all, that everyone has access to quality healthcare and that their right to vote is protected.
candidates.cong_q2: Hard working Wisconsinites are doing everything right but still struggling in this economy. Everyone should be able to afford groceries, no one should have to hold their breath when they are pumping their gas due to high prices and no one should worry that they can't pay their bills, especially those working full-time. Healthcare is an expense we all know is necessary, but it's simply out of reach because we have an administration that doesn't think it's a priority to ensure everyone has access to quality healthcare and Bryan Steil doesn't want us to have it even though we pay for his.
candidates.cong_q3: I have been blessed as the child of a career Navy dentist. That afforded my siblings and I the opportunity to live overseas and all over the country to meet people from all walks of life. I served in the Navy on active duty and as a reservist. I know the diversity of our world is our strength, and we need people in Congress who can combat the limited thinking of those who don't agree. I served in local government as an emergency manager, an expert in coordinating resources and stakeholders to achieve the best outcomes. I understand how best to leverage the power and resources of the federal government to help state and local partners and will do so when I get to Washington.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes, but not only over the president. Over its own power. Congress has ceded too much of its power to the executive branch and needs to take ownership of its role in regulating commerce and the power of the purse. The reason our economy is so devastated is because we allowed a failed businessman to take the reins of the world's largest economy and some of our neighbors miraculously expected positive results where he has never demonstrated any. My hope is that now that it is clearer than ever that Donald Trump is demonstrably inept, even Republican members of Congress will lend a hand in getting the economy back on track due to his failed leadership.
candidates.cong_q5: I'm a huge fan of The West Wing and I think it's great that Bradley Whitford is from Madison. His character, Josh Lyman even helped a Santos get elected in season 7.

candidates.name: Peter Burgelis
candidates.elected_experience: Milwaukee Common Council (2024-present); Milwaukee County Board (2022-2024)
candidates.cong_q1: Voters should send me to Congress because I’ve proven I put people first, not politics or donors. As an alderman, I’ve advanced public safety with common-sense proposals, served on key committees, and delivered for constituents by addressing infrastructure, parking, and small business concerns. My record on the Milwaukee County Board showed I’m willing to make tough decisions while staying focused on fiscal responsibility and accountability. I’ve also made history as an openly LGBTQ leader, fighting to uplift voices too often left out and ensuring that the government protects those who cannot protect themselves. From expanding inclusion to strengthening neighborhoods, my work reflects real results. Bryan Steil serves special interests, I serve the community. I’m ready to bring that commitment to Congress for Wisconsin families.
candidates.cong_q2: Things are less and less affordable — and it’s Trump’s and Steil’s fault. I’m focused on the pain hardworking people in southeast Wisconsin are feeling trying to afford basic necessities like groceries, utilities, housing, etc. These struggles are because of Trumps’ and Steil’s unwillingness to solve the affordability crisis. Trump’s war of choice shows that there’s plenty of money for billionaire tax cuts — just not for hardworking families in Wisconsin who need help. I’m ready to join my colleagues next January to begin the detailed work of urgently creating legislation to provide economic relief for the working families of southeast Wisconsin.
candidates.cong_q3: I bring real, hands-on legislative experience to Congress which no one else in this primary can claim. As an alderman and former county supervisor, I’ve written policy, built coalitions, and delivered results on public safety, fiscal accountability, and neighborhood issues. Just as importantly, I show up. I regularly meet with constituents, listen to concerns, and turn them into action. That’s how representative government is supposed to work. My opponent has relied heavily on telephone town halls while largely avoiding in-person engagement, following broader pressure within his party to limit live events. When he has held them, constituents have voiced deep frustration with his alignment to Trump-era policies. I’ll bring proven leadership, accessibility, and accountability to ensure Wisconsin voices are heard and put first in Congress.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes. Congress must exert strong oversight over the president because that is exactly how our Constitution was designed. The framers created a system of checks and balances to prevent any branch from becoming too powerful. Oversight is not partisan, but a duty. Congress has a legal and moral obligation to hold the executive accountable, demand transparency, and protect the American people. History shows why this matters, from Watergate to modern investigations into executive overreach. When members of Congress fail to uphold this responsibility, they neglect their oath of office. No president, regardless of party, should act without accountability. If leaders refuse to check abuses of power, they aren’t defending the Constitution. They are undermining it, and voters deserve representatives who will stand up and act.
candidates.cong_q5: One of my favorite Wisconsin history facts is that in 1919, our state became the first in the nation to ratify the 19th Amendment, helping secure women the right to vote. That moment reflects something I deeply believe in and Wisconsin often leads by standing on the side of fairness, inclusion, and expanding opportunity. It’s a reminder that progress doesn’t just happen in Washington; it starts in states and communities where people are willing to stand up and do what’s right. That same spirit still defines our state today. Whether it’s fighting for representation, protecting rights, or giving people a voice, I’m proud to come from a place that has always pushed the country forward and I’m committed to carrying that tradition with me.

candidates.name: Mitchell Berman
candidates.cong_q1: I am an ER nurse from rural Wisconsin who worked my way through school and became the first in my family to graduate from college, and I've been a union member at every organized facility I've worked. I spent over a decade at the VA and saw firsthand how gaps in our healthcare system impact veterans and working families. I'm running because it's going to take someone from the bedside and the working class to step up and make an impact, someone who can legislate from a place of empathy and firsthand experience. That's what I'll bring to Washington. Congress isn't reflective of the people in our district — I believe we can change that and make Congress work for the people again.
candidates.cong_q2: Healthcare affordability. As a nurse, I see every day how patients struggle to get the medications and care they need, not because hospitals can't provide them, but because of insurance company practices and government policies that stand in the way. Bryan Steil just voted to strip 15,000 of his own constituents of their health insurance through Medicaid cuts and the expiration of ACA subsidies, which had previously saved families an average of $700 a year. In Congress, I'll fight to protect coverage and lower costs, legislating from a place of empathy and firsthand experience.
candidates.cong_q3: I've spent over twenty years working in healthcare, including over a decade at the VA, where I cared for veterans in high-pressure conditions and saw firsthand how gaps in our healthcare system impact people's lives. I was raised by working-class parents and was the first in my family to graduate from college, working multiple jobs to pay my way through school. These experiences have given me a unique perspective on the challenges facing our communities and will allow me to legislate from a place of empathy, firsthand experience, and commitment to policies that actually serve people.
candidates.cong_q4: Absolutely. As a nurse at the VA, I saw the wounds, both visible and invisible, that our young men and women brought back from Afghanistan and Iraq. Congress has a responsibility to hold the White House accountable. The War Powers Act exists to ensure a president cannot commit our troops to an open-ended engagement without Congressional oversight, and yet Bryan Steil has repeatedly voted against resolutions to serve as a check on the President. In Congress, I'll fight to reassert those powers, ensure accountability, and end corruption in Washington.
candidates.cong_q5: Bong Recreation Area in Kenosha County, right here in our district, is a great spot for hunting, fishing, and enjoying the outdoors. But most people don't know it was named after Richard Bong, a decorated World War II aviator from Wisconsin who shot down more enemy aircraft than any American pilot in history.

candidates.name: Miguel Aranda
candidates.elected_experience: Whitewater Unified School District Board, vice president, (2021-present)
candidates.cong_q1: I bring real working-class experience to the decisions that shape our lives. I live the struggles families face, I have worked the jobs too often overlooked, and know what it means to fight for stability and opportunity. I’m running to be a voice for working families who feel Washington has stopped listening. This campaign is about real representation, rooted in lived experience, and making government work for the people who keep our communities running. I will put families first, and fight for a future where everyone has a fair shot at their American Dream.
candidates.cong_q2: The top issue in our district is the rising cost of living for working families. As a school board member, I see our children struggling, and that reflects how their families are doing. Parents are stretched thin by high costs and a lack of access to good-paying jobs. That’s why our top priority is accessible and affordable childcare. As a working father, my wife and I are fortunate to have community support raising our three children, but many families don’t. Universal childcare gives parents flexibility, allows mothers to continue their careers, and strengthens our economy. When we invest in childcare, we create ripple effects in supporting policy initiatives in public education, universal healthcare, housing, and retirement security. These are policies that lift us all.
candidates.cong_q3: I grew up poor in a mixed-status family, giving me a real understanding of the challenges working families face. I’m also bringing a clear set of policy priorities such as universal childcare to investing in public education. As the only Spanish-speaking candidate, I can directly connect with a constituency that too often feels unheard and underrepresented. Winning twice as an open Democrat in a conservative-leaning school district, my approach is simple but difficult: be transparent, accessible, and accountable. I listen to constituents, ask for honest feedback, and make hard decisions that serve everyone — not just those who voted for me. That’s how we build trust and deliver results for our district.
candidates.cong_q4: Absolutely. One individual should not have absolute, global influence that could endanger us all and impede our individual rights.
candidates.cong_q5: A new fun history fact, which has been a humbling experience, is that I will be the first Mexican-American on the ballot for Wisconsin's 1st Congressional District. This could not have been done without the support of family, community members, neighbors, and new friends.

candidates.name: Douglas Alexander
candidates.cong_q1:
1) The first step to grab back power from a corrupt and dysfunctional Congress is to impose term limits on Congress.
2) It requires a constitutional amendment.
3) You say “That’s hopeless Douglas! — Congress will never propose it.”
4) I say “Silly Wabbit, that’s what I thought, but Constitution Article V states if two-thirds of state legislatures call for a constitutional amendment on an issue, it gets proposed, thus end-running Congress.”
5) Fifteen states have already called for a constitutional amendment imposing term limits on Congress; 14 are in various stages of consideration. We only need five more, and we’ll have done it. There IS hope!
If elected, I’ll testify at state legislatures as a sitting member of Congress why its important they support this constitutional amendment.
candidates.cong_q2:
My issues: 
--$39 trillion debt.
--Providing undocumented immigrants a reasonable path to citizenship, so they are released from uncomfortable, quasi-slave working environments.
--Avoiding incoherent wars.
--Our dysfunctional health system brings obscene wealth to pharmaceutical and insurance companies and other power brokers quite happy JUST the way it is.
--Farm bill: rewards big ag and big chemical companies, and discourages regenerative farmers who recognize the failures of nutrition-bankrupt industrial farming.
--Pornography. No self-respecting society would put up with subjecting their youth to a firehose of moral sewage imprinting their minds with sexual violence, degredation, and domination. Love is patient and kind. It does not insist on its own way. 
--However…my TOP issue is getting career politicians out of Congress, for otherwise, none of the above will be addressed.
candidates.cong_q3: I’ve enjoyed wide and varied experiences: growing up in Madison, exchange year in England, political science major, Bucknell University, Navy P-3 pilot, ninth grade civics teacher, software instructor, major account executive in technical sales, paperboy in my 50s. Inneagram 7; Meyer’s Briggs J-E-R-K. I would bring to Congress integrity, a sense of humor, a serious intent on reforming it via term limits, a remarkable ability to establish rapport with members having differing views. Of specific concern is reforming the farm bill. Otherwise, our district is similar to most: they want Congress to do its job, stay in its lane, and stop spending more than it has. They want Congress to tone down the acrimony, and put more effort into solving issues than ensuring they get re-elected.
candidates.cong_q4: Heck yes.
candidates.cong_q5: I absolutely love living in Wisconsin. I lived along the Eastern US for more than 25 years. Returning to Wisconsin was one of the best decisions of my life. This “fun fact” probably isn’t what the intelligent, good-looking folks at Wisconsin Watch had in mind, but in 2021 Wisconsin became one of the 15 states to call for a constitutional amendment to impose term limits on Congress. (I testified in favor.) My website will soon show at what stages the 50 states are towards passing the resolution. Then all of you can call/text/email family and friends in that state, asking them to contact their state legislators to support it. This is how we together can assert our rights, grabbing back power from a corrupt and dysfunctional Congress!

candidates.name: Derrick Van Orden
candidates.elected_experience: US House of Representatives, WI03, 4 years
candidates.cong_q1: I’m a 26-year U.S. Navy SEAL veteran who served five combat tours, a small business owner, and a father. I’ve spent my life serving, building, and fighting for something bigger than myself. In Congress, I’ve worked to bring accountability back to Washington and stand up for rural Wisconsin families who feel ignored by the political class. I’ve pushed back on policies that drive up costs and weaken our communities, and I’ve focused on delivering results for veterans, farmers, and working families across WI-03.
candidates.cong_q2: I’m fighting to make sure rural communities like ours are never overlooked. That means standing up against wasteful Washington spending that fuels inflation, unleashing American energy to lower costs, and cutting unnecessary regulations that hold back our farmers and small businesses. I’m also working to strengthen rural infrastructure so our roads, bridges, broadband, and agricultural systems are not left behind or neglected. My goal is simple. Put rural America first, protect our agricultural economy, and make sure people can keep more of what they earn while building a real future in places like ours.
candidates.cong_q3: I bring 26 years as a U.S. Navy SEAL, including five combat deployments, along with experience as a small business owner and most importantly, a father. In Congress, I serve on the Agriculture, Veterans Affairs, and Armed Services Committees. More importantly, I’ve lived the same challenges many Wisconsin families face —balancing responsibilities, working hard to get ahead, and trying to give your kids a better shot than you had. I don’t need Washington to tell me what people are going through here. I’ve lived it. That’s why I focus on practical solutions that lower costs, strengthen paychecks, and make sure hard work actually pays off again in our communities.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes. Congress has a constitutional responsibility to conduct oversight of the executive branch, regardless of who is president. I’ve supported strong oversight of the Biden administration’s reckless spending and its failure to secure the southern border. Those policies created inflation, strained communities, and weakened trust in government. Oversight is not partisan, it’s essential to restoring accountability and ensuring the executive branch serves the American people.
candidates.cong_q5: The first commercial cheese factory opened here in 1868, launching an industry that made Wisconsin “America’s Dairyland.” Today, we still lead the nation in cheese production, and that success is built on generations of hardworking farmers across WI-03.

candidates.name: Emily Berge
candidates.elected_experience: Eau Claire City Council, member (2018-2023); Eau Claire City Council, president (2023-2026)
candidates.cong_q1: I have eight years of elected experience, including serving as the highest elected official in the largest city in the district. I also served as the League of Wisconsin Municipalities president. I have a proven record of bringing people together to solve problems and deliver results. I was raised with values of honesty, compassion, and opportunity for all, and those guide my leadership. I believe the government should improve people's lives, not make them harder. Leaders should unite communities rather than divide. For the past 14 months, I’ve traveled across all 19 counties of the 3rd Congressional District, listening and showing up in local communities. My campaign is rooted in western and central Wisconsin, and I’m demonstrating the kind of leadership I’ll bring to Congress.
candidates.cong_q2: I've traveled across all 19 counties in the 3rd CD, talking with people of all ages, backgrounds, and political perspectives. The issue I hear about most is healthcare. Too many people can't afford insurance or access critical care, including mental health services. That's why I support Medicare for All. In this race, I’m the only candidate advocating for universal healthcare. Many young people, farmers, and small business owners go without healthcare. Everyone deserves quality, affordable care. We're watching hospitals close and critical services disappear, from labor and delivery to hospice to mental health care. The U.S. is the only developed nation without universal healthcare. It's time to change and elect leaders prioritizing healthcare over endless foreign wars and tax cuts for the ultra-wealthy.
candidates.cong_q3: I’m the only candidate in this primary with elected experience. Over the past eight years in local government, I’ve worked with community members and government leaders to address issues affecting everyday people, including housing, water quality, and economic opportunity. As the highest elected official in the largest city in our district, I advocated for my community in Madison and Washington. When outside extremists targeted our community, I stood up for constituents and didn’t back down. I lead with courage, integrity, and commitment to common good. As a licensed professional counselor, I’ve supported people through the most difficult moments of their lives. I know how to listen, navigate conflict, and bring people together to solve problems. These experiences prepared me to effectively advocate for 3rd CD.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes. Congress has significant oversight powers under the Constitution. It needs to use them. Congress has authority to investigate the executive, control federal spending, regulate trade and tariffs, and decide to authorize or end wars. Too often, members of both parties defer to leadership instead of what's best for our country. Representatives should answer to the people, not parties or wealthy donors. Strong oversight is one of the most important ways to check executive power and protect democracy. We need campaign finance reform so elected officials are accountable to constituents rather than concentrated wealth and special interests. I’m committed to the people and will answer to them, not Washington. It’s how I’ve run my campaign, and it’s how I’ll serve in Congress.
candidates.cong_q5: Wisconsin was the first state to have a kindergarten in the country. Margarethe Meyer Schurz opened the first kindergarten in the United States in Watertown in 1856, just eight years after Wisconsin became a state. She later shared the concept with Elizabeth Peabody in Pennsylvania, helping spread early childhood education across the nation. As someone with an undergraduate degree in human development and family studies, I know how important the early years are in a child's development. This piece of Wisconsin history reminds me that when we invest in children, we invest in our future. Strong schools, supportive families, and opportunities for every child help build stronger communities and Wisconsin helped lead the way.

candidates.name: Alexander Valiensi Kent
candidates.cong_q1: "One voter, one vote on all issues." This is our voter empowerment promise. We believe we can come together on VoterDirectedNetwork.com and collectively discuss, research, and vote on issues. Online issue voting is possible. It’s a modern, honest, logical and intuitive way to practice democratic republicanism that’s 100% constitutional. We made an anti-corruption promise: No donors, lobbyists, Super PACs, or parties. There will be nothing between voters and their constitutional power to be represented on every issue. The party controlled political system is divide and conquer. It doesn't represent voters, it controls voters. Representing voters has always been easy. Ask all voters on all issues- they’ll tell you what they need and want. Then do it. This is how a democratic republic should function.
candidates.cong_q2: The economy. The authoritarian party controlled political system broke our economy enough that basic necessities- safe shelter, nutritious food, healthcare, energy- are increasingly unaffordable for over half of all voters. It's terrible. It’s caused immense human suffering for decades. Votes don't want to live like this. Full voter empowerment solves all systemic social, political, and economic issues. Our collective knowledge, wisdom, and expertise on issues is immense. Voters need and should have full control over the federal budget to choose what to fund, subsidize, and privatize. Voters need full control over and to be fully REPresented on every issue- this is what REPublics should do. When our republic actually represents voters on all issues, the vast majority of our issues will disappear within a generation.
candidates.cong_q3: Systems thinking. This is my greatest strength and passion. We have to improve how SYSTEMS operate in order to improve outcomes for individual voters, children, and families. To improve upon any social, political, or economic issue that causes human suffering we must address the system behind it that has created the suffering. Collectively voters are immensely compassionate and know so much about the human condition. Collectively we know exactly how to build social, political, and economic governing mentalities (government system) that will lead our country to mass peace, prosperity, and thriving. We just need to empower the real Will of the People on all issues. Voters know what they need- they always have. Corrupt and violent political parties have just always gotten in the way.
candidates.cong_q4: We need to follow the U.S. Constitution. The checks and balances and division of power in the U.S. Constitution need to be followed. Political parties are authoritarian structures and are NOT in the U.S. Constitution. Political parties are and have been the biggest corrupt, divisive, and violent authoritarian problem in our republic for a very long time. We were all meant to be equally empowered Independents represented by Independent elected officials at all levels and in all branches of government. The Will of the People should control all branches of government and be represented in all branches of government. This is what a REPublic is- a REPresentative government institution. Our governing mentalities must represent the voters. The ONLY way to represent voters on any issue is to ask all voters. If all three branches are aligned with the real Will of the People then voters will have oversight over all branches of government AND the internal oversight mechanisms in the U.S. Constitution will also work well or not even be needed.
candidates.cong_q5: Wisconsin is truly one of the most beautiful pieces of land in the entire world. Our geography and biodiversity is stunning. The 3rd Congressional District (where I am so fortunate to live) has one of the most breath-taking landscapes. Much of the district is composed of what is known as the Driftless Area. Where does this name come from? It is named for the lack of glacial drift in the area: the silt, gravel, and rock left behind by glaciers that can be found in other parts of Wisconsin. The Driftless Area was never covered by ice during the Last Glacial Period, so the area lacks the characteristic glacial deposits known as drift. Its landscape is characterized by steep hills, forested ridges, deeply carved river valleys, and karst geology with spring-fed waterfalls and cold-water trout streams. It is such a blessing to live in such a beautiful place that is also filled with so many wonderful people and unique rural, urban, and suburban communities.

candidates.name: Rustin Provance
candidates.occupation: Full-time certified nursing assistant; part-time HVAC-heating and cooling tech
candidates.cong_q1: I don't want to be there. I want to be in my home in Wisconsin with my community, I do however want to give as much back to the people as possible. I will vote for what they want for my whole term and leave knowing I voted on behalf of what the people wanted and not the lobbyist. This is not a career position or a job to gain power. This is an opportunity to make every day people's life's better.
candidates.cong_q2: Healthcare is a major issue. I would write and push a bill that would require medical facility providers to have healthcare for staff in order to run any healthcare facility in the nation. I would write a bill and propose a resolution that would require insurance companies to return 75% of the last fiscal year healthcare payments to the insurance company back to the consumer if they do not use their health insurance in the last fiscal year for any medical needs.
candidates.cong_q3: I am not organization backed; I am running truly Independent. That makes my only priority, the people of my district. My plans are to meet monthly with each county in my district to discuss their needs in real time with the voters. bring in open communication. Giving the people in my district their power back on what they want to do to move forward and hand voting power back over to them regarding congressional votes
candidates.cong_q4: Yes, we should have better checks and balances on the president and on congress. Why, congress is in charge of the government purse. If the president knows we are in debt and still spending money. That's an issue and a major problem.
candidates.cong_q5: That Pepin County in Wisconsin was never supposed to be a county. It was made up because of an angry politician that didn't get his way. So, he made up a county up. On February 25th,1858, by a special act of the Wisconsin legislature. No longer to be part of Dunn southern township or part of Chippewa

candidates.name: Rebecca Cooke
candidates.cong_q1: We need more people in Congress with working class backgrounds who have experienced failed policies and are going to lead from those lived experiences to deliver results for our communities. I grew up on a dairy farm in Eau Claire where we had to sell our cows because of the low price of milk and corporate competition. I went on to elect changemakers to public office before I came back home to start a small business and nonprofit focused on providing start-up capital to women-owned businesses across northwest Wisconsin. Because of that work I was appointed by Governor Evers to the Wisconsin Economic Development Corp. I'm running for Congress to embolden the working class and reclaim rural power.
candidates.cong_q2: Healthcare access and affordability are the biggest challenges facing communities across the region. Families are worried about rising costs, provider shortages, and losing local services. Recently, two major hospitals closed in Eau Claire, and in parts of the district, the nearest hospital with labor and delivery services is more than 40 minutes away. I've been meeting with health care providers, patients, and local leaders across the district to better understand these challenges. In Congress, I’ll work to expand Medicare to cover vision dental & hearing, create pipeline programs to bolster our healthcare workforce, increase Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement rates to keep our rural hospitals and clinics open. No one should have to travel hours or worry about going bankrupt to get the care they need.
candidates.cong_q3: As a small business owner, I know what it’s like to start a business, process payroll and balance a budget. If we had more leaders with business acumen in Congress we might be able to do something about our national debt. I founded a nonprofit to support other women on that same path to entrepreneurship — helping over 70 small businesses launch. Because of that work Gov. Evers appointed me to the Wisconsin Economic Development Board. In Congress, I’ll be able to lead on agricultural initiatives because of my family’s background in farming and pass a farm bill to support family farms vs. corporate ag. I’ll lead initiatives that support main street vs. wall street. And I’ll fight like hell to lower costs across the board.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes. Congress has a constitutional responsibility to provide oversight of the executive branch, regardless of who is president. Oversight promotes accountability, transparency, and responsible use of taxpayer dollars. It should be conducted in a fair, fact-based manner and focused on ensuring government works for the American people.
candidates.cong_q5: Wisconsin is the largest producer of cranberries in the country — with ample growers here in WI-03. Why? When the glacier receded from central Wisconsin (think Warrens, Wisconsin Rapids) it left a sandy region (Central Sands!) where typical cash crops like corn or soybeans can’t grow. This left a rich environment for native cranberries and led to a burgeoning family-led industry of growers.

candidates.name: Purnima Nath
candidates.cong_q1: Our Republic is buckling under the weight of partisan arrogance and the erosion of institutional norms. We deserve leaders who view the Constitution not as a suggestion, but as the bedrock of our democracy. I am running to restore the vital separation of powers, ensuring that Congress acts as a robust check on executive overreach, regardless of which party holds the White House. As a Lincoln Republican, I prioritise the rule of law, fiscal integrity, and a foreign policy rooted in steady, principled strength rather than volatile rhetoric. I am not beholden to the populist extremes of either side. If you are tired of the toxic polarisation and want a representative who will defend our institutions and Constitution, I ask for your vote.
candidates.cong_q2: The top issue in our district is the erosion of opportunity and quality of life, driven by economic stagnation, high taxation, educational concerns, housing shortages, and public safety challenges. These are not merely administrative lapses; they are the result of a political system that prioritises partisan theatre over institutional stewardship. As your Representative, I will champion federal incentive-based reform, making competitive grants for infrastructure and housing contingent on states adopting sustainable, tax-neutral funding models. By leveraging my background in engineering, management, corporate, nonprofit and foreign affairs-geopolitical strategy, I will streamline federal regulatory processes to incentivise private-sector production. I am committed to restoring fiscal discipline and demanding accountability. Governance is a serious, professional discipline — not a performance — and I am prepared to rebuild the prosperity our community deserves.
candidates.cong_q3: I bring the rigor of an engineer, the strategic foresight of an MBA, and the empathy of a nonprofit leader to Congress. My background as a geopolitical advisor allows me to analyse long-term systemic risks, while my experience as a corporate labourer and manager ensures I understand the practicalities of the American economy. I don’t just react to headlines; I apply forensic analysis to dismantle bureaucratic inefficiencies and restore institutional integrity. Whether leveraging federal incentives to reform local infrastructure or advocating for fiscal discipline, I offer a professional, solutions-oriented approach. I’m not a career politician seeking a title; I’m a strategist and builder dedicated to ensuring the long-term prosperity of our Republic. Governance is a serious profession of public service, not a performance.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes, Congress must exert robust oversight over the president. It is not merely a matter of political preference; it is a fundamental constitutional duty. The Founders designed our Republic with a system of checks and balances precisely to prevent the concentration of unchecked power. When Congress abdicates its responsibility to monitor the executive branch, it creates a dangerous vacuum that inevitably leads to administrative overreach, fiscal waste, and the erosion of the rule of law. Oversight is the primary mechanism through which Congress ensures that laws are faithfully executed and that the executive remains accountable to the people. A Congress that fails to exercise this power is a Congress that has forgotten its role as the guardian of the Republic.
candidates.cong_q5: The story of the 1820s lead miners whose grit earned us the "Badger" name. It resonates deeply with my own journey. I arrived here not as a tourist with a map, but as a corporate laborer focused on building products and services for the American economy. I did not choose Milwaukee; this city— w ith its industrial soul, its "Cream City" resilience, and its vibrant history as a cultural hub — chose me. My cultural roots in India have shaped my perspective, but Milwaukee has become the fabric of my life. From our rich ethnic diversity to the spirit of festivals like our own IndiaFest, I see that same "Badger" tenacity in every corner of our community. I am proud to serve the city that claimed me.

candidates.name: Amy Donahue
candidates.cong_q1: I’m a healthcare worker, public school parent, member of the LGBTQIA+ community, and organizer who has built a strong, deep, and vibrant network with connections across Wisconsin’s Congressional District 4, from Brown Deer to West Allis. This is the foundation I’ll have in Congress, legislating for CD4 in Washington, and the roots I’ll return to when I’m back home working in the district, connecting the power found in local, state, and federal offices. I am not a career politician, and I have not and will not accept donations from corporate political action committees. I answer only to the people of CD4, and I will fight with you to topple fascism, authoritarianism, and the billionaire class, to ensure the best possible future for all of us.
candidates.cong_q2: Cost of living is the top issue, based on what I’m reading, hearing, and experiencing myself. Working people are choosing between food, transportation, housing, healthcare, keeping the lights on, and so on. Affordability connects public safety, public health, the environment, education, and more. We are one of  the richest countries in the world, and we have to do better. To address affordability, I support taxing the ultra rich (H.R. 8085), blocking the use of tax dollars for bombs (H.R. 3565), enacting Medicare for All (H.R. 3069), and supporting the Green New Deal. I will work with everyone who shares these goals to both move these pieces of legislation forward and to hold those who stand in the way accountable to their constituents.
candidates.cong_q3: My unique career trajectory from medical librarian to genetic counselor comes with some highly specific expertise. But that expertise dovetails with my community organizing, and is rooted in helping people articulate their questions/concerns, and connecting them to next steps and resources. I translate complicated topics into direct implications and advocate for systemic changes and new solutions to address unmet needs. I build connections across the communities I work with, live in, and am a part of with authenticity, respect, and empathy. I will use all of this to help my district by elevating conversations on reparations, immigration, public safety, and more, and identifying and procuring resources that will help us (whether through federal legislation, community funded projects, or other channels).
candidates.cong_q4: Yes. I believe that in these times, when the balance of the three branches of government (executive, legislative, and judicial) has shifted so far to the president (with the help of the supreme court), Congress has an existential duty to pull on every lever of power in its control. When lawyers, legal scholars, political scientists, and other experts across the political spectrum are in agreement that the U.S. is accelerating towards authoritarianism and provide clear reasoning for their arguments, with data and examples (https://protectdemocracy.org/threat-tracker/), I listen. As a librarian, I know how insidious misinformation is, how numbing information overload is, and I see the window for fascist authoritarianism opening. Congress is absolutely vital in keeping it closed.
candidates.cong_q5: I have multiple, but will summarize as a single fact! One: Sen. Gaylord Nelson of Wisconsin is the founder of Earth Day. Second: the Waisman Center in Madison, which houses the genetic counseling graduate program I attended, is named after four-time UW alumnus Dr. Harry A. Waisman, who successfully advocated for creating a national newborn screening program (the heel prick blood test that identifies babies born with rare genetic diseases in time for effective treatment). Three: Milwaukee is the birthplace of “sewer socialism” and is now the launchpoint for a rebirth of socialist electeds in Wisconsin. So, to summarize my favorite fun fact: Wisconsin has an amazing history full of people and events that have had an enormous impact on the country and the world!

candidates.name: Gwen Moore
candidates.elected_experience: U.S. House (2005-present); Wisconsin State Senate (1993-1995); Wisconsin State Assembly (1989-1993)
candidates.cong_q1: I’ve proudly represented the 4th Congressional District since January 2005. It has been the honor of my lifetime to represent the hardworking Wisconsinites that call the 4th district home. I’m humbly seeking another term this coming November and it is with that awesome responsibility I know our work is more critical now more than ever. This next Congress must serve as a check on the executive overreach of the current administration and with that comes the need for established and tested leadership in the Congress.
candidates.cong_q2: Along with millions of others, the core issue my constituents face is affordability. That drives access to everything — healthcare, housing, the ability to feed your family, and transportation costs just to name a few. We’ve seen time and again, corporate profits far exceed our general ability to keep up. In short, prices keep increasing while wages have stayed stagnant. This is something we need to address in the coming Congress and hopefully with a Democratic administration starting in 2029.
candidates.cong_q3: Since my first election, I held seat on the power Financial Services Committee — which addresses a multitude of financial issues that face everyday Americans. I worked with then Chairman Barney Frank in helping pass the critical Dodd-Frank legislation, which was a cornerstone of financial reform in the last 20 years. Recently, I’ve been appointed to the House Committee on Ways and Means, which is one of the oldest committees in the Congress and has a voice in all bills and proposed legislation that comes through Congress. This experience and expertise are critical to the services I bring to the 4th CD.
candidates.cong_q4: The founders originally envisioned three co-equal branches of government and for over 200 years that was the general consensus of body politic. The election of President Trump in 2016 and then again in 2024 dramatically changed everything and we’ve seen a Republican majority, as well as a Supreme Court, treat itself as an arm of the executive branch instead of co-equal branch of government. To that end, yes, more oversight is desperately needed. We must put an end to this unbridled and unchecked power grab and bring back some pre-Trump normality to our politics.
candidates.cong_q5: In 1854, Joshua Glover, an escaped slave from Missouri, was captured in Milwaukee. Local abolitionists raided the jail, freed him, and helped him safely escape to Canada by boat from Racine. This incident led the Wisconsin Supreme Court to become the only state high court in the nation to declare the federal Fugitive Slave Act unconstitutional.

candidates.name: Andrew Beck
candidates.cong_q1: Voters should send me to Congress because I will put the people of Wisconsin’s 5th District ahead of party politics, special interests, and wealthy insiders. I’m a healthcare professional, business leader, union family member, and lifelong Wisconsin resident who understands the challenges working families face. I’m running to lower costs, create good-paying jobs, protect Social Security and Medicare, defend personal freedoms, and make healthcare more affordable. Government should work for ordinary people, not just those with money and influence. Scott Fitzgerald has spent years representing the powerful. I’m running to bring practical, common-sense leadership and a fresh voice to Washington. As I like to say, a change will do you good.
candidates.cong_q2: The top issue I hear across Wisconsin’s 5th District is affordability. Families are paying more for groceries, housing, healthcare, childcare, and utilities while wages struggle to keep up. Too many people are working hard but falling behind. In Congress, I would focus on lowering healthcare costs, protecting Social Security and Medicare, increasing affordable housing, supporting workforce training and apprenticeship programs, and standing up to corporate price gouging that drives up costs for consumers. I also support policies that strengthen American manufacturing and family farms, creating good-paying jobs here in Wisconsin. Working families deserve an economy that works for them — not just for corporations and the wealthy.
candidates.cong_q3: I would bring real-world experience from healthcare, manufacturing, technology, and small-business leadership. I spent years as an MRI technologist caring for patients, worked for a major Wisconsin healthcare company, and have led sales and business operations serving organizations ranging from local businesses to global manufacturers. That experience gives me a practical understanding of the challenges facing workers, employers, healthcare providers, and families. I know how decisions made in Washington affect jobs, healthcare costs, supply chains, and economic growth here at home. Wisconsin’s 5th District needs a representative who understands how policy impacts people in their daily lives. I will focus on practical solutions that create jobs, strengthen local businesses, lower costs, and improve access to affordable healthcare.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes. Congress has a constitutional responsibility to provide oversight of the executive branch, regardless of which party controls the White House. Effective oversight helps ensure that laws are followed, taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly, and government agencies remain accountable to the public. Checks and balances are one of the foundations of our democracy. When Congress fails to exercise oversight, power becomes too concentrated in one branch of government. Oversight should not be partisan or political theater — it should be focused on transparency, accountability, and protecting the public interest. I believe members of Congress should be willing to ask tough questions, follow the facts, and uphold their constitutional duties no matter who occupies the Oval Office.
candidates.cong_q5: One of my favorite Wisconsin history facts is that much of our state’s landscape was shaped by glaciers during the last Ice Age. As those massive sheets of ice advanced and retreated, they carved out lakes, rolling hills, kettles, moraines, and river valleys that still define Wisconsin today. What makes this especially interesting is that the glaciers largely missed the southwestern part of the state, creating the unique “Driftless Area,” known for its rugged terrain and steep bluffs. Because of this glacial history, Wisconsin has one of the most diverse and beautiful landscapes in the Midwest —from the Kettle Moraine to the Mississippi River Valley. It’s a reminder that Wisconsin’s natural beauty was thousands of years in the making.

candidates.name: Amanda Bell
candidates.cong_q1: For 24 years, I served the American people as a federal scientist at the U.S. Geological Survey. I managed a three-state office, oversaw 125 employees, and stewarded a $33 million  budget, all in service of evidence-based science that protects our water, our land and our communities. Science doesn’t have a political agenda. Neither do I. I understand how federal agencies work, how policy gets made, and how to fight for the resources our district needs. Wisconsin’s 6th district deserves a representative with real public service experience, real scientific credentials, and real accountability to the people, not to corporate donors.
candidates.cong_q2: The number one issue I hear across WI-6 is the cost of living. Gas, groceries, health care, housing, families are working harder than ever and still falling behind. This is the result of policies that protect corporate profits over working people. I’ll fight to lower prescription drug costs, expand affordable health care coverage, raise the federal minimum wage, and crack down on the price gouging by corporations that use inflation as cover to pad their margins. I spent 24 years managing federal resources and delivering results on a budget. I know how to cut waste, prioritize spending, and get things done. That’s the experience Wisconsin families deserve in Congress right now.
candidates.cong_q3: I bring a unique perspective to Congress after more than 24 years as a federal scientist focused on water quality, environmental research, and conservation. I know how to take complex problems and turn them into real solutions for real people. As deputy director of a three-state U.S. Geological Survey office, I managed a $33 million budget and led 230 employees across 13 facilities. I’ve worked alongside federal agencies at every level of government. WI-6 has real water and environmental challenges. I don’t need to be brought up to speed. I’ve spent my entire career working on problems just like them, and I’m ready to get to work on day one.
candidates.cong_q4: Absolutely. Our constitution designed our government to be a three-branch system with checks and balances. Right now, our judicial and legislative branches are not holding the executive branch accountable.
candidates.cong_q5: Wisconsin has produced more conservation giants than just about any state in the nation. John Muir grew up on a farm near Portage. Aldo Leopold wrote “A Sand County Almanac” right here in Wisconsin. Gaylord Nelson, a Wisconsin governor and U.S. senator, founded Earth Day. And the Wisconsin Conservation Hall of Fame, based in Stevens Point, has inducted over 80 Wisconsinites who shaped how this country thinks about land, water, and wildlife. Conservation is Wisconsin’s DNA, and I’m proud to carry that tradition into Congress.

candidates.name: Matthew Arndt
candidates.occupation: Tax accounting and finance business owner
candidates.cong_q1: Voters should send me to Congress because I don't owe my career to either political party, corporate PACs, billionaire donors, or foreign interests. I'm running because I believe the American people deserve representatives who answer to them and only them. If voters are looking for another politician who will repeat talking points, they have plenty of options. If they're looking for someone willing to speak honestly, challenge powerful interests, and fight for ordinary Americans, then I ask for their vote.
candidates.cong_q2: The top issue facing Wisconsin's 6th Congressional District is the rising cost of living. Families are paying more for housing, healthcare, childcare, groceries, and education while wages struggle to keep pace. Many people work harder than ever but feel like they're falling behind. I’d address this by focusing on policies strengthening the economic position of working people. That includes protecting workers' rights to organize, enforcing antitrust laws against monopolies driving up prices, supporting small businesses and family farms, investing in infrastructure and manufacturing, and reducing healthcare costs. I believe Congress should measure policies by one standard: Does it improve the lives of ordinary Americans? If elected, my priority will be building an economy that serves working families rather than concentrated wealth and powerful special interests.
candidates.cong_q3: I would bring real-world expertise in taxation, small business, investing, and financial planning. As a CPA, business owner, and investment advisor, I work directly with families, retirees, farmers, workers, and entrepreneurs. I see firsthand how government policies affect people's daily lives, from healthcare costs and taxes to inflation and retirement security. Too many members of Congress come from political or legal backgrounds and have never operated a business, met payroll, or helped families navigate financial challenges. My experience allows me to evaluate legislation based on its real economic impact rather than partisan talking points. That perspective would help Wisconsin's 6th District by ensuring that federal policies support working families, small businesses, and local communities instead of primarily benefiting large corporations and special interests.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes. Congress should exercise stronger oversight over the president regardless of which party controls the White House. The Constitution created three co-equal branches of government, not an elected monarchy. Congress has a responsibility to review executive actions, investigate waste, fraud, and abuse, ensure laws are faithfully executed, and protect the constitutional rights of the American people. Unfortunately, too many members of Congress abandon oversight when their own party holds power and suddenly rediscover it when the other party wins. That is not how our system is supposed to work. I will support consistent, principled oversight of any administration. Government accountability should never be partisan. It is one of Congress' most important responsibilities and essential to maintaining a healthy constitutional republic.
candidates.cong_q5: One of my favorite Wisconsin history facts is that the state was once home to the world's largest brewery. For many years, Milwaukee was known as the beer capital of America, with breweries like Pabst Brewing Company, Schlitz, and Miller Brewing Company helping put Wisconsin on the map. What I enjoy most about that history isn't the beer itself— it's what it says about Wisconsin. Generations of immigrants came here, built businesses, created jobs, and helped shape thriving communities. That entrepreneurial spirit, strong work ethic, and sense of community are still part of Wisconsin's identity today. It's a fun reminder that Wisconsin has always been a place where people build things and contribute to something larger than themselves.

candidates.name: Mike Thurow
candidates.cong_q1: 2% of Congress comes from the working class. As its made up now Congress is a club of millionaires serving the interests of billionaires and multi national corporations. Both parties take billions of dollars from these corporations, I am not and will not take money from them. I will work to break up corporate monopolies, ban Congressional stock trading and take on the for profit health industry profiting from our sickest and most vulnerable.
candidates.cong_q2: The Economy. From gas to groceries this economy is failing the vast majority of us. Most markets have shifted from free markets to anti-competitive cartels controlled by 4-5 major corporations at the top that stifle competition, set prices for sellers and buyers, and hoard profits for themselves. This has happened in farming, grocery stores, healthcare, tech, fire truck production, etc. I will show up to congress on day one ready to bring case after case to the FTC to enforce anti-trust rules, as they have mostly gone unenforced since the 1970s.
candidates.cong_q3: I am currently Wisconsin's HAZMAT director meaning I coordinate directly with government agencies, and build budgets based on available state and federal resources. So I have experience in allocating and selecting government resources based on a state wide departments needs. Most importantly though I bring the expertise of a normal American. I work 52 hour weeks, pick up overtime when I can, send my kids to public schools, and try to give them access to more than I had. Lived experience is not something you can't teach, or read about, and to continue to send a representative to DC who does not have this experience that the vast majority of WI-06 has is why we continue to see Congress not listen to us.
candidates.cong_q4: Since Obama started his drone wars with half the Middle East our Congress has allowed every president since to commit daily acts of war without their vote of approval. It is one of the most cowardly things I can think of from any government body, and has been going on for almost two decades now. So, in short, Yes!
candidates.cong_q5: The Republican party started and was founded in Ripon Wisconsin in response to the failure of the Democratic party and the Whigs.

candidates.name: Brad Smith
candidates.occupation: Owner and principal consultant, Kinetic Pursuit
candidates.cong_q1: I'm a lifelong Wisconsinite, Army veteran, dad, and business leader. I’m running because too many families are working harder than ever and still falling behind while billionaires and special interests keep getting ahead. My three key campaign pillars: a fair economy, including good-paying jobs that stay in Wisconsin, affordable healthcare as a fundamental right, and education and job training for every path, whether that’s college, the trades, or an apprenticeship. I’ve led soldiers in combat, built businesses, and raised a family here in the 6th District. I know the challenges our communities face because I’ve lived them. I’m not running to serve a party or special interests. I’m running to serve the people of Wisconsin and help rebuild a stronger middle class.
candidates.cong_q2:
The core problem: The economy is no longer working for the people who keep it running. Wages aren’t keeping up with rent, groceries, childcare or healthcare. Good jobs are being shipped out or automated away, while the cost of just living life keeps climbing. Solutions:
1) Raise wages by strengthening the right to organize and bargain so workers actually have leverage again. 
2) Stop rewarding companies that outsource jobs or cut corners after taking public support. If taxpayers help fund you, you should be creating jobs in the district.
3) Bring down the big cost drivers: healthcare, prescription drugs, childcare, and housing.
4) Invest in training and apprenticeships so workers can move into the jobs that are growing instead of getting left behind by automation and AI.
candidates.cong_q3: As a veteran, business leader, and first-generation college graduate, I would bring practical, real-world experience to Congress. My experience in the Wisconsin National Guard taught me discipline, accountability, and the importance of putting country over politics. My business background taught me how to manage budgets, support workers, lead teams through times of change, and make decisions that strengthen communities. And because the GI Bill changed my life, I understand how education and training can open doors and change a family's trajectory for generations. I would use that experience to fight for good-paying jobs, affordable healthcare, strong schools, and real solutions that help Wisconsin’s 6th District move forward together.
candidates.cong_q4: Congress not only should exert oversight over the president, it has a duty to do so. The founders didn’t create a system for blind loyalty to any one person in power. They built checks and balances because power concentrates fast, and when it does, working people pay the price. Oversight means sunlight. It means demanding answers when agencies overreach, when taxpayer dollars are misused, or when decisions are made behind closed doors that affect families in Wisconsin. This isn’t about party. It’s about responsibility. If Congress stops doing its job, it stops protecting the people it represents. I’ll support strong, serious oversight of any president, Republican or Democrat, because accountability isn’t optional; it’s the job.
candidates.cong_q5: Wisconsin is where Earth Day was born. In 1970, Senator Gaylord Nelson from Wisconsin helped spark a national environmental movement by organizing the first Earth Day, a moment that started here and spread across the country and the world. It’s one of those quiet Wisconsin facts that says a lot about us: we don’t just talk about protecting the outdoors, we’ve led on it.

candidates.name: Elizabeth Anne Fitzgibbon
candidates.cong_q1: Voters should send me to Congress because they deserve a representative who answers to them, not a party machine, special interests, or corporate donors. For too long, both parties have blamed each other during campaigns while costs rise, government becomes less accountable, and families struggle once those same politicians are in power. My background is not in political theater. I am running to restore constitutional limits, demand real transparency, and tackle the root causes of skyrocketing costs. I’ll ask the questions both parties avoid: Who benefits from this broken system? Who pays the price? And how do we give power back to the people? As an Independent, I will challenge what is wrong, support what is right, and refuse to let Washington ignore Wisconsin families.
candidates.cong_q2: The top issue is affordability. Families across the 6th District are working hard, but groceries, gas, housing, utilities, health care, and everyday expenses keep taking more of our paychecks. There’s an old saying: “Don’t p*** on my back and tell me it’s raining.” Washington cannot keep spending recklessly, creating red tape, protecting special interests, and then pretending someone else is to blame while families struggle. I would address this with a root-cause audit of Washington: serious oversight of federal spending, cutting waste, fraud, and abuse, reducing unnecessary burdens on families and small businesses, and challenging policies that protect monopolies instead of real competition. Taxpayers deserve to know where their money goes, who benefits, and why government makes life more expensive.
candidates.cong_q3: I bring the perspective of a mother, advocate, and litigant for liberty who has personally confronted powerful institutions that were supposed to serve people but instead protected themselves. My path to this campaign came through my landmark family law case that reached the U.S. Supreme Court and exposed serious failures in accountability, transparency, and constitutional protections. That experience taught me how hard it is for ordinary citizens to get answers from systems built to avoid responsibility. It also pushed me to draft federal reforms aimed at closing those gaps. In Congress, I would bring persistence, independence, and root-cause analysis, not political theater. Families, farmers, seniors, veterans, and small businesses need someone who will ask tough questions, not another politician who defends the system.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes. Congress has a constitutional duty to provide rigorous oversight of the executive branch, no matter which party controls the White House. Oversight should never be treated as a partisan weapon used only when the other side is in power. It is a basic responsibility of representative government. Federal agencies spend taxpayer dollars, enforce regulations, and make decisions that affect families, businesses, farmers, veterans, and seniors across Wisconsin. Congress must demand transparency, investigate waste and abuse, and ensure the President and federal agencies stay within the law. When Congress fails to do that, power shifts away from the people and toward unelected bureaucracies. Accountability should apply to every administration, without exception.
candidates.cong_q5: One of my favorite Wisconsin history facts is that the Republican Party was founded in Ripon, Wisconsin, in 1854 by people who were frustrated with the political establishment of their time. Whether someone is Republican, Democrat, Independent, or politically homeless today, I think that history is a reminder that Wisconsin has always had people willing to challenge stale politics and demand something better.  Our state has a strong tradition of independence, reform, and civic courage. That spirit still matters. Voters do not have to accept a system that feels broken, unresponsive, or controlled by insiders. Wisconsin has helped change American politics before, and we can do it again.

candidates.name: Fred Clark
candidates.cong_q1: I’m the only Democrat in this race with the resources, the support, the experience and the ability to win back those rural voters that we need to win. My broad base of experience living and working in rural Wisconsin and my experience as an elected representative will ensure that I am ready to represent the people of northern Wisconsin in Congress on day pne.
candidates.cong_q2: A growing number of people cannot afford the basic costs of living and are falling farther and farther behind.  In the last 50 years the costs of housing, healthcare, childcare, transportation, and higher education have all risen much faster than wages. Northern Wisconsin families just can’t keep up. Families who earn more than the Federal Poverty Level or $32,500 but less than $100,000 - true working and middle class families - are falling behind because the traditional safety net doesn’t help them. We'll need a broad- based, multi-faceted approach to affordability that includes tax reform, ensuring access to affordable health care, financial support for families with children, college and tech school tuition support, affordable housing, and meaningful anti-trust regulation and enforcement. That's just the beginning!
candidates.cong_q3: As a forester and land manager I’ve spent years working outdoors in all seasons throughout Wisconsin. As a long time business owner and employer, organizational executive, and volunteer leader, I’ve led teams and helped people solve problems and perform at their best. As a rural legislator, I’ve worked hard to tackle challenges at home and support people from all walks of life, and politics. My broad base of experience living and working in rural Wisconsin and my experience as an elected representative will ensure that I am ready to represent the people of Northern Wisconsin in Congress on Day 1.
candidates.cong_q4: In 2025 the Trump Administration consistently violated the clear language of court orders, engaged in an unprecedented pattern of contempt of courts, verbally attacked judges, and fired agency Inspectors General and other officials who simply tried to do their job consistent with their oath to the Constitution. Trump officials used the power of government to threaten and silence voices of dissent, clear First Amendment violations. The Republican congressional majority has, time after time, refused the constitutional power to check abuses of power. In Congress I’ll use Congressional authority to investigate corruption, violations of law by this administration, pass legislation to further limit excessive presidential power, and reassert the role of Congress as a co-equal branch of government. We aren’t a monarchy — we’re a constitutional democracy.
candidates.cong_q5: Wisconsin is the number one producer of paper, cranberries, and ginseng in America, and Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District is home to businesses producing all three of those important products!

candidates.name: Kevin Hermening
candidates.cong_q1: I am asking for your vote because Congress needs people who are ready on day one. I have spent a lifetime serving our country and our communities — as a U.S. Marine, former Iranian hostage, small-business owner, financial advisor, educator, school board president, and community volunteer. I have created jobs, balanced budgets, met payrolls, and helped families plan for their futures. I understand the challenges facing northern and western Wisconsin because I have lived and worked here for 40 years. I will fight to secure our border, control spending, strengthen our economy, support our veterans, protect Social Security and Medicare, and defend our constitutional freedoms. I offer proven leadership, tested judgment, and real-world experience — not promises, but results.
candidates.cong_q2: The top issue facing Wisconsin’s 7th Congressional District is affordability. Families, seniors, farmers, and small-business owners are working hard, but inflation, housing shortages, healthcare costs, and energy prices continue to squeeze household budgets. I will address this by focusing on policies that grow the economy rather than grow government. We must reduce reckless federal spending, unleash American energy production, cut burdensome regulations, and support workforce and housing development in rural communities. I will fight to protect Social Security and Medicare for current retirees while strengthening their long-term future. I will also work to expand opportunities for good-paying jobs in manufacturing, agriculture, forestry, healthcare, and technology. Prosperity comes from opportunity, not dependence, and I will work every day to restore both.
candidates.cong_q3: I would bring a unique combination of military service, business leadership, financial expertise, and public service to Congress. As a U.S. Marine and former Iranian hostage, I understand national security, leadership under pressure, and the importance of American strength. As a financial advisor for nearly four decades, managing hundreds of millions of dollars for Wisconsin families and businesses, I understand budgets, economic growth, retirement security, and fiscal responsibility. As a school board member and president for sixteen years, I have experience solving problems, building consensus, and governing at the local level. These experiences will help me advocate effectively for Wisconsin’s Seventh District by promoting economic growth, supporting veterans, strengthening rural communities, improving workforce opportunities, and bringing practical solutions — not partisan rhetoric — to Washington.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes, Congress should exercise oversight over the President because the Constitution requires checks and balances. Oversight is not about partisan attacks; it is about accountability, transparency, and ensuring that laws are faithfully executed. Whether the President is a Republican or a Democrat, Congress has a duty to ask questions, review spending, and make sure taxpayer dollars are being used effectively. At the same time, oversight should be responsible and focused on results, not political theater. I support a strong president, but I also support a strong Congress that fulfills its constitutional responsibilities. The goal should be better government, protection of individual liberty, and greater confidence that Washington is working for the American people rather than for itself.
candidates.cong_q5: One of my favorite Wisconsin fun facts is that our state motto is simply, “Forward.” Adopted in 1851, it reflects the pioneering spirit, optimism, and determination that have defined Wisconsin for generations. I love it because it captures what I believe about both our state and our country. Wisconsinites are practical people who solve problems, work hard, help their neighbors, and keep moving forward no matter the obstacles. From our farmers and manufacturers to our veterans and small-business owners, we are a state built by people who don’t quit when times get tough. “Forward” is more than a motto — it is a reminder that progress comes through hard work, personal responsibility, and a commitment to leave things better than we found them.

candidates.name: Don Raihala
candidates.cong_q1: Voters should send me to Congress because I'm the only unifying choice to represent them. I am the only candidate to have gone door to door collecting over 1,100 signatures from both Republicans and Democrats. These people decided that they can trust someone that's willing to make that effort to represent their voices in congress. We're not going to agree on some issues, but I have promised that if elected I will visit each county at least five times, and provide daily updates on what is occurring in Washington, D.C., in an interesting and somewhat entertaining way. My desire is to keep people factually informed, engaged and interested in how the federal government is trying to make this country better for all Americans.
candidates.cong_q2: I don't think there's just one federal issue on people's mind. What people talked about, as I was gathering my 1,100 nomination signatures, were issues regarding Immigration/ICE, high gas prices and the Epstein files. While many large components of these particular issues are out of control of congress, what was interesting was the overwhelming majority that I came across were in support of illegal immigration deportations to continue and the complete release of the Epstein files. If I'm elected to Congress, I will not ignore their unified viewpoints. Especially the complete release of the Epstein files as literally everyone, both Republicans and Democrats, want this to happen.
candidates.cong_q3: As a degreed accountant with a work experience in accounting, purchasing, and project management, I possess a keen eye for details and accuracy on were the money is flowing which will be very useful in this era of massive uncovered fraud being exposed almost daily. I also have built over 20 houses as a construction contractor and am currently planning a friend's build this summer. I will be doing several videos in regards to the 'housing crisis' on my Facebook page doing a deep dive in comparing this current home with the one I built during COVID. I believe the facts will be revealing and hopefully if I win I can land on a congressional committee that's willing to do something about the housing crisis.
candidates.cong_q4: No. Congress already has the funding authority to limit the president's actions and agenda. If congress had power to micro-manage the executive branch, then nothing would get done especially if there were opposing political ideologies and majorities.
candidates.cong_q5: At the turn of the 20th century, Superior Wisconsin had the highest bar/tavern to citizen ratio in the country of 100 citizens to each licensed bar. This was largely due to the maritime ship building industry and its direct access to Lake Superior. Some say it exceeded a ratio of 50-to-1 if you were to include the illegal and hidden speakeasies and houses of prostitution. Definitely something not to be proud of, but it is history.
