candidates.name: Ginger Murray
candidates.cong_q1: To benefit from 30 years as an award-winning, results driven lawyer/court official (90% settlement rate), to advocate for Districvt 7 in D.C. To get results that: Defend our Democracy and prioritize improving lives of "we, the people" not corporations and billionaires. To obtain laws that: fairly tax all earnings, scrap the cap, cut tax breaks for billionaires, require congress to pay promised funds in lieu of taxes (PILT) to avoid referendums for public school funding, provide quality affordable healthcare choices (Obamacare or better), require due process when defending boarders and reform the process and timelines for naturalization of qualified applicants, and DEMAND PERSONAL ACCOUNTABILITY for everyone who violated children and women (secret slush fund settlements for congressional sexual misconduct and Epstein co-conspirators).
candidates.cong_q2: Living the American Dream: when wages for an honest day's work allows families to afford a home, food, and healthcare in a community they love, with at least a week of paid vacation!  This will require passing laws that provide competitive wages, affordable quality healthcare and housing, fully funded schools in a safe & healthy environment. These results can be obtained by cutting breaks for billionaires, funding needed programs, reviving the intended impact of the Clean Air Act and re-authorizing the EPA, holding Congress accountable for promises made (PILT/treaty rights), taxing equitably, and stopping corruption/fraud.
candidates.cong_q3: A 30-year legal career as counsel and court official, with unequivocal commitment to community & family serve as a solid foundation for advocating for the folks in this District.  Invaluable experience to obtain results in DC: 1) successful advocating/issuing decisions in the best interest of children and families, and protecting abuse victims; 2) representing government entities while bringing in new funding and businesses; 3) excelling in environmental law; 4) serving as a stakeholder when creating the current Wisconsin Indian Child Welfare Act; 5) volunteering on Mid-State Independent Living Consultants board; 6) founder/small business owner; 7) win multistate class action labor union cases; 8) coach/ educate high school students; 9) utilize restorative justice, and 10) 26 year marriage with two amazing adult children.
candidates.cong_q4: ABSOLUTELY: Celebrating the 250th birthday of our independence provides the perfect lens to reflect on our Declaration of Independence and Constitution. Our founders left a country run by a king to find freedom and to provide power to the people.  The pillars of our democracy (and our White House) are being demolished by this right wing regime lead by POTUS as he gives orders and makes decisions that fly in the face of our Constitution (Due Process, war powers, power of the purse, etc.); our 1st Amendment (Freedom of Assembly, Press and Speech); 4th Amendment Freedom from Unreasonable Search & Seizures, and the next infraction in the next headline. Our democracy demands that the power be returned to the people, not to a dictator.
candidates.cong_q5: The Green Bay Packers are the only NFL team owned by fans through a community-based nonprofit structure!

candidates.name: Chris Armstrong
candidates.cong_q1: In February 2025, amidst the flurry of illegal and unconstitutional actions of the Trump administration, I went down the busiest intersection in New Richmond and started protesting by myself. After years of putting up lawn signs and voting, I decided I needed to do more. In March 2025, I got involved with the Democratic Party to get out the vote for the spring election. Then I decided to host a “Hands Off!” protest in New Richmond and over 250 people attended! And after that founded New Richmond Indivisible with other local organizers. In April 2025, I started my campaign to take that fight to Congress. There is nothing we can’t do when we work together to demand change. 2026 is the year of the people!
candidates.cong_q2: Congress must stop the lawlessness and corruption of the Trump administration. Whether it’s the illegal war in Iran, tearing down the East Wing of the White House, building the nonsensical ballroom, the insane tariffs, the assault on science, our environment and National Parks, the Epstein coverup, this government is doing everything it can to make life worse for everyone except the ultra-rich and well-connected. We need to tax the ultra-wealthy, implement Medicare for All, provide family leave and childcare, protect our environment, invest in our children’s education, abolish ICE, help our veterans, house the homeless, feed the hungry, invest in renewable energy, and adopt sensible international trade and ag policies.
candidates.cong_q3: I’m just a normal guy who grew up here, raised my family, and started my own IT business. I’m running for Congress because as my grandson gets older, I want to be able to look him in the eye and tell him I did everything in my power to make this a better place for him, so he can find a good job, find a place to live, and raise his family here. My job as an Enterprise Architect is to bring together disparate groups of stakeholders, work to a common understanding of the problem, and then collaborate to come up with the optimal solution that best meets the needs of everyone, in the face of overwhelming complexity and a continually changing landscape.
candidates.cong_q4: The first thing I’m going to do when I’m seated in the House of Representatives in 2027 is work with my fellow members and introduce Articles of Impeachment against Donald Trump and his cabinet. I’m not doing this because I don’t like Trump (which I don’t) and I’m not doing this because I don’t agree with the administration’s policies (which I don’t); I’m doing this because this administration breaks the law every single day and nobody is doing anything about it. What’s the point of passing any new legislation when this administration breaks the law, flouts the Constitution, and ignores the will of the people every single day? We are a nation of laws, not men.
candidates.cong_q5: Oh my, there are so many to choose from! Perhaps that Wisconsin started the first kindergarten in the U.S. Or the first state to implement an unemployment compensation program. Or that we’re the Badger State not because of the animal, but because of the miners that dug holes in the ground in the early history of our state. Or that Wisconsin had the largest concentration of effigy mounds of any place in the world. When I work with people across the world, I can’t help but share the storied history of the world’s best football team — the Green Bay Packers! The only community-owned professional sports team in the U.S. and the only NFL team to win three championships back-to-back twice! Go Pack Go!

candidates.name: Niina Baum
candidates.occupation: Founder and owner of Valo Media (digital marketing agency)
candidates.cong_q1: I am the only candidate who has spent nearly my entire life in the 7th District. I grew up on a small dairy farm in Price County, co-founded Northwoods Young Professionals to keep young people here, built a small business, served on my town's planning commission, represented Team USA as a dog musher (earning silver & bronze medals), and organized events that brought $500,000 in economic impact to the Northwoods. I have accepted no corporate PAC money, spent under $20,000, and was still the first candidate in this district to secure ballot access. My opponents have taken millions. That contrast tells you everything about who we will each answer to in Washington. I will read the bills, seek testimony from constituents, and make decisions grounded in evidence and the needs of this district rather than party pressure or donor priorities. If we want Congress to work differently, we need to change the type of people we elect to office. Vote for one of us!
candidates.cong_q2: Rural economic decline. WI's 7th-CD is losing small farms, healthcare providers, young people, and small businesses. These challenges are connected and getting more complex. AI data centers are coming to Wisconsin with promises of economic growth while driving up energy costs and receiving $1.5 billion in state sales tax exemptions with no federal standards attached. Social Security trust fund insolvency is projected by 2032; a 23% automatic benefit cut would be catastrophic for rural communities where seniors on fixed incomes make up a significant share of the local economy. I would address this by supporting policy for small farms, protecting Social Security benefits, investing in rural healthcare, removing unnecessary regulatory barriers to building houses, and establishing federal accountability standards for data centers.
candidates.cong_q3: I’m a small business owner and economic development professional who grew up on a dairy farm and spent my career in rural communities. Beyond that background, I bring specific expertise that directly applies to challenges facing this district. My B.S. in business administration from Northland College and master's in information and communication technologies from UW-Stout give me a foundation to critically evaluate the AI and data center policies reshaping our energy grid and rural landscape. I taught as an adjunct professor at a local technical college, giving me firsthand understanding of workforce development and the education to employment pipeline. I serve on my township's planning commission where I work directly on zoning, land use, and development decisions, the exact issues driving our housing shortage.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes, and this isn’t a partisan position. Former Republican Speaker Paul Ryan said it plainly at Harvard this spring: Congress has steadily ceded its authority to the executive branch, and that erosion predates this administration. Both parties are responsible. Conservatives by definition should believe in constitutional limits on executive power. The power to declare war, the power of the purse, oversight of federal agencies, these are legislative functions, not executive ones. A Congress that defers to a president simply because he or she is from the same party is abandoning its constitutional role. Ryan sued both the Obama and Trump administrations as Speaker to protect legislative authority. That’s the standard. I’ll hold myself to the same one regardless of who is in the White House.
candidates.cong_q5: The Republican Party was founded on March 20, 1854 in a one-room schoolhouse in Ripon, Wisconsin. A group of everyday citizens gathered there fed up with wealthy special interests controlling politics and government. Their slogan was "Free soil, free labor, free speech, free people." They believed if you worked hard, opportunity should be there for you. That government should work for everybody, not for the powerful few. That is still the right idea. And it was born right here in Wisconsin. I think about that a lot as I travel this district asking for your vote.

candidates.name: Mark Christopher Scheffler
candidates.cong_q1: People ask me why I’m running for Congress. The answer is actually pretty simple: I believe in sustainability. Not just environmental sustainability, but preserving and strengthening the things we care about like our economy and our democracy while fixing and rebuilding the things that just aren’t working anymore. My old home is a good example. You don’t tear down something meaningful just because it needs work. You restore it. You strengthen the foundation. You modernize what needs modernizing. And you preserve what makes it worth loving in the first place. I believe America deserves that same kind of care.
candidates.cong_q2: A sustainable society depends on trust. Trust in our institutions. Trust in each other. Trust that government exists to serve people — not special interests. Congress just isn’t working for the US anymore. Americans are exhausted by division, outrage, and corruption. I hear it across the spectrum. Our politics must change. We deserve better than politicians spending all day trying to get reelected or making soundbites instead of solving problems. That’s why I’m running as a Democrat but I’ll serve as an independent voice in Washington. Voters want representatives who are less partisan and not poisonous; they want folks who build bridges, not burn them down. I want to show America we can do better, we must do better, and that starts right here, right now.
candidates.cong_q3: I believe we need real leadership to create what I call a prosperity economy — one that rewards productivity, innovation, and hard work, while making life more affordable again for everyday Americans. I'm ready to lead, and I believe sustainability starts with a solid economic foundation. I just think the economy should work for the people who actually keep this country running: Workers, families, farmers, small and mid-sized businesses. But our economy - the real economy is at the breaking point. Right now, too many Americans feel like they’re working harder every year just to fall further and further behind. The cost of living crisis is real, and our national debt is out of control. That isn’t sustainable.
candidates.cong_q4: I believe the House of Representatives is the FIRST branch of government, and that the President's role, while representing a co-equal branch, should be limited to administering the laws that Congress passes and nothing more. That means ending the power to pardon political allies, the power to rewrite spending bills or impound appropriations and the power to unilaterally wage war. And I’m not running for Congress to become part of the political machine. I’m running because I believe we can build something better. More sustainable. More honest. More connected to one another. A Congress that works again — not just for some of us, but for all of us.
candidates.cong_q5: In 1991, Wisconsin experienced one of its strangest disasters when a fire broke out in a massive cold-storage warehouse in Madison containing millions of pounds of government-owned butter, cheese, and other food products. The blaze burned for days, melting huge quantities of butter and cheese into literal rivers that flowed from the building. Because butter is fat and highly combustible, it actually fueled the fire, making it even harder to control. Firefighters found themselves battling flames while wading through melted dairy products, and environmental crews had to contain the runoff to prevent damage to nearby waterways. The incident became known as the Great Wisconsin Butter Fire and remains one of the most unusual and memorable industrial fires in state history.

candidates.name: Katrina deVille
candidates.cong_q1: I'm not part of the establishment or a coward. I don't care about money, title, or credit. I can't stand by and do nothing while this country continues to be destroyed, citizens disregarded, and our Constitution burns. I believe in America and will fight for all of us with my life, because tyrannical authoritarianism has come to destroy us. None of my opponents are going to bring this level of ferociousness to this moment; a ferocity which is desperately needed. I fight for America, her citizens, and our Constitution; so we may all have happier, healthier lives, and live free of tyranny and oppression. So help me God.
candidates.cong_q2: I'd say the top issue is affordability, but healthcare is most likely a tie. Healthcare is definitely part of why people are genuinely struggling with affordability, so addressing that concern specifically will help fix some of the affordability crisis. I would address healthcare by working to finally get Americans Medicare for all. I'd also be pushing for $22 minimum wage, universal childcare, ending this illegal war with Israel and Iran, tossing out the One Big Beautiful Bill and rewriting the tax structure to tax the rich and give tax breaks to middle class Americans.
candidates.cong_q3: Conventionally, I'm a small business owner and musician; both of these endeavors have granted me invaluable skills very relevant to the office I seek.  I'm accustomed to balancing budgets, project management, task delegation, marketing, scheduling, planning and project creation from being a business owner.  As a musician, I've learned to think outside the box, improvise, marketing, and how to genuinely connect with people and keep them engaged. Unconventionally, I'm a transgender woman in a time of widespread discrimination against us, so I understand what oppression feels like, while also being able to see things from both male and female perspectives.  I'm also a first time politician, so I'm not committed to the establishment and party protocols, but solely for the people, by the people.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes, absolutely. They've been abandoning the Constitution, failing to do their job of keeping the president in check.  Congress has made themselves virtually irrelevant, capitulating their powers to Trump and it has served to weaponize law against Americans, enable the hateful brown shirt tactics of the ICE Gestapo, allow for rampant out in the open government corruption, and the starting of unconstitutional wars.  Every sitting member of Congress which has allowed this to continue needs to be voted out and removed from government.
candidates.cong_q5: Wisconsin was the first state to ratify the 19th Amendment, which when ratified gave women the right to vote.

candidates.name: Tony Wied
candidates.cong_q1: Since my first day in oﬃce, I have fought for the people of northeast Wisconsin and delivered results for our communities. This past year, I secured millions in federal funding for priorities including water treatment resources in Kaukauna and Suamico, improvements to Austin Straubel Airport, and a new Green Bay Metro Fire Department station. I have also worked to put more money back into the pockets of hardworking Wisconsin families. I was proud to vote in favor of the Working Families Tax Cuts, which prevented the largest tax increase in American history and included provisions such as no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, the largest tax deductions for seniors in history, and an increased child tax credit.
candidates.cong_q2: Aﬀordability remains a major challenge for families throughout our district. Under the Biden Administration, families faced decade-high inflation (9.1%), sky-high mortgage rates (8%), and a loss of almost $3,000 in annual purchasing power. When I got to Washington, I, alongside my Republican colleagues, acted quickly to reverse this damage and bring down costs for Wisconsinites by working to pass the One Big Beautiful Bill and deliver the Working Families Tax Cuts. As a result of this work, inflation has dropped, mortgage rates have eased, and real wages are now outpacing inflation. However, the job is not done. We need to retain control of the House to extend our pro-family policies and continue this progress.
candidates.cong_q3: I am not a career politician. After spending over two decades as a small business owner, I know how to solve problems and get things done. Since being elected, I now sit on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, the Agriculture Committee, and the Small Business Committee. From these positions, I have worked to improve our roads and infrastructure, protect Wisconsin farmers, and constantly support our small businesses, including by introducing important legislation like the Dump Red Tape Act that is working its way through the Senate right now. This experience will allow me to continue to fight for the great people of Wisconsin’s 8th District.
candidates.cong_q4: One of the great things about Congress is that Article I of the Constitution gives us power of the purse and investigate powers. These are key tenants of our system of checks and balances that make our great American system work so well. When oversight is needed, I think it must be targeted and eﬃcient with a focus on delivering results for the American people, not political theater, witch hunts, or partisan madness.
candidates.cong_q5: I’ve gotta go with Seymour being the home of the hamburger. It’s pretty great to know that it all originates at the Outagamie County Fair, right here in northeast Wisconsin.

candidates.name: Rick Crosson
candidates.occupation: Retired transportation/logistics executive; retired U.S. Army Lt. Col.
candidates.cong_q1: I have spent my life solving hard problems and bringing people together to do it. Twenty years in the Army taught me how to lead under pressure, build coalitions at all levels, including nationally and internationally, and get results when the stakes are real. I carried that into running large operations in business. But the part I am proudest of is simpler: I make a point of knowing people, finding common ground, and listening before I talk. That is what is missing in Washington right now. I am not running to score points. I am running to represent every corner of this district, because I believe we get further working together.
candidates.cong_q2: The top issue is the cost of living. Families here are getting squeezed from every direction with high costs of groceries, gas and diesel, housing, health insurance, and a farm economy thrown into chaos by tariffs and bad policy. People are working hard and still falling behind. Here is what I would do. Push to lower everyday costs by going after the price-gouging and consolidation driving them up. Protect the farm economy from trade decisions made without rural Wisconsin in mind. Support funding for the health coverage families and rural hospitals depend on, while pushing for universal healthcare. And bring the same problem-solving I used in logistics: find where the system is broken, fix the choke point, and measure whether it actually helped people.
candidates.cong_q3: I solve problems for a living. In the Army and in business, my job was to take something complicated and broken and make it work, on time and on budget, with real consequences if I got it wrong. I have negotiated across borders, run large organizations, and managed budgets where every dollar was accountable to someone. This helps the district because most of what is failing people right now is fixable: supply chains, costs, access to care, a VA that buries veterans in paperwork, common sense policy choices. I see those as logistics problems, and logistics is what I do. I will not just give speeches about them. I will work the problem until it is solved.
candidates.cong_q4: Yes. The Constitution built three branches to keep each other in check, and Congress has been handing its power away for years. That is not how this is supposed to work. Congress holds the authority over the budget and the power to declare war, and I will never vote to give those away. Right now presidential overreach is hitting levels we have not seen, and it is on Congress and the courts to do their jobs and rein it in. Oversight is not partisan. It is the job. I would take that job seriously.
candidates.cong_q5: The name “Badger” is actually originally attributed to thousands of lead miners who lived in horizontal dugout burrows during harsh winters in the 1820s and 1830s.

candidates.name: Barbara Bittner
candidates.leg_q1: Voters should elect me because I bring real-world experience, not a political career. I grew up on a Wisconsin dairy farm, have owned and operated businesses, created jobs, and understand the challenges facing farmers, small businesses, and working families. I will fight to lower taxes, protect constitutional freedoms, support law enforcement, defend parents' rights, and keep our communities safe. I'll listen, work hard, and make decisions based on common sense and what's best for the people of Senate District 1 — not special interests. I'm running to be your voice in Madison and to help ensure Wisconsin remains a place where families, businesses, and future generations can thrive.
candidates.leg_q2: The top issue facing Senate District 1 is affordability. Families, seniors, farmers, and small businesses are all feeling the pressure of rising property taxes, increasing utility and insurance costs, and the high price of everyday necessities. We need to make Wisconsin more affordable by providing meaningful tax relief, reducing unnecessary regulations that drive up costs, supporting family farms and small businesses, and creating an environment where good-paying jobs can grow. My goal is to help ensure that people can afford to live, work, raise a family, and retire right here in northeast Wisconsin.
candidates.leg_q3: Government should operate more like a well-run business. It should live within its means, balance budgets, eliminate wasteful spending, and focus on delivering results for the people it serves. Every tax dollar should be treated with respect and spent wisely. We should measure success by whether government policies improve the quality of life for our constituents, strengthen our economy, and create opportunities for families, farmers, seniors, and small businesses to succeed. Government exists to serve the people — not the other way around —and it should be accountable, efficient, and focused on solving problems with common sense.
candidates.leg_q4: One of my favorite Wisconsin history facts is that our state is the birthplace of the Republican Party. In 1854, citizens gathered in the Little White Schoolhouse in Ripon to stand against the expansion of slavery and affirm the principle that every person is entitled to the fruits of their own labor and the blessings of freedom. I think it's inspiring that such an important moment in American history began right here in Wisconsin. It reminds us that ordinary citizens, working together with courage and conviction, can make an extraordinary difference.

candidates.name: Jacob VandenPlas
candidates.leg_q1: I’m running for Wisconsin’s 1st Senate District because I believe public service is about putting people before politics. As a combat veteran, Wisconsin National Guard member, farmer, and small business owner, I’ve spent my life serving others and solving real problems. My experiences gave me a firsthand understanding of challenges facing veterans, families, farmers, and small communities across northeastern Wisconsin. I’m committed to bringing accountability, practical leadership, and common sense solutions to Madison. I believe government should work for the people, not special interests. If elected, I’ll fight to protect our values, strengthen our communities, and ensure voices of local residents are heard. I’m asking for your vote because I’m ready to serve Wisconsin with the same dedication and commitment guiding my life and career.
candidates.leg_q2: The top issue in the 1st Senate District is strengthening our local economy and ensuring families, farmers, and small businesses can succeed. Rising costs, workforce shortages, and increasing burdens on agriculture are making it harder for people to get ahead. I will focus on policies that promote economic growth, support family farms, reduce unnecessary regulations, and expand workforce development opportunities. We need to create an environment where businesses can grow, young people can build careers here at home, and communities can thrive. As a veteran, farmer, and nonprofit leader, I will bring practical, results-driven leadership to Madison and work to ensure state government serves the people of northeastern Wisconsin — not special interests.to your constituents.
candidates.leg_q3: Simple. Listen to our constituents.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin's Iron Brigade was one of the most famous fighting units of the Civil War. Made up largely of Wisconsin soldiers, the Iron Brigade earned a reputation for toughness and suffered some of the highest casualty rates of any Union brigade. Wisconsin's Iron Brigade was so fierce during the Civil War that Confederate soldiers called them "those damned Black Hats" — and history still remembers them as one of the Union Army's most elite fighting forces.

candidates.name: Katie Baney
candidates.occupation: Managing director of government and regulatory affairs, Delta Defense LLC
candidates.leg_q1: I'm a conservative, Christian, wife, and the only mother in this race. I've spent my career championing our constitutional freedoms in both the public and private sector. I understand how the political game is played, how businesses are run and ultimately how all of these decisions impact our families and communities. Send me to Madison and I'll fight for medical freedom, cut red tape strangling small businesses and farms, and demand accountability for taxpayer dollars.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordability is the primary concern I hear from folks when I'm out in the district. Wisconsinites are concerned about rising property taxes, increased health care costs, and high utility bills. I'll fight to freeze property taxes so families can stay in their homes and seniors aren't taxed out of theirs. I'll work to bring energy costs down through an all-of-the-above approach that embraces reliable, affordable power like nuclear and protects ratepayers. I'll take on the red tape and overregulation that quietly drive up the cost of everything, from housing to health care. Government can't control every price, but it can stop contributing to making life more expensive for Wisconsinites.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government has grown bigger, spent more, and added rules. That has to change. Government should do less, but do it well, and trust the people of Wisconsin to keep more of what they earn. I'll measure success not by how many bills I pass, but by how much red tape I repeal. We should sunset outdated regulations, demand accountability for every taxpayer dollar, and return surpluses to families instead of growing government with them. We should respect the constitutional balance between the branches, so unelected agencies can't write costly rules without oversight. This means less duplication, more accountability, and a government that remembers it works for the people of Wisconsin.
candidates.leg_q4: The ice cream sundae was originally invented in Two Rivers, Wisconsin in 1881!

candidates.name: Nic Cravillion
candidates.occupation: District director, Office of state Sen. Andre Jacque; Wisconsin Army National Guard; small business owner
candidates.leg_q1: I'm running for state Senate because I believe northeast Wisconsin deserves a strong conservative voice that understands our communities and the challenges they face. As an Army combat veteran, small business owner, husband, father, and public servant, I've spent my life serving my country and community. For the past 5.5 years, I’ve proudly served as Sen. André Jacque's district director, working directly with residents across northeast Wisconsin to solve problems, cut through government red tape, and help deliver results. Through that work, I’ve built relationships, listened to constituents, and gained a firsthand understanding of the issues facing our communities. In many ways, I have already been doing the work of serving northeast Wisconsin every day. I’m running to continue that work in Madison.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordability. Rising property taxes, housing shortages, increasing utility costs, and growing pressure on local governments are making it harder for families to put down roots and get ahead. To address this, we must reduce the tax burden on working families by reining in Gov. Evers' wasteful government spending and delivering meaningful property tax relief. We also need to reform how local governments are funded so rural communities can maintain roads, bridges, and emergency services without continually raising property taxes. Expanding workforce housing by reducing barriers to development, supporting affordable energy, and investing in local infrastructure will help lower costs and strengthen our communities. Our goal should be simple: make it easier to afford a home, raise a family, and build a future in northeast Wisconsin.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should focus on doing the basics well, operating within its means, and being accountable to the people it serves. Too often, government takes a one-size-fits-all approach that overlooks the unique challenges facing rural communities. The needs of northeast Wisconsin are not always the same as those of Milwaukee or Madison, and local leaders are often in the best position to understand and solve local problems. Government works best when it is transparent, fiscally responsible, and focused on delivering results. That means controlling spending, reducing the tax burden on working families, and giving local communities the flexibility and resources they need to succeed. Wisconsin families deserve a government that listens, responds, and respects their hard-earned tax dollars.
candidates.leg_q4: One of my favorite, although not fun, Wisconsin history facts is the story of the Peshtigo Fire, the deadliest wildfire in American history. In 1871, the fire devastated communities across northeast Wisconsin and claimed more lives than the Great Chicago Fire. Yet because both disasters occurred on the same day, the tragedy in Peshtigo is often overlooked in history books. The story is especially meaningful to me because the grounds of the Shrine of Our Lady of Champion and my family's homestead just down the road from it were both spared from the fire. Knowing that my family has lived in this area since those early days gives me a personal connection to a remarkable chapter of Wisconsin history.

candidates.name: Mark Becker
candidates.occupation: Owner, Specialty Auto Sales (Suamico) and Appleton Motorcars (Appleton)
candidates.leg_q1: As the former chair of the Brown County Republican Party, I have witnessed, firsthand, how extreme politics have warped the fabric of our state politics, for the worse. As a small business owner, I know the pressures facing our state’s industries and workforce. And as a devoted husband and father, I believe that we must do everything in our power to support the hardworking families of this state. As state Senator, I will fight on behalf of my constituents, not any one party or special interest – that’s why I’m running as an Independent. I will fight against the special interests that prioritize profits over everything else, and I’ll make sure Madison prioritizes people over politics.
candidates.leg_q2: Bringing down costs for working families is my top priority. Whether it’s rising property taxes, health insurance premiums, grocery bills, or the price of a tank of gas, people are being squeezed in every conceivable way. And anyone who tells you that our state government is helpless to bring down costs for working families is just wrong. This year’s statewide property tax hike is a direct result of failed negotiations and poor decisions made in Madison. Too many legislators believe that we can either choose to support schools or provide property tax relief. The truth is, we can do both. By investing in our schools, we can lower property taxes, end the never-ending cycle of referendums, and support our kids, all at the same time.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin voters are desperate for change. When knocking on doors in the district, I have heard time and time again that today’s politics isn’t working for people, especially for the hardworking people of northeastern Wisconsin. For far too long, our elected officials have demonstrated that their loyalties lie with partisan donors and special interests, and not the people that they have sworn an oath to serve. We cannot keep electing the same type of politicians and expecting different results. In November, the people of Wisconsin’s 1st Senate District have a choice to make. They can send another partisan to Madison, or they can elect an independent, people-focused champion, who will fight for them and them alone.
candidates.leg_q4: I’m an avid motorsports fan, so I take pride in the fact that Wisconsin is home to over 35 active race tracks — including the Milwaukee Mile, the oldest continuously operated speedway in the entire world. Senate District 1 is home to four racetracks that host racing events every single week, which (I believe) is the most of any Senate district in the state. I’ve raced on three of four of these tracks, myself, and am hoping to visit all four on the campaign trail!

candidates.name: Tim Carpenter
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Senate (2003-present); Wisconsin State Assembly (1985-2003)
candidates.leg_q1: I have a proved track record of serving my constituents by sending surveys, holding frequent town hall meetings, E-Updates and keeping in touch with voters. I’m proud of not have missed a Senate Roll Call vote since February 2011, when Gov. Walker signed Act 10 repealing collective bargaining rights in Wisconsin.
candidates.leg_q2: Improving the quality of life for my constituents and holding government accountable. Many people believe Wisconsin has taken a step backwards under many years of Republican control of the State Legislature.
candidates.leg_q3: After the November 3rd election I believe voters will see a major change in how the state Senate operates and what issues will finally  receive proper attention. For too long many important issues weren’t even a given public hearing or debate in committee.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin once led the country with the Progressive Movement improving our quality life.

candidates.name: Robyn Vining
candidates.occupation: Legislator; professional photographer; small business owner
candidates.leg_q1: People matter and are worth fighting for. I’ve spent eight years in Madison fighting for constituents, and rejecting special interests. Life is unaffordable for Wisconsinites. It's far too difficult to get by. As a small business owner for almost two decades, I understand small businesses’ needs. I understand when life is tough, when family jobs are lost and the struggle to afford childcare, transportation, food and housing. There are numerous people running for office to climb a ladder--not me. I work hard, show up for constituents, and always remember who sent me to Madison, who I work for — the people. Voting is an act of trust, and I respect the trust you place in me when you vote. I’ll never take that for granted.
candidates.leg_q2: Access to quality, affordable healthcare, housing and childcare; the desperate need for adequate public school funding. Property taxes have skyrocketed due to Republican lawmakers failing to properly fund the schools, and these skyrocketing property taxes have driven up already unaffordable housing costs — which has hurt every generation's need for affordable housing.
candidates.leg_q3: We deserve a Wisconsin that works for everyone, and Wisconsin with affordable healthcare — including mental healthcare, housing and childcare; communities safe from gun violence; strong public schools, universities and the trades; safe, secure, free and fair elections; state leadership engaging with the urgent needs related to climate change; an accessible world for everyBODY; and the kind of economic security and freedom that allows for all Wisconsinites to chase the American Dream.
candidates.leg_q4: The first kindergarten in the United States was founded in Wisconsin!

candidates.name: Chris J. Larson
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Senate (2011-present); Milwaukee County Board (2008-2010)
candidates.leg_q1: Inequality is growing, public education has been defunded, the planet is warming, and too many of my neighbors feel like the social contract doesn't apply to them. I have worked to ensure their voices are heard these past 15 years by fighting back against wealthy interests, WeEnergies, and short-term thinking. With a forthcoming majority, we can finally enact forward-thinking, long-term solutions that unrig the system.
candidates.leg_q2: People really don't want to see data centers expand in Wisconsin. They don't like the wasted water, continues heating, the increased energy costs, the reliance on fossil fuel infrastructure, the tax breaks for big tech, or the use of AI for mass surveillance, reduction in jobs, and a lack of a safety net for when they are phased out.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin should be responsive to the people, not to the special interests that have a profit motive to get their bills passed. We should be more transparent and responsive to public needs.
candidates.leg_q4: The first practical typewriter was invented in Wisconsin.

candidates.name: Mike Moeller
candidates.leg_q1: Because I live here. I shop here. I worship here. I raised my family here. I am not passing through state Senate District 7 on my way to something bigger this community is my something bigger. For years, our district has had passionate representation. But passion without results leaves families with higher tax bills, struggling schools, and neighborhoods still waiting. I am a small business owner who understands budgets, a neighbor who understands people, and a conservative who believes government should work for you, not around you. I will be fair in every decision, kind in every interaction, just in every vote, and always empathetic to the real lives behind every policy. That is my promise. Not a slogan.
candidates.leg_q2: Property taxes. Full stop. Families across Oak Creek, South Milwaukee, Cudahy, St. Francis and Milwaukee have watched their bills spike 20% or more in a single year.  Seniors on fixed incomes are being priced out of homes they spent decades building. Working parents are choosing between staying in their neighborhood and staying afloat. I will fight to reform the 400-year veto that locked in perpetual property tax increases, oppose unfunded state mandates that shift the burden onto local homeowners, and introduce a property tax freeze for seniors on fixed incomes. Good schools and safe neighborhoods matter deeply to me. But we should fund them through smarter state solutions, not by making it impossible for working families to keep their homes.
candidates.leg_q3: It should start by listening before legislating. For too long, Wisconsin government has operated as two teams competing for wins rather than neighbors solving shared problems.  That produces gridlock, frustrated communities, and families who stop believing government is capable of helping them at all. I believe in bipartisan deal-making, not because I lack convictions, but because I have enough respect for my neighbors across the aisle to find common ground wherever it exists. Property tax relief, workforce-ready education, and community safety are not Republican issues or Democratic issues. They are Wisconsin issues. Government should be transparent, accessible, and ruthlessly focused on results. Every dollar spent, every vote cast, every bill introduced should answer one question:  does this make District 7 families' lives better?
candidates.leg_q4: Although frozen custard was invented in Coney Island, New York, Milwaukee, Wisconsin is universally recognized as the "Frozen Custard Capital of the World."  The city boasts the highest concentration of frozen custard shops per capita globally, heavily supported by the State's rich dairy tradition. I love this because it reflects the Wisconsin spirit: practical, creative, community-centered, and deeply good-natured. We work with what we have, we serve our neighbors well, and somehow, we end up making something wonderful. That is the spirit I will bring to Madison — practical, neighborly, and always a little sweet.

candidates.name: Christian Ellis
candidates.occupation: Small business owner, managing partner, Packstaff
candidates.leg_q1: I bring proven experience working with people I don’t always agree with. From the Marine Corps to the county board, I’ve been part of environments where people come from different backgrounds and viewpoints. We still found ways to come together and get things done for the community. I understand what it means to be part of a team, and I know we all have to live with the results of the decisions we make. That’s why I approach this work with a focus on practical solutions, listening first, and being accountable for the outcome. As a state senator, I’ll bring that same approach to Madison and work just as hard for the people here.
candidates.leg_q2: What I hear consistently from people is the pressure of rising costs and the feeling that decisions are being made without real local input. At the same time, we see infrastructure needs, public services under strain, and local communities being asked to shoulder more of the burden when the state doesn’t function as it should. We need to refocus on the basics. That means investing in infrastructure and services people rely on, supporting local control, and making decisions based on what actually works for the communities affected. At the state level, I’ll stay focused on outcomes and work to make sure our communities aren’t left carrying the cost of inaction or gridlock.
candidates.leg_q3: Too often, decisions are made based on positioning rather than what actually works for people. I believe in a more practical, locally grounded approach that starts with listening, works across differences, and stays focused on solving problems. That also means being transparent about decisions, explaining the tradeoffs, and staying accessible to the people being represented. We don’t need more politics. We need steady leadership focused on delivering results, being honest about how decisions are made, and making sure those decisions reflect the needs and voices of the people.
candidates.leg_q4: One of my favorite Wisconsin history facts is that a piece of Sputnik IV actually fell in Manitowoc in 1962. A chunk of a Soviet satellite landed right in the middle of the street. It’s one of those stories that reminds you how even a small community can end up connected to something much bigger. It’s also a good reminder of how local history shapes identity. Whether it’s something unusual like that, or something foundational like Wisconsin being home to the first kindergarten, those moments reflect how communities think, learn, and grow over time.

candidates.name: Steven J. Doelder
candidates.leg_q1: My motto has always been to make sure things work and getting things done for everyone. It doesn’t matter if am in the garden, the classroom, or the board room. I’m ready to problem solve and to use my skills to fix anything that needs fixing. The mission of good governance and representation is possible. I believe we need to prohibit dark money from influencing and buying our politicians.
candidates.leg_q2: Wisconsin needs to fund its public schools and universities properly. When I went to college in the late sixties the state funded over 60% of the cost of my tuition … my cost was $110 per semester.  That support has dropped to 19%. That has to change. We also need to adequately fund our K-12 public schools. No more taxpayer money to private schools. We need to stop funding our public schools using property taxes. It isn’t good to pit public schools against property owners. Every Wisconsin student should have the same opportunities!
candidates.leg_q3: Rank choice voting would definitely help reform our Wisconsin political system. It would increase voter participation and help restore faith in our ability to solve problems by the government. We should also explore using something like the  Montana Plan to reduce the influence of dark money on our political system.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin has always been a leader in reforming our political system and moving the political system towards helping the working class. We were the first state to directly elect our U.S senators. We were the first state to pass workers compensation.  The first state to prohibit DDT. We were the first state to have kindergarten classes. We need to continue to be first in helping to improve the lives of our working class.

candidates.name: Sandy Wiedmeyer
candidates.leg_q1: I'm not a career politician. I'm a community builder with a record of real results. As Kenosha County GOP chair, I helped deliver the highest Republican presidential vote share in the county since 1972. I co-founded the first Moms for Liberty chapter in Wisconsin, founded Wisconsin Patriots, and served as an RNC delegate who voted for President Trump. In my day job, I manage nearly $13 million in public dollars as lead administrator of the largest municipally-owned sports complex in the United States. I've run a small business, worked as a classroom educator at every level, and championed patient visitation rights legislation. District 11 needs someone who has actually done something — not another Madison insider. I'm ready to deliver real results.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordability. District 11 families are crushed by property taxes, rising costs, and state government sitting on a $2.5 billion surplus. Gov. Evers' 400-year veto locked in perpetual increases — that must go. In Madison, I’ll fight to repeal that veto, return the surplus to taxpayers, and eliminate state tax on retirement income, tips and overtime so seniors can stay in the homes they've lived in for decades and workers can keep more of what they earn. I've managed a nearly $13 million public budget. I know how to make every dollar count. Government should work for the people who fund it — not accumulate reserves while working families can't make ends meet. Fiscal responsibility isn't a talking point for me. It's how I operate every day.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government needs to stop operating for the benefit of those who work in it and start operating for the people it serves. That means passing budgets that actually return money to taxpayers when there's a surplus, not sitting on $2.5 billion while families struggle. It means keeping special interests out of decisions that belong to local communities. It means restoring parental rights in education, protecting local control over energy and land use, and treating small business owners and farmers like the backbone of this state, not an afterthought. I've spent my career outside of politics building real things. I'll bring that same accountability to Madison. Transparency, results, and a government that answers the grassroots — not career track politicians.
candidates.leg_q4: The Republican Party was founded in Wisconsin. In 1854, a group of citizens gathered in a small schoolhouse in Ripon to oppose the expansion of slavery into new territories. They believed government should protect individual liberty, opportunity, and the principles on which our nation was founded. That meeting is widely recognized as the birth of the Republican Party. Whether you're Republican, Democrat, or Independent, it's a reminder that some of America's biggest ideas started with ordinary people who cared enough to get involved. Wisconsin has always had a proud tradition of citizen leadership — and that's something worth celebrating.

candidates.name: Adam Duda
candidates.leg_q1: Voters deserve a representative focused on delivering results, not advancing a political career. Coming to America at age nine with few resources, I experienced firsthand the incredible opportunities this country provides. I earned a master's in engineering and a law degree to solve real-world problems.  As an engineer, a law school graduate, and someone for whom English was not a first language, I learned how to listen, advocate, and collaborate across diverse backgrounds.  I am running simply to give back. I offer you a strong work ethic, practical problem-solving, and a deep appreciation for American values to tirelessly serve everyone in Wisconsin's 11th Senate District.
candidates.leg_q2: The 11th District's top issue is the rising cost of living. I will address this through housing, public education, and property tax relief. First, smart development ensures attainable housing and drives "net new construction," expanding our tax base to fund local services without raising rates. Second, Wisconsin's Constitution mandates schools be "as nearly uniform as practicable." When families must flee their home district to find a "sound basic education" because local schools lack resources, the state is failing its duty. We must increase state funding so municipalities stop relying on endless property tax referendums while Madison sits on a multi-billion-dollar surplus. Finally, keeping property taxes low ensures elderly residents on fixed incomes are never priced out of their homes.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government needs to get back to common-sense problem-solving.  Right now, Madison relies on closed-door deals and leaves a multi-billion-dollar surplus sitting idle while our hometowns struggle. This broken system shortchanges our local communities, forcing schools and towns to pass endless property tax referendums just to fund basic needs. State government should be a partner, not a roadblock. As an engineer and law school graduate, I look for permanent fixes instead of temporary solutions that tend to have severe repercussions. We need a fair way to fund public education and actual support for local leaders. Finally, by treating early education as a true opportunity, we can build a secure economic future for every Wisconsin family.
candidates.leg_q4: East Troy Railroad operates the last 7.5 miles of original interurban railroad track in Wisconsin!

candidates.name: Sasha Ripley
candidates.leg_q1: People want elected officials who have their backs and government to make their lives better, not harder. I love rural Wisconsin and care about the people in my district. Wisconsinites deserve a representative who shows up and fights for working and middle-class Wisconsinites instead of bowing down to special interests, millionaires, and big corporations. Small business owners, farmers, and families struggle to make ends meet. These people are the foundation of our rural economy. People can’t afford a place to live and the American dream of owning a home is quickly disappearing. I think we can all agree in the wealthiest nation in the world, someone working full-time should afford a roof over their head, food on the table, and medical care.
candidates.leg_q2: Schools and taxes. We need to restructure the way we fund our public schools so we can have great schools that give our kids the education they deserve and lower property taxes. Public schools are an integral part of our communities and our rural culture. Rural schools are important to kids, families, local businesses, school employees, and local homeowners. There were seven public school referendums in the 13th district and we have schools closing due to the failures of the school funding policies of the current legislature. We should stop using taxpayer money to fund private schools and focus on making our public schools better.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government needs to be more efficient, more frugal, and more focused on the working and middle-class families of Wisconsin. The purpose of government is to make the lives of the voters better, not make the rich richer, the politicians more powerful, or the biggest corporations more wealthy. Government representatives need to start working for the people. To combat the high prices and rigged system we currently find ourselves in, we need to have representatives with bold ideas and big goals. We don't need more of the same old status quo, small ideas, and tired policies of the past. We need new people with new ideas.
candidates.leg_q4: I have loved fishing all of my life. I love being outdoors and enjoying the beautiful natural resources we enjoy in Wisconsin. The Wisconsin muskie record was broken three times in 2025. I have never caught a muskie myself, but I hope to do so someday. My largest catch is a northern pike, just under 38 inches.

candidates.name: Christopher Dean
candidates.leg_q1: In recent years, partisan politics have stalled our system, with too many elected officials prioritizing their party’s interests over the needs of the people they represent. I’m running to serve my community by putting people first. Our neighborhoods are struggling under the economic pressure caused by leaders who’ve lost sight of why they were elected. My goal is to ease the burden of poor decision-making and foster an environment where the people of Wisconsin can truly thrive.
candidates.leg_q2: Over the past few months, I’ve spoken with many residents of District 15, and the concern I hear most often is a lack of representation. I believe that a lack of accountability is at the root of many issues facing Wisconsin today. Too often, elected officials disregard the wishes of the people on matters ranging from data centers to property tax hikes. My goal is to restore an environment where people are respected and truly represented by serving as a bridge between major parties. I’m committed to ending the all-or-nothing approach to politics in Wisconsin by forcing negotiation and bipartisanship.
candidates.leg_q3: Our government is unique compared to most others in the world because it draws its power from the will of the people. Unfortunately, that principle has been largely forgotten in today’s political climate. Wisconsin’s government needs to refocus on serving the best interests of its residents, rather than catering to national political parties. It should concentrate on creating an environment where the people of Wisconsin can thrive and on protecting, rather than restricting, the individual liberties guaranteed to all Americans.
candidates.leg_q4: My favorite Wisconsin history fact is that it was once part of the Virginia Colony.

candidates.name: Mark Spreitzer
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Senate (2023-Present); Wisconsin State Assembly (2015-2023); Beloit City Council (2011-2015)
candidates.leg_q1: I have a proven track record of fighting for the priorities of the 15th District, providing excellent constituent services, and showing up to public events to meet people where they are. I’m running for re-election because there is more work to be done, and I am already a legislative leader on many of the most pressing issues facing our district, including housing, AI and data center regulation, supporting our family farms, and reducing the burden of property taxes. I serve as the Senate Democratic Caucus Chair and am in a position to play a lead role in a Democratic majority. We must tackle the high cost of child care, health care, housing, and everyday necessities while providing targeted tax relief to seniors and working people.
candidates.leg_q2: The cost of everyday goods and services is going up, and too many people feel priced out of child care, health care, housing, and other necessities. At the same time, big tech companies are moving quickly to deploy AI and build data centers across our communities before we have time to put guardrails in place. I would continue to expand access to child care by subsidizing both parents and providers and partnering with businesses. I would expand access to affordable health care by creating a public option for people to buy into insurance through the state and cracking down on prescription price gouging and insurance denials. I would crack down on AI algorithmic price gouging that is raising the price of consumer goods and services.
candidates.leg_q3: We need sustainable long-term solutions to our biggest challenges, especially funding and staffing for critical services. We need to diversify local funding and reduce reliance on property taxes. We need to modernize our school funding formulas and ensure public school funding keeps up with inflation to end the cycle of districts having to go to referendum to raise property taxes for basic needs. We need to address funding gaps for transportation and natural resource management as past revenue streams haven't kept up with modern needs. We need to update state law to recognize the need for shared services and increased collaboration in providing fire and EMS service. We need to adequately staff our state agencies so they can be proactive in responding to emerging needs.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin was the first state in the country to ban discrimination based on sexual orientation, all the way back in 1982, and signed into law by Republican Gov. Lee Sherman Dreyfus. We were also the first state in the country to elect an openly LGBTQ+ person to Congress who was already out when first elected, sending Tammy Baldwin to the U.S. House in 1998. As a gay man, I’m proud to serve in a state that has led on issues of equal rights. However, Wisconsin has since fallen behind, relying on U.S. Supreme Court decisions to allow for same-sex marriage and to bar discrimination against transgender people. I’m proud to have authored bills to update our LGBTQ+ equality laws and lead once again.

candidates.name: Jenna Jacobson
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly, 50th District (2025-present); 43rd District (2023-2025); Oregon Village Board (2017-2022)
candidates.leg_q1: I bring a strong record of public service, practical problem-solving experience, and a commitment to Wisconsin communities. As a state representative, I have worked to strengthen public education, support farmers and rural communities, and advocate for working families, all things of importance for the 17th Senate District. Before serving in the legislature, I was a village trustee who helped oversee local budgets, public safety initiatives, and housing development. Combined with my volunteer work in the community and consistent dedication to improving opportunities and quality of life for people across Wisconsin, I know SD-17 is ready for someone who will actually represent them.
candidates.leg_q2: Everybody is feeling the pinch of rising costs of prescription drug prices, utilities, groceries, food, and gas. The people of the 17th and all across Wisconsin deserve someone who’s making sure that they’re not getting nickeled and dimed to death because the state refuses to look after families and Wisconsin workers. In addition to costs, I hear a lot about public school funding – which is another way we can help alleviate rising costs. Properly funding our schools will lower property taxes. Schools, like the rest of us, are facing budget pressures. Wisconsin must properly fund our schools so every child has access to a high-quality education.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should operate with greater transparency, accountability, and a stronger focus on solving problems that affect everyday families. For too long, partisan gridlock has prevented progress on critical issues such as education, affordable housing, prescription drug prices, and support for local communities. I believe government works best when leaders listen to constituents, collaborate across differences, and make decisions based on the needs of the people they serve. My experience in local government, housing policy, and the State Assembly supports a practical, community-centered approach to governing. I want the state government to invest in public schools, strengthen local economies, support working families, and ensure that every Wisconsinite has a voice in the decisions that shape their future.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin has the world's largest six-pack of beer.

candidates.name: Lisa Rose White
candidates.leg_q1: I am the right choice to serve as state senator for District 17 because I bring a lifetime of real-world experience, deep roots in this region, and a proven record of showing up for people. As a lifelong resident, a mother, and a grandmother, I understand what’s at stake for our families and future generations. For nearly four decades as a businesswoman, I’ve worked across this district — helping people build their homes, improve their communities, and make smart, responsible decisions with their money. I’ve traveled the entire 17th District, listening, learning, and solving problems. I don’t just talk about issues — I take action. I will bring that same work ethic, accountability, and commitment to representing every community in this district.
candidates.leg_q2: We need a serious restructuring of how we fund public education and maintain our infrastructure. Right now, the burden falls far too heavily on local property taxpayers, especially in rural communities. The funding models we’re using are outdated, and they are holding us back — hurting our schools, our communities, and our future. When schools are underfunded, it limits opportunities for our kids and drives up costs elsewhere, from referendums to student debt. At the same time, families are struggling to afford homeownership while carrying more of the load. We need a fair, modern system that invests in education, supports communities, and ensures the next generation can succeed without being buried in debt.
candidates.leg_q3: Local control over land use and zoning has become one of the clearest lessons of this campaign for me. When large corporations move in to use our land, water, and infrastructure without giving back to the people who actually live there, something is deeply broken. Communities must have the power to slow down or stop projects that steamroll their interests. At the same time, the state has a responsibility to modernize our funding formulas so they reflect today’s realities, and ensure every child — no matter their ZIP code — has access to strong public education without families being crushed by taxes or student debt. We also need smart investments in roads, broadband, and housing so staying in our communities feels like an opportunity, not a penalty.
candidates.leg_q4: During World War II, Wisconsin quietly hosted several prisoner-of-war camps, and many residents never learned the full story. One notable site was Camp McCoy (now Fort McCoy), which held German, Italian, Polish, and Japanese prisoners and could house up to 5,000 people at its peak. Another was Camp Beaver Dam, a tent-city camp that held about 300 German POWs in the summer of 1944. Many of these prisoners worked on local farms and in canneries, helping fill labor shortages while getting a close look at everyday American life. After the war, a number of former POWs chose to return to the United States and eventually became American citizens, drawn back by the people and communities they had come to know.

candidates.name: Corrine Hendrickson
candidates.leg_q1: Voters should elect me because I have been working with state and federal elected officials for about a decade to increase funding and services for children with special needs, child care, and small businesses. I have helped to write legislation and was the first child care business owner to testify before the House Small Business Committee in February of 2023 as a business. I co-founded Wisconsin Early Childhood Action Needed in 2020, a grassroots community of 2500 child care professionals, business owners, parents, and community members who learned how to advocate, share their story, testify at state committee hearings, speak to media, and become involved in our democracy to advocate for policies that will benefit their communities. I will use those skills as a senator.
candidates.leg_q2: State level public education funding has reduced to zero increase per pupil for public schools while increasing the amount to private voucher schools. This forces the local property tax base to make up the difference if they can. Children come in with more special needs, complex needs, and the reimbursement from the state is too low so the services provided are inadequate impacting the education of all children. The lack of affordable childcare means that fewer children are being identified and provided services before they enter school, increasing those costs as well. The reimbursement for the technical school courses for apprenticeship and dual credit courses is also about half of what it was promised to be further cutting into school budgets and opportunities for students.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should be responsive to their constituents. Our representatives should be talking to one another on both sides of the aisle to come to a consensus on how best to solve the problems faced by Wisconsinites together. Committees should hold hearings on bills that are overwhelmingly supported by their constituents and passed in an efficient manner. An example of this were the postpartum Medicaid expansion bill and Gail's Law which took almost a decade for them to pass and when they were voted on the floor, they were almost unanimously passed. Another example is the pharmaceutical benefits management bill that has had even more co-sponsors than those two bills, but was never put on the floor for a vote.
candidates.leg_q4: Our state had the very first Kindergarten in Watertown, WI in 1856!

candidates.name: Emily Daniels Tseffos
candidates.leg_q1: Too many working people are doing everything right and still falling behind — and we're being told to fight amongst ourselves as wealth disparity continues to balloon in this country. As a mom, educator, organizer, and lifelong Wisconsinite, I've spent years helping people navigate challenges with schools, healthcare, disability services, and government programs. I've seen firsthand where our systems work and where they fail. I'm running to be a problem-solver, not a politician. I believe that at its best, government should help the most people it can. We can make life more affordable, strengthen public schools, protect healthcare, support farmers and small businesses, and ensure every community has a voice in Madison. I'd like to be that kind of leader for state Senate District 19.
candidates.leg_q2: The top issue around here is affordability. Working people are paying more for groceries, housing, healthcare, childcare, and utility bills while the wealthiest corporations and special interests continue to gain influence over our politics. Too many neighbors are working hard and falling further behind. I'll fight to lower everyday costs by treating problems at the root. I'd work to expand access to affordable healthcare, invest in childcare, fully fund public schools, supporting family farms and small businesses, and reform our tax structure so that it benefits working people instead of just those at the top. Wisconsin's economy should work for the people who do the work and elected officials ought to fight for them in Madison.
candidates.leg_q3: I think more important than anything else, we need to stop being blindly allegiant to a party or politician. I'd like to see our state legislature work together to get something done for the people of Wisconsin through rational, factual dialogue and compromise.  I'd also like to see our legislative leadership refrain from engaging in cultural wars and proliferating misinformation.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin was the first state to ratify the 19th Amendment, giving women the right to vote!

candidates.name: Trevor Jung
candidates.occupation: City of Racine transit and mobility director
candidates.leg_q1: Hardworking people in southeast Wisconsin deserve a fair shot at opportunity and a fair share from Madison. Having served as an alderman and now as Racine’s director of transit and mobility, I have firsthand experience solving issues that affect families every day. My campaign is focused on five pillars for growth: talent, training, transportation, technology, and tourism. My plan is to attract and retain talent by investing in Racine’s assets, strengthen training pathways to in-demand careers, build a reliable transportation system that connects people to opportunity, support innovation and technology for future growth, and invest in tourism that supports small businesses. With strong grassroots support and growing momentum, I am running a campaign centered on listening, accountability, and delivering real results for the 21st District.
candidates.leg_q2: My top priority is making life more affordable for working families through the economic revitalization of District 21. In an era of high inflation and rising costs, Wisconsinites are left stretched too thin by housing, childcare, transportation, and everyday expenses. Using state government as a tool to strengthen economic opportunity, I’ll prioritize policies that make housing more attainable, expand access to affordable childcare, and improve transportation options so people can reliably get to work and school without financial strain. There is significant work ahead to ensure families are not left shackled by the cost of living, but by addressing affordability across these core areas, we can support working families, strengthen our local economy, and ensure southeast Wisconsin is a place where hard work brings prosperity.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should be more focused on responsiveness, accountability, and delivering tangible results for residents. Too often, state policy moves slowly or becomes disconnected from the day-to-day realities facing working families. Going forward, state government should empower locals and prioritize practical solutions that directly improve affordability and opportunity, while making it easier for people to access the services and programs that already exist. That includes reducing unnecessary barriers, improving coordination between state and local partners, and ensuring decisions are guided by clear outcomes. At its core, Wisconsin government should operate with a greater sense of urgency around the challenges people are facing right now, especially rising costs and economic pressure on families across the state.
candidates.leg_q4: One of my favorite fun facts about Wisconsin history is actually about my hometown. Racine was once known as both “Invention City” and “The Machine Shop of the World.” By the early 1900s, Racine had become a global center of innovation and manufacturing, producing products used around the world, producing more patents per capita than anywhere else in the U.S. during that time. Companies like J.I. Case revolutionized agriculture, InSinkErator invented the garbage disposal, Twin Disc became a leader in industrial transmissions, and S.C. Johnson grew into an internationally recognized household brand. This spirit of hard work and invention attracted generations of entrepreneurs and workers from across the globe, helping make Racine and Wisconsin grow.

candidates.name: Jeff Foster
candidates.leg_q1: I am running for increased state funding for our public schools, an end to the voucher system, and lower property taxes. I am running for rural revitalization, including family farms, health care, main street, and housing. I'm running for my fully funded childcare solution which requires only the wealthy to reimburse the state for childcare services provided, without creating a new bureaucracy.
candidates.leg_q2: Property taxes have increased in double digits in each of the last two years largely because of reduced funding from the Republican-led legislature. Property taxes are paid by homeowners and renters. State funding has fallen short for 17 years while Republicans have held the majority and caused many school districts to go to referendum for necessary funding, adding insult to injury. I’d introduce or support a bill that restores the two-thirds state funding requirement passed in 1996. I’d introduce or support a bill ending the voucher system. The state cannot afford to fund two school systems. These actions would significantly reduce property taxes, which are not based on income or ability to pay and can result in people losing their homes and landlords raising rents.
candidates.leg_q3: The greatest change for good would be exclusive public funding for elections. Candidates are lured into supporting causes that they may not entirely believe in due to the possibility of a campaign donation and endorsement. Once elected, large contributors hold considerable sway in influencing how a legislator will vote while dangling the prospect of financial support for the next election. State-only funding would free candidates to appeal only to the voters and to be answerable only to the voters.
candidates.leg_q4: The Super Bowl trophy is called the Lombardi Trophy.
