candidates.name: Keith Mogel
candidates.leg_q1: Why vote for me, I care about the people. As an officer you learn nothing is important if you do not protect the people — their health, safety and welfare, and to me this is the mission of our government. I have 28 years of experience in the U.S. Army serving in various command and staff assignments to include multi-national headquarters in NATO. This required the ability to work in a leadership style that produced cooperation and integration of various national units and non-governmental agencies to support the civilian population — with healthcare and food in a safe environment. It is this leadership style I will bring to the Assembly to push forward the state’s citizens' need for affordable healthcare, education, and environmental stewardship.
candidates.leg_q2: My top issue is the affordability of health care to include health insurance premiums and deductible requirements, which then often leads to independent contractors, farmers, small business owners, and employees of smaller businesses with high-cost plans being offered to either forgo purchasing insurance, not being able to offer it to employees, or employees cancelling their Health Insurance due to cost. I want to expand Badger Care with no income limits and include small businesses with less than 100 employees to opt into a small business cooperative to reduce premium and deductible costs.
candidates.leg_q3: First, I believe both parties have become us vs. them. I am a progressive and at one time both parties had strong progressive wings. Wisconsin needs to return to its progressiveness at a bi-partisan level, which then focuses on what is best for ALL the citizens of the state and not the corporations.  This includes providing and funding health care, appropriate school and rural road funding, and our strong belief in being stewards of the land we want our grandchildren to inherit through our DNR, state park funding, and the Knowles-Nelson stewardship program.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin was the proud leader for many years in progressive leadership at both the state and national levels. It is this leadership in progressive politics, environmental responsibility, and education that was copied to create other states' DNRs. This is why I moved to Wisconsin and want to serve in the state government to bring back the progressivism of Wisconsin.

candidates.name: Duke Tucker
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2025-present); Burnett County Board (2024-present)
candidates.leg_q1: Work ethic and I recognize the need for elected officials to serve everyone they represent. In short, turn the temperature down and work together to provide an effective and efficient government.
candidates.leg_q2: Funding for infrastructure and education. Infrastructure is under-funded, part of the issue is increasing costs another is irresponsible borrowing. Wisconsin currently has $440 million in debt for past road projects. 7.2% of the gas tax collected goes toward debt service rather than maintaining roads. Regarding education, the school funding formula favors schools in more populated areas and leaves our per pupil funding in rural Wisconsin being shorted. Our students are worth exactly the same from a funding standpoint as any other student in the state.
candidates.leg_q3: Within the last year, the state government agencies have the ability to create laws/regulations without legislative oversight. This is a problem. When laws/regulations are put into place, Wisconsin residents should have the ability to support or reject those who enacted the regulations. Bureaucrats at state agencies can't be held accountable by voters due to this recent ruling, this needs to change.
candidates.leg_q4: Not sure about it being a fun fact, but Wisconsin was the first state to enact an income tax...ugh.

candidates.name: Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford
candidates.occupation: Food service worker; small business owner; Madison alder
candidates.leg_q1: District 76 deserves a legislator who will fight like hell for working people and our democracy. I don’t have the typical background of someone who runs for the Assembly. I’ve worked for $2.33 an hour plus tips in the food service industry. I’ve experienced homelessness and gone without healthcare for most of my life. I don’t just see the struggles our neighbors face — I live them. Our perspective is missing in government, and that’s exactly what I will bring. As an alder, I’ve secured over $60 million for affordable housing, expanded mental health services, and passed a moratorium on data centers. I’m ready to take that fight to the state so we can lower costs and protect our rights from this authoritarian federal government.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordability. The cost of everything keeps going up and people are being priced out of the communities they love. As someone who works multiple jobs and can barely afford rent, I know what that feels like. Our state government can be doing so much more to lower costs and make life affordable. We need to raise the minimum wage and tie it to inflation, cap healthcare and utility costs, build truly affordable housing, and fully fund our public schools so we can end this referendum madness and finally lower property taxes. And we need to stop giving tax breaks to billionaires. I believe in Wisconsin where we take care of each other and we can all get ahead. That’s what I am fighting for.
candidates.leg_q3: We deserve a government that works for working people, not billionaires and big corporations. Republicans have controlled the legislature for the past 15 years and look where it’s gotten us. The cost of everything is out of control and our democracy is under attack like never before. But we have a real opportunity this year to elect a new legislature. Instead of just being a barrier, our state government can focus on making our lives better. In the Assembly, I’ll fight for a living wage, real property tax relief, universal healthcare and childcare, fully funded public schools, and housing we can afford. We can deliver bold, progressive change in Wisconsin, but we need to elect leaders with a backbone and the will to do it.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin was the very first state in the country to pass a law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation. As Wisconsin's first transgender state legislator, I will work to build on that legacy. In this climate of attacks against transgender people, representation has never been more important. I won’t just be representing the people of District 76, but also every queer and trans kid across Wisconsin who doesn’t see themselves in government. I will fight to expand our 1982 non-discrimination law to include gender identity and expression and advance a positive, proactive agenda for full LGBTQ+ equality in our state. Wisconsin should be a progressive beacon for our democracy and civil rights. We have led before, and we can lead again.

candidates.name: Isaia Ben-Ami
candidates.leg_q1: Experience. I have worked in the Legislature for the last six years, most recently as a policy director for the assistant minority leader. I have the most state-level legislative experience of anyone in this race. For the first time in a long time, Wisconsin has a chance at a Democratic trifecta. That means we have an opportunity to invest in a Green New Deal, fix our school funding formula, and restore workers' rights. We need someone committed to building coalitions and power so that we can make progressive policy a reality. I have worked in Democratic leadership, and worked to elect Democratic lawmakers around the state. I know what it takes to be effective, and efficacy is what we need in this moment.
candidates.leg_q2: Housing costs. Rents are skyrocketing, and property taxes are pushing many residents out of their homes. We need to fix our school funding formula so that we rely less on property taxes and more on high-income earners and rolling back corporate tax breaks. We also need to protect our tenants from onerous rent increases and build more housing that is actually affordable for the workers within a community. This can be done through a tenant bill of rights that protects tenants and allows consideration of affordability in our building approvals. Lastly, we need to build more housing. Not just high-rise, high-price apartments, but condos, duplexes, and cooperatives. We need to grow our housing stock so that more people can own a home in the community.
candidates.leg_q3: We must be dedicated to ensuring the freedom of working people. Everyone deserves the freedom to access healthcare, housing, and education. Everyone must have the freedom to breathe clean air and drink clean water. Freedom takes positive policy change to ensure. Freedom is not guaranteed by shrinking government; it is created when we generate the conditions for everyone to live a dignified life. That means instead of cutting government as we have, we need to grow it. Grow our government into an entity that represents the interests of people, not profits. One that will stand against corporations seeking to exploit our people and our planet. One that fights to make life better for our neighbors. One that provides a better future for our kids.
candidates.leg_q4: Because of the Toledo War, the Upper Peninsula (UP) became part of Michigan instead of becoming a part of the Wisconsin Territory. Ohio is the reason the UP is not a part of Wisconsin.

candidates.name: Juliana Bennett
candidates.leg_q1: I’m running for the state Assembly to build an affordable Wisconsin where working people can thrive. There are three things I bring to this race that no one else does: (1) I am the only one in this race that has drafted and passed original legislation; (2) I am the only one in this race that has worked on a bipartisan basis on the local, state, and federal level; (3) I am the only one in this race with a clear anti-establishment stand and commitment to not taking corporate PAC’s money. I will be the person that rallies our Wisconsin state legislators around a clear vision that reflects the needs of the working class, not big money lobbyists.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordable housing is my top priority. Everything is a housing issue: Healthcare, worker’s rights, education, climate change — all of the above stem from housing issues, which is why “Housing First” initiatives are so vital. My plan starts with passing a tenant bill of rights and making strategic investments in deep and permanent affordable housing. Next, we need to remove the handcuffs from municipalities on addressing their local housing crises by legalizing rent control, inclusionary zoning, and a vacancy tax. At the same time, I will prioritize making sure the state pays its fair share in supporting local efforts to shelter people. Finally, I will advance a statewide Department of Housing and Homeless to fill the absence of a dedicated team working to house Wisconsinites.
candidates.leg_q3: I understand through personal and professional experience the impact of legislators who do nothing, versus those who stand up and fight. The central mission of this campaign is to go beyond the outer limits of what others believe is possible and push the Democratic party and our state to do better. I’m stepping up because I’ve been in the rooms of power as a former alder and as the chief of staff to a state representative, and I have seen how our leaders are not stepping up to meet the moment. I will be the person that rallies our Wisconsin state legislators around a clear vision that reflects the needs of the working class, not big money lobbyists.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin has a claim to fame for a wide range of inventions: from the ice cream sundae, to the first electric guitar, to the QWERTY Keyboard. But did you know that Wisconsin, specifically Milwaukee, has been a major part of American Socialist history? Milwaukee was the center of the “sewer socialism” movement and was the first major city to elect a socialist mayor in 1910. The term sewer socialism was the idea that we should prioritize funding social initiatives to improve public health and wellbeing — which is an issue still highly relevant today. Democratic Socialist New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani even referenced Milwaukee’s history of work under socialist mayors as an inspiration for his own priorities in 2026.

candidates.name: Zoe Sullivan
candidates.leg_q1: I bring more than 30 years of practice listening to people as both an organizer and a journalist, and I use a systems lens to reflect on issues. I was one of the first people in the state to raise the alarm about data centers’ potential environmental impact, and in my work on immigrants’ rights, I forged coalitions with financial institutions, a law school, and nonprofit organizations. Additionally, thanks to my reporting experience and my work expanding access to solar power across the state, I have connections to and insights into communities from Wausau to Westby.
candidates.leg_q2: Education funding is the top issue in the district, both for the K-12 system and the university system. One of the first things I would do in office would be to draft legislation to roll back the voucher program. That program is siphoning money out of the public school system and forcing communities across the state to hold referenda on raising property taxes to make up the gap. We could also pass a bill to tax the wealthiest Wisconsinites at a higher rate and direct those funds to K-12 schools. I would also work to close prisons and reduce the incarcerated population. The state currently spends nearly 15% of its budget on corrections, while the university system receives roughly one third of that amount.
candidates.leg_q3: Since 2011, the Republican-controlled state Legislature has epitomized partisan power politics by stymying Democratic administrations and legislative efforts to the detriment of all Wisconsinites. I would like to see an end to the partisan infighting that frustrates so many in the state.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin was the first state to ratify the 19th Amendment.

candidates.name: Tony Castañeda
candidates.leg_q1: I've lived in the 76th for over 50 years where I have raised my family and worked. I've been politically active in Madison since I arrived here in 1974. I am a radio host for the Thursday Buzz on WORT for 33 years where we address local, state, national and international issues. I feel I have a good understanding of the issues affecting this district and the State overall. I am here to fight back against the 15 year Republican agenda of attacking our public commons.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordable housing is a big concern for renters and homeowners alike. The state needs to adequately fund our public schools so that Madisonian homeowners are not covering 75% of school district costs. We need to provide and develop more affordable rental housing so that people like me who work as cooks, artists, musicians, bartenders are able to stay in our neighborhoods. I like the idea of charging developers "linkage fees" to add to our city and school budgets or to fund more affordable housing.
candidates.leg_q3: We should have the good of the public commons in mind when making policy which I don't feel the Republican majority has in the past. Along those lines it is imperative that Democrats win the Assembly or for that matter, all three branches of state government.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin is first in many areas of progressive policies but the fact that the first Kindergartens in the country were started in Wisconsin is one I like.

candidates.name: Renuka Mayadev
candidates.leg_q1: Throughout my career, I have advocated for the urgent needs of women, children, and working families. Now, as a legislator, during a time when our long-standing public programs and benefits are vanishing, I am standing up to protect Wisconsinites and sustain our state's democratic institutions. I have authored bills to strengthen our public schools, prevent gun violence, prioritize our environment, increase access to childcare, and reduce healthcare costs. After years of stalling in the Assembly, I delivered on my campaign promise that Wisconsin must provide vulnerable mothers with a year of postpartum healthcare coverage after delivering a baby. As your State representative, I deliver results.
candidates.leg_q2: Fully funding our public schools. Currently, school districts across the state have to rely on local referenda to make their district budgets work. This places a heavy tax burden on Wisconsinites. We must once and for all fix our school funding and provide districts with predictable long term support. Recently, given the state surplus, I, along with my Democratic Assembly Caucus, authored AB 1176, which increased general school aid and raised the state’s reimbursement rate for special education costs to ease the burden on local property taxpayers and provide greater financial stability for school districts. We must act. Strong public schools are essential to a thriving democracy and future economic growth.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government is not protecting the state's beautiful lands. The long-standing Knowles-Nelson Stewardship Program was not reauthorized this past legislative session, leaving it to end in June 2026. The Knowles-Nelson Stewardship Program has a long tradition of protecting land, water, natural spaces for wildlife habitat, and outdoor recreation. The state  must return to our deep roots of conservation and environmental protection.
candidates.leg_q4: It is a great honor to work in the Wisconsin State Capitol. The building's grand architecture and large scale art are breathtaking. For a fun fact: The Capitol's construction took over 10 years, commencing on Oct. 12, 1906 and ending sometime in 1917, making the Capitol building 109 years old.

candidates.name: Jane McCormick
candidates.occupation: Professional interior designer; real estate broker
candidates.leg_q1: I am running for the Wisconsin Assembly because I believe government works best when elected officials listen first, treat people with respect, and focus on practical solutions. Drawing on decades of business leadership, entrepreneurship, and experience across multiple industries, I bring a real-world perspective to solving problems and making sound decisions. I will work tirelessly in a moderate, nonpartisan manner to represent the needs and priorities of residents of the 77th District. Guided by common sense, thoughtful persuasion, and a balanced mindset, I will work with anyone, regardless of party, to address the most pressing issues facing our district and state. Voters deserve a representative who puts people ahead of politics.
candidates.leg_q2: One of the top issues facing the 77th District is Wisconsin's outdated public education funding model. From our K-12 schools to the University of Wisconsin-Madison, public education is essential to our state's future workforce, economic growth, and quality of life. Yet schools are being asked to meet increasingly complex needs — including special education, mental health support, truancy intervention, and assistance for students facing poverty — while local property taxpayers shoulder much of the burden. I have already begun meeting with education leaders and researching potential solutions. Wisconsin needs a more equitable, sustainable funding approach that reflects the real needs of students and communities, supports educational excellence, and reduces excessive reliance on local property taxes.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should operate with greater honesty, transparency, and respect for the people it serves. Too often, political divisions and partisan battles take priority over solving real problems. Elected officials should communicate candidly about challenges, be accountable for results, and focus on representing their constituents rather than political interests. We also need a more balanced approach that recognizes the unique needs of every district—from urban centers to rural communities and everything in between. No region should be overlooked, and no district can expect to get everything it wants. Progress requires listening, compromise, and a commitment to the greater good. Our leaders should model the civility, responsibility, and collaboration we hope to see now and in future generations.
candidates.leg_q4: My favorite Wisconsin fun fact is that while Wisconsin was not the first state to grant women the right to vote, it was the first state to ratify the 19th Amendment, helping secure women's suffrage nationwide. As a woman running for elective office for the first time, I find that especially meaningful. Wisconsin's role in that history reminds us that ordinary citizens can help shape extraordinary change. It inspires me to step forward in public service and encourages future generations to believe they can make a difference as well.

candidates.name: Shelia Stubbs
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2019-present); Dane County Board (2006-2022)
candidates.leg_q1: My extensive career in public service over the past 24 years, specializing in a wide variety of issue areas, including public safety, finance, and health and human needs, has demonstrated both my ability to enact sound policy and my dedication to representing the voices and needs of my constituents. As one of the only Democratic lead authors on a bill to pass this legislative session in a divided government, I understand what it takes to work effectively across the aisle while remaining true to my Democratic values. Voters should elect me because I work diligently to introduce and pass quality legislation and continuously advocate for the state of Wisconsin to invest in initiatives, development, and programming that benefit the residents of the 78th Assembly District.
candidates.leg_q2: The top issue in my district is affordability. My constituents are increasingly facing a shortage of affordable housing and rising costs for childcare, groceries, and virtually every other necessity. Our broken school funding formula is forcing my constituents to choose between properly funding their public schools and keeping their property taxes stable. Many residents of the 78th Assembly District, from working families to seniors on fixed incomes, are finding it difficult to make ends meet. Both as a Dane County Board supervisor and a state representative, I have worked hard to make public investments in programs that promote financial stability for my constituents and connect them with resources. I will continue to champion initiatives that combat poverty, lower costs, and promote economic opportunity for all.
candidates.leg_q3: The decisions we make in our state Capitol are supposed to be made in the best interest of all Wisconsinites, but for far too long, the most vulnerable members of our communities have been overlooked or haven’t been given a seat at the table at all. Our Wisconsin government must do a better job of representing and prioritizing those who have been left behind. We must do a better job of making our state a place where everyone, regardless of background, can live safely and comfortably and reach their full potential. I have always stood by my values of equity, inclusion, and civil rights, and I will continue giving a voice to those who have historically gone unheard.
candidates.leg_q4: My favorite fun Wisconsin history fact is that Beloit, my hometown, has an Underground Railroad site! Growing up in South Central Wisconsin, I had the privilege of being surrounded by history. From the Underground Railroad site that paved the way to freedom for enslaved people, to the Native American mounds on the Beloit College campus, I was immersed and instructed from a young age in the stories of the many diverse peoples who call Wisconsin home. I believe that honoring and acknowledging that history is an integral part of who we are as Wisconsinites. Whether our ancestors are indigenous to this land, immigrated here, or came here from enslavement, we all have a role to play in shaping and stewarding the future of our state.

candidates.name: Henry Johnson
candidates.leg_q1: No response
candidates.leg_q2: No response
candidates.leg_q3: No response
candidates.leg_q4: No response

candidates.name: Lisa Subeck
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2015-present); Assembly Democratic Caucus Chair (2023-present); Madison City Council (2011-2015)
candidates.leg_q1: It is an honor to serve as your state representative. I strive every day to provide progressive and effective representation as I bring your voice to the state Capitol. As your representative in the legislature, I have been a leader on access to health care, reproductive rights, support for children and working families, strengthening our public schools and University of Wisconsin system, protecting our natural resources, fairness and equity, supporting our workforce, and protecting our democracy. I am committed to providing accessible, responsive, and accountable representation as I work to ensure Wisconsin's future as a great place to live, work, and raise a family. It is a privilege to represent you, and I hope to earn your vote.
candidates.leg_q2: The issue I hear about most is affordability. Families are struggling with the rising cost of healthcare, prescription drugs, housing, groceries, child care, and other everyday necessities. Those challenges have only been made worse by economic uncertainty, including the impact of Donald Trump's tariffs and instability in the Middle East. I believe government should help make life more affordable, not harder. That is why I have worked to expand access to affordable healthcare through a BadgerCare public option, lower prescription drug costs through our "Less for Rx" plan, invest in affordable housing and public education, support affordable child care, and provide healthy school meals for all. These are practical solutions that help Wisconsin families succeed.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should be more transparent, collaborative, and focused on solving problems than scoring political points. For too long, legislative leaders have decided behind closed doors which ideas deserve consideration, leaving many thoughtful proposals without a hearing or vote simply because of who introduced them. Every proposal should be judged on its merits. If an idea will make healthcare more affordable, strengthen our public schools, support working families, or improve public safety, it deserves a fair hearing and honest debate. My own experience passing bipartisan legislation has shown that when lawmakers work together in good faith, we can achieve meaningful results. Wisconsin works best when government is responsive, accountable, and willing to listen. Our constituents expect us to do the work, not play politics.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin was the first state to ratify the 19th Amendment, allowing women the right to vote, in a dramatic race to the finish with Illinois (Perhaps this was the impetus for our Packers/Bears rivalry).

candidates.name: John Fons
candidates.leg_q1: I'm a "New Old" candidate. My occupations have taken me from the board rooms of billionaires in Canada to the streets of Dallas where I worked among the homeless. I've contributed to the science of energy exploration and attained a master's degree in theology. I am older in years than my political opponent and many others in the Wisconsin Assembly, but I'm new among them all. Therefore I owe no favors and I have the experience that allows me to go carefully and responsibly through the complex issues facing our state. The agenda I bring is to learn and with that knowledge serve the people of Assembly District 79 and every other citizen of Wisconsin.
candidates.leg_q2: Property taxes are the single greatest expense of my household and therefore a personal issue which I presume also affects every other taxpayer in District 79 within the City of Madison. There are other issues which go beyond city limits. Penalties for driving while intoxicated should be made more severe. Crimes involving firearms likewise severely answered. We tend to separate environmental concerns from public safety, but we are all subject to the environment we create and if that environment is not safe, however it may be defined, we are all at risk. I would add that health care is also crucial to the well being of our citizens and should be made as accessible as possible in terms of both location and cost.
candidates.leg_q3: "We stand on the shoulders of giants." That is a time-honored expression which simply means we receive what previous generations have given, what they have contributed to our society. Add to this the inevitability of change and you have both a tension and an opportunity going Forward. Rely on the institutions that have proven themselves and use them as a firm foundation to examine each and every demand brought forward upon which the future depends. Examine and investigate, study and demand accountability, use the tools provided to build and not demolish the essential functions for which Wisconsin government has been created.
candidates.leg_q4: In 1880 my great grandfather John Fons built a log cabin which still stands in Door County. In 1909 my grandfather, also named John Fons, carved his name in a rock that to this day remains on the ground outside the door of that cabin. My grandfather left home at 15 to work in the lumber camps saying, "It was just as easy to starve somewhere else." My heritage demands my personal commitment to this place, this Wisconsin where I now live and where I seek to serve to the best of my ability. It may not always be fun, but the people here and elsewhere I admire most are the ones who get the job done first and then go out and have fun.

candidates.name: Simran Arora
candidates.occupation: Program director, Outpatient Mental Health Services
candidates.leg_q1: If you want a leader who truly understands your struggles, I’ve lived it. As a parent who raised a child, felt the daily pressure of inflation, and paid rising property taxes that burden families, I know what you’re going through. As a legal immigrant, I understand the hope and hardship of chasing the American dream while waiting for my own father’s visa to reunite with me. With deep knowledge of mental health and substance use disorders, along with proven experience managing budgets, contracts, and expanding vital services, I’m prepared to deliver results. After 15 years in counseling, I’ve listened to thousands and supported people through life’s toughest moments. Vote for me, together, we can bring real change.
candidates.leg_q2: The top issue I will stand up for is what matters most: educating our children. I will prioritize student’s needs while also protecting parental rights. If you're frustrated with rising property taxes, I will fight for relief. The surplus belongs to the people of Wisconsin, and it’s time to return those dollars to families. As a mental health counselor, I understand the importance of psychoeducation on mental health, addiction, and recovery programs. I will advocate for these programs before crises occur. Additionally, I support apprenticeships and evidence-based models like Individual Placement and Support to help individuals find meaningful work. By strengthening our economy and giving everyone purpose, we invest in lasting success. I’m ready to do the work and hope you’ll stand with me.
candidates.leg_q3: The Wisconsin government should operate with greater caution and prioritize community needs through transparent, deliberate decisions. First, focus on real needs by investing in essential services backed by clear data and measurable results, and avoid wasteful projects like replacing functional shelters with smaller ones. Second, eliminate duplication by stopping redundant funding across multiple organizations and overlapping programs, ensuring taxpayer dollars are used efficiently. Third, plan collaboratively by carefully weighing the pros and cons, engaging local residents early, and sharing major plans in advance to rebuild trust. By respecting taxpayers and working hand-in-hand with communities, we can create a smaller, smarter government that truly serves the people of Wisconsin.
candidates.leg_q4: The Lake Mendota Ancient Canoes. Archaeologists and divers recovered multiple hand-carved wooden canoes from the bottom of Madison’s Lake Mendota. The oldest dates back approximately 3,000 years, to around 1000 BCE. These remarkable artifacts provide a tangible connection to the ancestral Ho-Chunk Nation and other early Indigenous peoples who navigated these waters long before European settlement. It is a powerful reminder of the deep history beneath our feet right here in Dane County.

candidates.name: Mike Bare
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2023-present); Dane County Board (2020-2023); Verona City Council (2013-2014)
candidates.leg_q1: I work hard for the 80th District. I'm a member of Assembly leadership and several committees, and I'm committed to making progress on giving Wisconsinites a raise, fixing our democracy, restoring our rights, and making investments in our schools and communities.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordability is the top issue. We must give Wisconsinites a raise. We could raise the state earned income tax credit, raise the homestead credit, pay for healthy school meals for every student, and relieve the property tax burden that's been created by Republicans defunding our public schools.
candidates.leg_q3: I'm hopeful that Democrats will have the majority in the Legislature. That would allow us, with a Democratic governor, to take on the big money spent on campaigns and lobbying to rig the economy and outcomes against the people. We could make our democracy work for us, not them.
candidates.leg_q4: The Green Bay Packers should be credited with 14 world championships, not 13.

candidates.name: Mark S. Maier
candidates.leg_q1: I would like to see accountability on how we are spending our tax dollars. The literacy rate in our schools is not acceptable. We as taxpayers pay more per student than all but one country in the world, yet our literacy rate is far below other countries that pay  thousands less per student than us. Property taxes continue to rise to pay for our schools but we are not seeing the results of the spending. The rising property taxes are making home ownership unaffordable for many people. Funding our schools is important, but we cannot spend our way to better test scores. I would like to work at changing how we fund our schools so that our children have the education they need.
candidates.leg_q2: Rising property taxes is the number one complaint that I hear from property owners.
candidates.leg_q3: Less new programs. Our government should work on making the existing programs affordable and workable.
candidates.leg_q4: The Green Bay Packers are the only franchise that is publicly owned and the third oldest franchise in the NFL.

candidates.name: Alex Joers
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2023-present); Dane County Board (2020-2023)
candidates.leg_q1: The challenges facing Wisconsin families are real, and they deserve more than talking points. I am focused on lowering everyday costs, protecting fundamental rights, strengthening our public schools, supporting small businesses and farmers, and defending our democracy. These priorities are about making sure working families can build stable, secure futures right here in our community. I will continue to fight for practical, common-sense solutions that improve people’s lives and move Wisconsin forward.
candidates.leg_q2: Wisconsin’s Constitution guarantees every child the right to a public education. When we invest in our schools, we are building a better future. Property taxes continue to rise because of 15 years of a Republican-led legislature not meeting the state’s obligation to education. School districts are continually forced to go to referendums to make ends meet. The state's share to fund public schools has not increased with inflation, voucher schools continue to siphon off public dollars while avoiding transparency, and teachers are leaving the profession because of burnout and low wages. This is all while our students take the biggest hit in educational outcomes. We need to commit to fully funding public schools and reimburse special education costs at a higher rate.
candidates.leg_q3: Even during 15 years of one-party rule in the Legislature, I proved that progress is still possible. I worked across the aisle when it meant delivering real results, and I have stood firm when our rights were on the line. Whether it is protecting our freedoms, investing in our kids, supporting small businesses and farmers, strengthening our democracy, or tackling the climate crisis, my focus is always the same: what actually improves people’s lives.I believe our government should work for the people, not special interests. We should work to lower people’s everyday bills, respect our rights, protect our environment, and create opportunities in every corner of our community. That is the standard I hold myself to in the State Assembly.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin has a lot of "firsts" to be proud of. This state was the first to ratify the 19th Amendment which recognized women's right to vote. We were also the first state to pass anti-discrimination laws based on sexual orientation. Our state was where Earth Day was founded, highlighting sustainability and conservation. We were also the first to begin the kindergarten system in education. These examples of history-making successes along with many others are my favorite parts of Wisconsin's legacy.

candidates.name: Bryson Reyes
candidates.occupation: Supply chain analyst in the manufacturing industry
candidates.leg_q1: Voters should elect me for the state Assembly because I can bring an outside perspective to Madison. I proudly served this country as an infantry officer in the United States Army and have spent the last several years working in the manufacturing industry. I have seen firsthand what businesses and residents are facing in the current economic environment. That experience has shaped my belief that government should work with businesses and workers, not against them. I want to change that by bringing a practical, common-sense voice to the state Assembly that focuses on solving problems, cutting through bureaucracy, and strengthening Wisconsin’s economy for the long term. I will support policies that make Wisconsin more competitive, support job growth, and increase public safety.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordability and the cost of living are the top issues not only in Waukesha, but across Wisconsin. I hear it constantly when I am out knocking on doors and talking with residents. Families are working hard, but too much of their paycheck is being taken by rising costs and taxes. To address this, we need to lower taxes and allow Wisconsinites to keep more of their hard-earned income. Wisconsin currently has a budget surplus in Madison, and we should use that as an opportunity to provide meaningful tax relief. That means reducing property taxes, personal income taxes, and corporate income taxes to make our state more competitive and affordable for working families.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin is the 13th most regulated state in the country with 165,000 regulations on the books. That, combined with the fact that we have the 12th highest corporate tax rate, 9th highest personal income tax rate, and 8th highest property taxes in the country is not enabling Wisconsinites to thrive. The primary way we need to operate differently than in the past is to reshape our regulatory environment and reduce the tax burden. We can be a state where entrepreneurs want to start businesses and companies want to invest, produce, and hire here. By creating a more competitive economic environment, we can ensure the current and next generation of Wisconsinites have the opportunity to prosper.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin has more dairy cows than the entire human population of about eight U.S. states!

candidates.name: Rico Camacho
candidates.leg_q1: I’m running because Wisconsin deserves a leader who shows up with steadiness, clarity, and lived experience. As a teacher, father, and alderman, I’ve spent my life protecting families, guiding young people, and helping our community stay grounded through difficult moments. My leadership arc has always been about service. Creating safety, stability, and opportunity for the people around me. In the state Assembly, I’ll fight for strong public schools, mental‑health support, public safety partnerships, and a workforce pipeline that prepares our kids for real careers. My commitment is simple: to listen, to lead with integrity, and to make decisions rooted in the everyday realities of Wisconsin families.
candidates.leg_q2: The top issue for the 82nd district can be seen all over the country. We are facing an affordability crisis. I plan to go to Madison to help create new economic formulas to ensure that, through ACT 10 and ACT 12, we can lower property taxes and still ensure city services are being met. I plan to suspend the gas tax until we can move forward with lower property taxes, and most importantly, I will look to cut taxes for the middle class and ensure families are able to live in a way that follows the patriotic belief system of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.
candidates.leg_q3: The Wisconsin government needs to come together and begin actually functioning as a coherent entity that focuses on the people of Wisconsin and not the politics that are played. There have been budget proposals to increase special education spending that have failed. There has been proposed legislation for farmers, working-class families, and seniors that has not been fully adopted. We need to put people first and truly look at what is in the best interest of all Wisconsinites.
candidates.leg_q4: The Springs in Waukesha were believed to have healing powers and therapeutic properties that people would travel from all over the world to be healed. That is why it has the nickname Spring City, which — on a personal note — my first soccer club was called Spring City Soccer.

candidates.name: Dave Maxey
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2023-present); New Berlin City Council, president (2019-present); New Berlin School Board (2008-2017), president (2011-2017)
candidates.leg_q1: As the fiscal and family values conservative running for the State Assembly, I want to bring our shared family values and the expertise I have gained through my business career and public service to Madison. I am committed to advocating for our community and ensuring our voices remain heard at the state level.
candidates.leg_q2: The top issue facing families in our district is affordability. Rising property taxes, inflation, and the increasing cost of everyday necessities are putting pressure on household budgets. Throughout my service in the state Assembly, on the New Berlin Board of Education, and on the City Council, I have worked to keep property taxes as low as possible while maintaining quality services. To address this challenge, I will continue fighting for lower taxes, responsible government spending, and a simpler tax code that allows families and small businesses to keep more of what they earn. Wisconsin taxpayers deserve a government that lives within its means and focuses on providing value, not growing bureaucracy.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should focus on doing the basics well while respecting taxpayers. For too long, government has continued to grow, adding programs and spending without always evaluating whether they are effective or necessary. We should lower taxes for working families, retirees, and small businesses by trimming waste, eliminating unnecessary spending, and making government more efficient. Just like families and businesses must live within their means, state government should do the same. By prioritizing core services, reducing bureaucracy, and demanding accountability for every tax dollar spent, Wisconsin can remain financially strong while allowing citizens to keep more of their hard-earned money. Responsible budgeting — not bigger government — is the path to long-term prosperity.
candidates.leg_q4: My favorite Wisconsin history fact is how our state's lakes and rivers have long been a gathering place for families and communities. That resonates with me because some of my favorite Wisconsin memories are spending summer days out on the water boating with my family. Whether it's enjoying the sunshine, exploring new spots, or simply spending time together, Wisconsin's waterways have helped create countless family traditions for generations, including my own.

candidates.name: Chuck Wichgers
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2017-present); Muskego City Council (1999-2002); Waukesha County Board (1999-2002)
candidates.leg_q1: A true citizen legislator.
candidates.leg_q2: Levy limits, we must work for reforms that are sensible for the tax payers and fund necessary services.
candidates.leg_q3: Less giveaways to big lobby groups and look to support local government and reduce property taxes.
candidates.leg_q4: We ended slavery and abortion in the same year, declaring all people have liberty, dignity and rights. Whether in the womb or from another country, people are not property and no one can take that away from them, it is God given.

candidates.name: John Kroll
candidates.leg_q1: I’m a husband, working father — and former county board supervisor. Even with two working parents in our household, we’re feeling the same issues that residents in Marathon County are experiencing as my wife and I try to raise our family — skyrocketing housing and property taxes, increasing health care premiums, and rising energy costs. In my professional career, I’ve worked to reduce energy and housing costs for thousands of homeowners. My career shows I know how to get things done for working Wisconsinites while offering a new generational perspective from the status quo in Madison.
candidates.leg_q2: Rising costs. Families are being hammered by increased prices in gas, groceries, housing, health care, and energy. We need to fix the property tax issue first by getting off the referendum roller coaster by addressing public school funding so municipalities are not asking voters to keep raising their property taxes to account for school funding gaps. We can also reduce health care costs through lower prescription prices and holding insurance companies accountable. Finally, we can lower energy costs by increasing energy production in Wisconsin with a goal toward energy independence, cap energy rate increases, and good old fashioned energy efficiency — work I’m very experienced in professionally.
candidates.leg_q3: One thing is clear from knocking doors in our district — people want structural changes that deliver concrete results for their families, regardless of what party proposes the bill. This starts by making sure party leaders cannot unilaterally control which bills are allowed to be voted on, votes for bills are taken at reasonable times of the day so the public is aware, and working across the aisle to make life better for working families across Wisconsin. These steps will allow common sense bills that most Wisconsinites agree on to have their public hearing and votes instead of being blocked by party leaders.
candidates.leg_q4: My family and I love the outdoors and care deeply about being good stewards of our environment in Wisconsin. I appreciate that Earth Day is a Wisconsin idea first developed by former governor and Sen. Gaylord Nelson and is now celebrated every year on April 22 around the world, with the original Earth Day in 1970 remaining one of the biggest single day protests in history.

candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2017-present); Schofield City Council

candidates.name: Andy Wuethrich
candidates.leg_q1: I hope to represent the people of my district, not corporate interests. I also hope to bring honesty and integrity back to government and begin to restore faith in our institutions.
candidates.leg_q2: The top issue the people I've talked to is funding our public schools fully. The voucher program has stripped away necessary funding for our public schools, and schools need to keep using referendums to make up the difference.
candidates.leg_q3: We need to begin to tax the top 1% of earners appropriately. They profit off the public services this state provides, and they don't pay their fair share to cover those services.
candidates.leg_q4: I've always been proud of the fact that Wisconsin has historically been the place that people travel to to relax and enjoy nature.

I feel that my experience to find solutions and cooperation is essential for the state of Wisconsin.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordability! Too many citizens are trapped by unfair access to justice and opportunities. In this state, "Act 10" has created restraints for economic growth for valuable employees like government workers, teachers and union workers. This is causing a "brain drain" of talented individuals choosing to go elsewhere in search of a better opportunity.
candidates.leg_q3: It's looking to the past to remind us how Wisconsin was considered a progressive state. Strong unions representing the working class for fair wages and benefits. Support for public schools and not a handout for private schools. For providing quality and affordable medical care throughout the state. Plus, the wealthy paying their fair share for the overall betterment of this state.
candidates.leg_q4: The Wisconsin Badgers football playing and winning the Rose Bowl in 1994 after a long absence.

candidates.name: Brandy Tollefson
candidates.leg_q1: I’m a working mom of three kids, treasurer of the De Pere School Board, and have seen first hand how Madison is failing our families. Rising costs are hurting working families. As a school board member, I have worked to protect our schools, listen to families, and stand up for students, teachers, and taxpayers. I know what it is like to navigate a healthcare system that is too expensive and too complicated. I am running to bring hard work and practical leadership to Madison. This district deserves a representative who listens, shows up, and fights for the people who live here.
candidates.leg_q2: The cost of living is squeezing families across AD 88. Rising costs, including housing, groceries, healthcare, and gas prices are out of control. I'd fight to make healthcare more affordable and accessible, make sure kids have access to healthy school meals in order to lower grocery costs for families, and make sure that we’re building affordable housing.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should be more transparent, more responsive, and more focused on solving problems. For too long, too many decisions in Madison have been driven by partisan fights instead of the needs of local communities. I believe legislators should listen first, work across the aisle when possible, and be honest with voters about what they are doing and why. Most importantly, elected officials should remember that they work for the people, not special interests or political insiders. It’s time to put working families and local communities first.
candidates.leg_q4: As we celebrate 250 years of American democracy, I keep coming back to the fact that Wisconsin was the very first state to ratify the 19th Amendment in 1919, helping fulfill the founding promise that all people are created equal. It took 131 years to get there but Wisconsin led the way. Wisconsin has always been at the forefront of progress and I promise to continue that tradition when I get to Madison.

candidates.name: Ben Franklin
candidates.occupation: Director of operations, Papa Johns Pizza; Air Force Reserve

candidates.name: Bobby R. Lindsey
candidates.leg_q1: I've spent my adult life serving others, first as a United States Marine, and later as a law enforcement professional. Wisconsin needs leaders who understand public safety, fiscal responsibility, and the values that make our communities strong. I believe government should live within its means, support law enforcement, protect taxpayers, defend parental rights, and ensure that opportunities to attain a prosperous life are available to future generations. I will work to provide relief from rising costs for families, empowering parents and putting kids first when it comes to meeting needs for a quality education, and I'll advocate for keeping our communities safe by supporting measures and policies that provide public safety professionals the resources they need to protect our communities.
candidates.leg_q2: Addressing rising costs. I see the impact rising costs have on family budgets. Groceries, energy prices, housing, childcare, and property taxes are stretching families thin. The middle-class is the backbone of Wisconsin's economy and I will work to provide relief for families, retirees, and those with kids in childcare to ensure families and individuals keep more of their hard-earned money and stop efforts to raise taxes.
candidates.leg_q3: Ongoing political gridlock contributes to bureaucratic stagnation, less government efficiency and accountability, and budget-crippling rising costs and taxation on Wisconsin's middle-class. Wisconsin citizens can be served best by elected representatives who understand and prioritize the critical need to exercise fiscal responsibility to curb rising costs and the increasing tax burden on middle-class families and retirees. Government operating differently begins with electing representatives who are committed to collaboratively identifying and taking action on common ground issues from across the political landscape within Wisconsin government; issues that impact all Wisconsin residents.
candidates.leg_q4: It is a legendary Wisconsin tradition for parents to add their children to the Green Bay Packers season ticket waiting list immediately at birth. As a result, there are more people on the waiting list for Green Bay Packers season tickets (approximately 155,000) than there are residents of the City of Green Bay (approximately 107,000)!

candidates.name: Ryan Spaude
candidates.leg_q1: As a prosecutor, I fought to keep our streets safe. As your state representative, I'm fighting to keep more money in your pocket. Over the past two years, I've introduced legislation to lower the cost of groceries, housing, and prescription drugs. I authored bills to curb reckless driving and close loopholes in our drunk driving laws.  In addition, I opposed the most recent state budget, which underfunded our public schools and caused property taxes to skyrocket. In these challenging times, we need to keep a steady hand at the wheel. It's been an honor to serve you, and I hope to earn your vote again in November.
candidates.leg_q2: The cost of living remains the top issue in Green Bay and Ashwaubenon. In my first answer, I described the legislation that I've introduced to ease the pain that working families are facing. A few months ago, I also voted to return a significant portion of the state surplus to the taxpayers. I was one of only 10 Democrats who crossed the aisle to do that. I'm an independent leader who's focused on your bottom line.
candidates.leg_q3: Most people believe that when a legislator introduces a bill, it's automatically given a public hearing and voted on. Unfortunately that's not the case in Madison, where Republicans have been running the show for 16 years. Democrats introduced exactly 500 bills this past legislative session. Guess how many were given a hearing? Only 19. That's less than 4%. Meanwhile, Republicans gave 76% of their own bills a hearing. If this sounds like a healthy system of government, you can vote for my opponent. If you believe the Republicans have lost their way, I'd appreciate your support.
candidates.leg_q4: In 1994, Gov. Tommy Thompson signed a bill to make polka the official state dance of Wisconsin. He inked the document at a special ceremony in Pulaski, instead of Madison!

candidates.name: Amaad Rivera-Wagner
candidates.leg_q1: Voters should re-elect me because I believe in showing up, listening, and turning community priorities into real results. In my first term, I helped pass bipartisan legislation expanding housing opportunities and to help DACA recipients (Dreamers) get access to local jobs, fought for veterans shelters, safer neighborhoods, stronger schools, consumer protections, and local control. I have held dozens of community conversations and attended hundreds of meetings and events because leadership should be rooted in the people we serve, not politics as usual. My story is Green Bay’s story: working hard, overcoming challenges, and believing government can be a force for good. I will keep choosing progress over politics, community over chaos, and results people can feel in their everyday lives. Green Bay deserves nothing less.
candidates.leg_q2: My top priority is making government work for the people it serves. Across Green Bay, we see the problem is not that people are not working hard enough. The problem is that the system is not working for them. Homeownership, the cornerstone of the American Dream, feels more out of reach than ever. Health care decisions are being made by unaccountable companies instead of patients and their doctors. Property taxes keep rising while the state legislature refuses to act. I am running to change that. I will keep fighting to expand housing access, raise the minimum wage, hold health insurance companies accountable, fully fund our schools and regulate AI and data centers so our communities, workers, and families are protected. Government should make life better.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should look more like our communities and less like the chaos and cruelty of Washington, D.C. I was elected after the most gerrymandered maps in the country were overturned, and we have already seen what becomes possible: new coalitions, new policies, and bipartisan progress on housing and immigration. But to truly change the system, we need leaders who center our communities, not petty politics, extremism and conspiracy theories. I am proud that I am not just talking about that, I am doing it: holding more than 30 town halls and roundtables, attending over 500 community meetings, and passing bipartisan legislation that improves people’s lives.
candidates.leg_q4: My favorite Wisconsin history fact is that our state has so often been first in the nation at showing how government can be a force for good. Wisconsin helped lead the way on unemployment insurance, workers’ compensation, public sector unions, women’s voting rights, Earth Day, and the first statewide protections for LGBTQ people. That is what our state motto, “Forward,” really means to me. It is not just a slogan. It is a responsibility. I am proud to fight for a future rooted in that legacy: one where government protects people, expands opportunity, and helps communities thrive. With your support for re-election, we will continue to move Wisconsin forward, together.

candidates.name: Jessica Henderson
candidates.leg_q1: I believe my years of experience as a case manager, and my education are exactly what Green Bay needs to discover solutions to the complex issues and concerns we are currently experiencing.
candidates.leg_q2: To me, and many others in this district, the top issue is property taxes and cost of living. I would vote to end the 400 year planned property implemented in recent years and to refund some of the budget surplus back to taxpayers.
candidates.leg_q3: To be more effective our Wisconsin government should work to reduce the hyper-partisan politics we see coming from both sides of the aisle, and to increase transparency to gain more trust and accountability.
candidates.leg_q4: The Republican Party was formed right here in Wisconsin!

candidates.name: Jodi Emerson
candidates.leg_q1: I am proud to be born and raised in the Chippewa Valley. My husband and I were proud to raise our children here. I understand the challenges we face as a community and I go to work everyday trying to make life better for those in the Chippewa Valley.  In the Assembly, I am fighting to make housing and child care more affordable, getting tax relief to small businesses, and taking on health care companies to cover important medical care and protecting families’ ability to access IVF treatment. I am working to make Wisconsin a state where everyone can live, work, and raise a family.
candidates.leg_q2: One thing I consistently hear about in my district is the rising cost of living across. Whether it is the cost of groceries, healthcare, gas, housing, or utilities, folks are struggling to make ends meet. One way to address these challenges would be to pass our lowering costs, improving lives bill package — aimed at lowering the cost of groceries for families through providing free healthy school meals, lower prescription drug costs, and lower housing costs through expanding the homestead tax credit to help seniors and renters.
candidates.leg_q3: For many years, the legislature has operated under a gerrymandered majority. This really impacted what bills were heard in committee and brought to the floor. Regardless of what party had the idea, the legislature should work more collaboratively to pass bills that will move Wisconsin forward.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin has been the No. 1 cranberry-producing state for over two decades, yielding millions of barrels annually and producing over 60% of the nation's crop and over 50% of the global supply. More than 250 family farms and growers manage roughly 21,000 acres of cranberry marshes across 20 counties in central and northern Wisconsin.

If we take that issue away from the GOP, there will be no reason to vote for the GOP and lose Social Security in the process. candidates.leg_q2: The fear of parents having their children ripped from them by secret genderizing and secret court trials to emancipate children for sex change operations and hiding. candidates.leg_q3: I propose to cut the salaries of all legislators in half and eliminate 40 Assembly seats (I would be affected too). That forces redistricting to combine districts, because our legislators do not earn their pay.  Republicans just follow the commands of the majority leader after their caucus votes for a law. The savings can pay for school tutors and apprentices paid union wages to chaperone kids in grade schools to protect them from racial gangs and same sex indoctrination. Gangs threaten to kill children  who do not join. We can solve both problems at once.
candidates.leg_q4: My idea of fun is not the circus and not drugs. It is learning. My favorite fun thing was discovering the greatest chess players in America are from Wisconsin. And a close second  was in my research of history discovering before Wisconsin was even a state, the framers and representatives of the first constitutional convention in 1846 wanted to make education of every child a constitutional right so no state has better educated kids. candidates.name: Clint Moses
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2021-present); Menomonie Area School Board (2013-2020)
candidates.leg_q1: Over my time in public office, I have proven that I can listen to varying perspectives, work hard and get the job done. This past legislative session I introduced 26 pieces of legislation and had 16 bills passed, 13 of which were passed with bipartisan support and over half of them were signed into law by our governor. I was proud to introduce legislation that will lower the cost of healthcare, improve access to healthcare, clean-up our environment and lower the tax burden to Wisconsinites to name a few of the vary diverse topics that I worked on.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordability! From going to the doctor, putting groceries on the table, filling up the car with gas or buying a home we all know that it's gotten more expensive to live. I know because I see it every day in my business and household. Raising four daughters isn't cheap!
candidates.leg_q3: At the state level we need to rebalance the powers of the three branches of government by restoring the legislative oversight powers to the state legislature. We also need to restore local control to provide local municipalities with flexibility to handle local issues specific to them. I also think that it would help to decentralize our state agencies and modernize our services into a single digital platform instead of the current system where users have to try and navigate between all the different agency websites.
candidates.leg_q4: All four of the Green Bay Packers Super Bowl victories have been when our state had a Republican governor.

candidates.name: Jeremiah Fredrickson
candidates.occupation: Owner/operator of Jeremiah's Bullfrog Fish Farm
candidates.leg_q1: I am running for the Assembly because the 92nd deserves a representative who truly listens to them. I am not a career politician — I am a fish farmer, teacher, coach, and working dad who knows what working families are going through. Having been an agricultural science teacher, I taught numerous subjects that has helped make me a well rounded candidate and a life long learner. As a teacher and farmer I understand the value of hard work and dedication. I will bring these values with me to represent the 92nd Assembly District.
candidates.leg_q2: As I’ve knocked doors and talked to people in my district, Data centers continue to be the top issue. My goals when elected would be to create safe guards in their construction to protect communities from the negatives they could bring. This would include protecting our natural resources: water, air, and land, but also safeguarding electrical rates for communities surrounding the centers and making tech companies pay their fair share. Finally, when all of those safe guards are in place, making sure that they are built by Union Wisconsin Construction workers.
candidates.leg_q3: I believe that government officials need to get back to representing the people that elected them and not the special interests that line their pockets. Too often people get elected and they seem to forget about the areas and people they represent. In addition we need to get back to working with each other and not being divided left and right. Compromise and finding a common good should be our goal; not “winning” for a party or group, but making the best decisions for our respective areas and Wisconsin as a whole.
candidates.leg_q4: My favorite bit of Wisconsin history was taught to me while listening to Brewers baseball on the radio by the late great Bob Uecker. He told stories of making oleo runs with his family. This was in reference to the margarine bans from 1895 to 1967. This makes sense as we are the “Dairy State” and this helped the dairy industry. Even today restaurants in Wisconsin can not serve margarine as a butter substitute unless the customer requests it.

candidates.name: Christian Phelps
candidates.leg_q1: I represent a change in leadership after 15 years of a Walker-Trump status quo that has damaged the Chippewa Valley's economic well-being. In my first term, I've brought my years of experience as a nonprofit organizer, journalist, and public school employee to the capitol. I've leaned on my existing relationships to drive a pro-public narrative that Wisconsin should guarantee healthcare, housing, food, and education as rights, instead of passing the bill to my neighbors through high property taxes and skyrocketing costs. With the real possibility of flipping the Legislature this year, young, bold leadership will be more important than ever to govern bravely and reshape Wisconsin's economy.
candidates.leg_q2: Public education and high housing costs through property taxes. School districts throughout the 93rd have had to close public schools, propose school consolidations, go to repeated referendums, and cut staff, all because the state doesn't hold up its end of the agreement. The cost of living and the quality of education for Chippewa Valley kids are related. I have a plan (AB 1176 and more) to to "pick up the tab" for our public schools (through fair, sustainable taxes on the very wealthy), keep property taxes down, stop relying on referendums, and invest in what kids need: fantastic teachers and specific supports for students with disabilities, students learning English, and students in poverty.
candidates.leg_q3: I've seen how little transparency exists in our state government. That is intentional. I will continue leaning on my background as a journalist and communications professional to show all of my constituents what's going on in Madison: the pace of work, how and when bills move through the legislative process, exactly who you should contact to advocate on an issue, how procedural moves can change the culture of Wisconsin politics, etc. I do not believe in back-room dealmaking without input from the public, and I do not believe in rushing bills through the process to limit public awareness. We should be open, transparent, and flexible in the capitol so all of our constituents can provide feedback.
candidates.leg_q4: I wish more people knew that Wisconsin was home to the first kindergarten in the United States! All the way back in 1856. I think this fact matches so well with our long history of leading on public sector services and labor issues: farmer-labor movements here in western Wisconsin, labor union movements in the early 20th century, and more. Okay, maybe this is more of a nerdy fact than a fun one, but it's a great example of the positive parts of Wisconsin's education and economic legacies, and what I hope to play a small part in carrying forward.

candidates.name: Steve Doyle
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2011-present); La Crosse County Board (1986-present), chair (2002-2011).
candidates.leg_q1: I’m proud of my record of bipartisan successes in the state Legislature, but there is still so much more I would like to accomplish. I want to revisit the recent property tax cut/education funding deal and get it right. We have a surplus and that should be put to work making life more affordable for everyone, and ensuring our schools have the resources they need to be successful.
candidates.leg_q2: Affordability is the top issue in the district. Everything is more expensive these days: gas, groceries, healthcare, childcare, the list goes on. We need to lower taxes for the middle class, cut property taxes, rein in the cost of healthcare, and work with our farmers and grocers to make food more affordable. We have a 2.5 billion dollar surplus that could be put to work right away, but that’s just the start.
candidates.leg_q3: As a mediator by trade I know first hand that the quickest way to success is bringing everyone to the table to work together. We saw a glimpse of this with the passage of the state budget this session when both parties in both legislative houses all got together with the Governor to craft the final budget. At the same time, the recent property tax cut deal fell apart because several parties were not at the table for the negotiation. I believe for any major policy we should bring everyone to the table to negotiate. That’s the only way things get done.
candidates.leg_q4: The Wisconsin Capitol building has 40,000 light bulbs. When the classes of fourth graders visit the Capitol for a tour I like to tell them that fact, then, later I will visit the classroom to talk about my role in government. I ask them how many light bulbs are in the Capitol and all their hands shoot in the air. Talking about State Government with those classes is one of the best parts of being a state legislator.

candidates.leg_q1: Over my 15 years of service I have proven to be a very hard worker for the people I represent and while in the minority I have still been able to get things done in a bi-partisan manner. I have passed bills concerning human trafficking, clean water, substance abuse, hunting and fishing, stopping on-line predators and scenic byways. I have always carried a heavy load of commissions and committees because I enjoy the work and feel it's important to have the ears and eyes of Western Wisconsin at the table in the legislature. My staff and I understand the importance of listening to constituents and addressing their needs in a timely manner.
candidates.leg_q2: In the past, I would have said either education, healthcare or taxes are the top issues. Currently, affordability has risen to be an extremely important issue to voters in my district. Current practices on the federal level have left people feeling uncertain of the future and concerned about the price of fuel, groceries, taxes, healthcare and insurance. I still believe we should use some of the surplus for tax relief. Although it is difficult for states to alleviate all problems of affordability resulting from federal level policies, we can use some surplus dollars for help for first time home buyers, relief from state fuel taxes and helping with healthcare costs.
candidates.leg_q3: Wisconsin government should operate in a more bi-partisan manner, while listening to the needs and concerns of all Wisconsinites. In my years serving in the state Assembly minority party I was able to get some bills signed into law, although it is extremely rare for that to happen. Under Republican control, only 2-4% of Democratic sponsored bills even received a public hearing. I believe we can work better for the people of Wisconsin when both parties have a seat at the table.
candidates.leg_q4: Since we are celebrating the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, my fun fact is that our very own Wisconsin State Historical Society houses many important national historical documents. Our collection includes significant early drafts and historical prints of the U.S. Constitution and papers from the Lewis and Clark Expedition. As a member of the Board of Curators and the State Building Commission, I am proud that we will soon have a new Wisconsin History Center to display more of our 290 million items of historical significance. I am also grateful to the early collectors who brought these incredible artifacts to our Historical Society in Wisconsin for preservation.

candidates.name: Cedric Schnitzler
candidates.elected_experience: Monroe County Board (1996-present), chair (10 years); Town of Sparta Board, chair (1992-1996)
candidates.leg_q1: Since the age of 26 when I was first elected to county board, serving the people is an honor as well as a responsibility not to be taken lightly. It means listening to the people you represent, never taking any one's opinion lightly but weighing everyone's input. Serving western Wisconsin would be a great honor — putting people first, looking for solutions that empower hardworking families and residents that call western Wisconsin home.
candidates.leg_q2: Unfunded mandates on county government, public schools and all forms of local government, result in uncontrolled property tax increases, if Madison is going to pass mandated services it needs to fund it this would result in local levy relief for county and schools, and local units of government. In short, it would be real property tax relief, for seniors, working class, and new homeowners.
candidates.leg_q3: Start working for the people, not the next election cycle. When they start on bills ask the question: how's this going to affect the working people — the retirees in Wisconsin, not just for today but long-term.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin had the first rails to trails or bike trails are awesome. I remember walking the tunnels of the Sparta Elroy bike trail as a kid before it was a bike trail. Great memories.

candidates.name: Tara Johnson
candidates.elected_experience: Wisconsin State Assembly (2025-present); La Crosse County Board (2000-2020), chair (2011-2020)
candidates.leg_q1: In local government, there are no D’s or R’s, just problems that need to be solved. I spent two decades fighting for my constituents and problem-solving on the county board without a letter after my name. This is the attitude I take to Madison. The people of the 96th deserve an experienced representative with the know-how to deliver on critical issues like healthcare and transmission lines. This term didn’t go exactly how I imagined. Despite Republican leadership’s roadblocks, we managed to get some huge wins: Gail's Law and postpartum Medicaid expansion. These laws will deliver healthcare coverage for tens of thousands of Wisconsin women. This is just the start of me getting work done for the 96th.
candidates.leg_q2: From the gas pump to the grocery store, people are struggling to afford their lives. In my first term, I co-authored countless bills to make life more affordable by reducing childcare and healthcare costs, lowering property taxes, and protecting workers and their wages. As the Assembly lead author of BadgerCare public option, I am fighting to expand coverage and create a state marketplace for individuals and small businesses. Not only will this bill make healthcare more affordable, it is a critical step towards ensuring every Wisconsinite has access to quality healthcare which is a deeply personal issue for me and one of my top priorities.
candidates.leg_q3: It begins with setting aside partisan gamesmanship. The state Legislature is becoming famous for what they don’t get done. Common sense bills designed to address challenges such as data centers, education funding, and affordability are ignored, so the GOP majority can focus on political fights and culture wars. Democrats introduced 500 pieces of legislation this session. Of those 500, only 19 were given a committee public hearing and zero had a floor vote. We should be working for the people of Wisconsin passing good bills no matter whose idea it is.
candidates.leg_q4: Wisconsin has long valued education for young people. In 1856, German immigrants in Watertown, Wisconsin, offered the first kindergarten classes in the United States. MS taught those students in keeping with German culture. I learned about the importance of early childhood education to Germans in my undergraduate studies as a German language major at Carroll University in the early 1980s. I continue to honor this legacy by fighting for comprehensive K-12 public education funding in Wisconsin.

candidates.leg_q1: The working class needs and deserves help. We need affordable housing, groceries, and healthcare. Universal childcare is a must so we can help parents get back to work. Wisconsin belongs to the people, not billionaire tech companies and their data centers. Corporate greed and short-sighted policies threaten to permanently damage our state's fragile ecosystems. I will propose policies that keep our state beautiful and our summers magical. Public School teachers work way too hard for how little they are compensated. I want to push for mandatory state minimum salary for public school teachers as well as a supply stipend so they don't need to depend on parents to donate or for teachers to pay out of their own pocket for school room necessities.
candidates.leg_q2: We are in an affordability crisis. After gas, groceries, housing, and insurance, families have little left. An affordable economic environment can be done through a dozen small steps that each do a little to ease the pressure. The apartment my wife and I rented in 2019 was $900/month. Today, that same apartment is $1,500/month. Rent increased $75 a year for that apartment. Wisconsin minimum wage has remained the same since 2008. We need to raise the minimum wage to $15. Childcare costs are keeping parents out of the workplace. Parents like me literally cannot afford to go back to work because they would need to make $30 an hour just to break even. Universal childcare will help parents get back into the workplace.
candidates.leg_q3: I want to return the governorship and state attorney general to their original legal powers so we can have proper checks and balances in the state. Republicans held all 3 branches of Wisconsin government from 2011 to 2018, and in the waning days of Scott Walker's term, he and the Republican-led Assembly colluded to consolidate much of the power of the governorship and state attorney general into the Assembly instead — where the Republicans would maintain control after the election. "We have allowed far too much authority to flow to the executive," Assembly Speaker Vos (R) said. This "authority" imbalance only seemed to be an issue after seven years, when they no longer had control of the office.
